source: Virtual Moon Atlas database, C. Legrand. Copyrighted, dev only

8 homeward.general_1: Crater visible on the iconic color picture taken by W. A. Anders onboard Apollo 8 mission on the December 24th 1968. Symbolise Apollo 8 return to Earth. Previously named Ganskiy or Hansky M.

abbe.facts: Director of Iena observatory. Author of a classical theory of microscopes in 1877 and of sinuses relations. Associated with Carl Zeiss. Conceiver of a refractometer and of the first apochromatic objectives and of orthoscopic eyepieces.

abbot.general_1: Circular formation isolated with bowl shape.
abbot.facts: Director of the observatory of the Smithsonian Institution. Determination of the value of the solar constant and the distribution of energy in the solar spectrum.

abel.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
abel.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Abel L to the West Barnard and Abel A to the North.
abel.walls: Slightly high walls almost gobbled to the East in the Mare Australe lava.
abel.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting a ghost crater to the North-east.
abel.facts: Specialist of the theory of elliptic integrals and works on the so called abelian integrals.

abenezra.general_1: Circular formation with hexagon shape composing a remarkable gathering with Azophi and Abenezra C
abenezra.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushing Abenezra C to the West and bearing Azophi to the South-West.
abenezra.floor: Tormented floor.  Circular crest lines. Hills.

abetti.floor: Flat floor filled with the lava of Mare Serenitatis.

abul wafa.facts: Author of an arithmetrical treaty and of a precise method for sinuses calculations.

abulfeda.general_2: Partly covered by imbrian ejecta. Typical
abulfeda.slopes: Steep slopes bearing many craterlets whose Abulfeda R to the North-West and Abulfeda S and W to the North.
abulfeda.walls: Very high walls in terraces overlapped by Catena Abulfeda to the South and by Abulfeda U & Y to the North.
abulfeda.floor: Extensive flat floor filled with lava.  White stpot off center and hills.  Craterlets to the North-East and to the South-West.
abulfeda.facts: Prince of the dynasty of Ayyubides. Author of  the "History" that follows Ibn al-Athir work

acosta.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated on the North slope of Langrenus

adams.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Adams B to the West and Adams D to the East.
adams.walls: Fairly high walls in terraces overlapped by two craterlets to the North and a crater to the South.
adams.floor: Flat floor with craterlets whose a central.
adams.facts: Has demonstrated the existence and indicated the position of Neptune independently of Le Verrier but his works have not been published by the Royal Observatory.

aepinus.floor: Flat floor riddled with craterlets and one big crater in the South-West.

agatharchides.general_1: Damaged formation partly submerged by the lava of Oceanus Procellarum.
agatharchides.walls: Slightly high walls partially destroyed to the North and ridden by Agatharchides F to the South-West.
agatharchides.floor: Extensive flat floor filled with dark lava.  Ruins of central mountain.

agrippa.general_1: Circular  Formation with destructed shape to the South-West.
agrippa.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Agrippa F and Tempel to the East.
agrippa.walls: Walls in terraces supporting Agrippa H to the North.
agrippa.floor: Fairly flat floor.  Central mountain.  Hills and debris to the West.  Rille and craterlets.
agrippa.facts: Observer in 92 of an eclipse of Pleiads by the Moon.

airy.general_1: Wrecked formation forming an aligned trio North - South with Argelander and Vogel.
airy.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Argelander to the North Airy D to the North-West and Airy G to the South-East.
airy.walls: Tormented and high walls ridden to the South by Airy H.
airy.floor: Irregular Slightly widened floor.  Double central mountain.
airy.facts: Director of the Observatory of Greenwich in 1835. Works on the celestial mechanics. Author of a theory on the diffraction of the light.

aitken.facts: Author of New General Catalogue of Double Stars in 1932.

al-bakri.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing 2 lines of North South oriented crests to the South.
al-bakri.floor: Extensive flat floor filled with lava.
al-bakri.facts: Specialist of the North Africa and Arabia.  Author of a 'Dictionary of Geography' and a 'Geographical description of the known world'

al-biruni.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
al-biruni.facts: Great traveller. Astrologist of Rhazni Sultan in 1017. Civilizations historian. Author of Kitah al Qanun al Mas'udi general astronomy treaty inpired from Ptolemeaus.

al-marrakushi.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a double craterlet to the West and a triple craterlet to the North.

alan.general_1: Squared formation included in Catena Davy.
alan.slopes: Two sides shared with adjacent craterlets.

albategnius.walls: High walls ridden by many craters whose Klein to the West and Albategius B to the North.
albategnius.floor: Large flat floor.  White spot to the West.  Central mountain.   Depressions and craterlets.
albategnius.facts: Author of the 'Zidj' improving considerably astronomical knowledge of his period. Measure of the obliquity of the Ecliptique.

albert.general_1: Circular formation not very visible near Luna 17 landing site.

alder.facts: Professor in Koln University in 1940. Nobel prize in 1950 with Otto Diels.

aldrin.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
aldrin.facts: Pilot of the LEM of the mission Apollo 11.  Second man to have walked on the Moon on 21 July 1969.

alexander.slopes: Very damaged slopes bearing Calippus to the South-West.
alexander.walls: Slightly high walls collapsed to the East.
alexander.floor: Flat floor filled with dark lava.  Hills rilles and craterlets.  Two white spots.
alexander.facts: King of Macedoine from 336 to 323 BC. Worked for the expansion of his kingdom to India. Seized Babylone and burnt Persepolis.

alfraganus.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Alfraganus E and H to the North and Alfraganus K and M to the East.
alfraganus.facts: Author of a 'Book of the science of stars and celestial movements '.

alhazen.general_1: Circular formation located on the East slope of Mare Crisium.
alhazen.general_2: Possibly Nectarian but younger than Crisium Basin
alhazen.facts: Discoverer of laws of reflection refraction and propagation of the light.  Author of 92 known works with many about astronomy.

aliacensis.general_1: Circular formation forming a remarkable couple with Werner.
aliacensis.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta. typical
aliacensis.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Werner to the North-West a couple of craters to the South-East and Aliacensis B to the West.
aliacensis.walls: Very high walls supporting an anonymous crater to the South.
aliacensis.floor: Flat floor.  Small mountain off-center.  Wrinkle ridges and craterlets.
aliacensis.facts: Author of a work on the reform of the Church in 1416 and of 'Imago Mundi' work evoking the sphericity of the Earth.

almanon.slopes: Fairly steep slopes overlapped to the North-East by Almanon C to the South by Almanon A and B and bearing Catena Abulfeda to the North.
almanon.walls: Walls highetr to the East than to the West.
almanon.floor: Fairly flat floor.  Hills and line of crests. Craterlets.
almanon.facts: Son of Harun Al Raschid. Organizer of the translation in Arabic of scientific and philosophical works of old Greek authors.

aloha.general_1: Few deep circular formation on the North slope of Montes Agricola.
aloha.walls: Steep walls collapsed in the West and bearing two craterlets.

alpetragius.general_1: Circular formation situated between Alphonsus and Arzachel.
alpetragius.slopes: Steep slopes bearing the ghost crater Alpetragius X to the North-West and Alpetragius M and N to the South-East.
alpetragius.floor: Tormented floor little widened.  Important central mountain.
alpetragius.facts: Tried to improve the system of Ptolemee.

alphonsus.general_1: Circular formation composing a remarkable trio with Ptolemaeus and Arzachel.  Several observed transcient phenomena whose a gaseous emission spectra obtained by Kozyrev in November 1958.
alphonsus.slopes: rugged steep slopes riddled with craterlets.
alphonsus.floor: Flat floor to the North tormented to the South with black spots.  Central mountain.  Craterlets and hills.  Contains Rimae Alphonsus.
alphonsus.facts: Initiator of the Greek and Arabic works translation. Coordinator of the calculation of 'Table Alphonsines' replacing astronomical tables of Ptolemee in 1256.

ameghino.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
ameghino.general_2: Formerly Apollonius C. 15 km SW from Luna 20 sample return site.

amici.facts: Director of Florence observatory. Inventor of a specteoscope with prism. Survey on cristals orientation in minerals.

ammonius.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated in the arena of Ptolemaeus.
ammonius.facts: Founder of a new Plato school also called School of Alexandrie.

amontons.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
amontons.slopes: Slightly steep slopes with bright spot to the East
amontons.facts: Inventor of many devices as several thermometers a pyrometer a rotary pump and a telegraph with luminous signals. Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1699.

amundsen.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
amundsen.slopes: Steep slopes bearing an anonymous crater to the East and another one to the South.
amundsen.facts: Specialist of the Antarctic. With the 'Fram' first to have reached the terrestrial South pole on December 14th 1911 and to have overflown the North pole in 1926 in dirigible.  Disapeared in researching the expedition of Nobile.

anaxagoras.general_1: Overlaps the West wall of Goldschmidt.  Circular formation.  Rays.
anaxagoras.facts: Creator of the first school of philosophy in Athens. Tutor of Pericles Euripide and Socrate.  Explanation of eclipses.  Works in anatomy.

anaximander.slopes: Slightly steep slopes crushed by Carpenter to the North and by Anaximander D to the South.
anaximander.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by a craterlet to the North and gobbled to the South.
anaximander.floor: Flat floor in communication with Anaximander D to the South. Craterlets and line of crest.
anaximander.facts: Inventor of the gnomon.  Recommended a flat circular Earth.  Map of the world known.  Discovery of the Polar Star and of the obliquity of the Ecliptique.

anaximenes.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Anaximenes G to the North-East and Philolaus to the East.
anaximenes.floor: Flat floor filled with lava.  Craterlets.

andel.slopes: Steep slopes rugged to the South and to the South-West and bearing Andel M and N to the North-West Andel A and D to the South-West and Andel S P and E to the South.
andel.walls: Walls more high to the East than to the West collapsed to the South and ridden by Andel G to the South.
andel.floor: Tormented floor with hills.  Craterlets whose an important near the center.
andel.facts: Selenographer.  Author of a map of the Moon in 1926.

anders.facts: Apollo 8 mission astronaut in december 1968 with Frank Borman and Jim Lovell.

anders' earthrise.general_1: Formation without a definite shape composed with hills and a small central valley.
anders' earthrise.facts: Crater visible on the iconic color picture taken on board of Apollo 8 by W. A. Anders on December  24th 1968. Symbolize the return on Earth of Apollo 8. Previously named Ganskiy (Hansky) M.

andersson.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

ango.general_1: Elongated formation few deep and oriented North - South.

angstrom.general_1: Bright circular formation with bowl shape.
angstrom.facts: First measure of wavelength.  Specialist of the spectral analysis.

ann.general_1: Elongated formation parallel to Rima Vladimir.

ansgarius.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

antoniadi.facts: Survey of planetary surfaces (Mars and Mercury principally) with 82 cm Meudon refractor. Opponant to Lowell theory of Mars channels.

anuchin.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

anville.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on Dorsum Cushman.
anville.facts: Author of a map of Africa in 1727 an atlas of China and an ancient 'Geography' .  Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1773.

apennine front.general_1: North slope of Mons Hadley Delta supporting the Saint George crater.

apianus.slopes: rugged slopes bearing many small craters whose double crater Apianus A to the North-West and Apianus B to the South-East.
apianus.floor: Flat floor filled with lava.  Craterlets
apianus.facts: Calculation of the longitude from movements of the Moon.  Author of 'the Astronomicum Caesareum'.

apollo.facts: Dedicated to Apollo american human missions that brought 12 astrnauts on the Moon surface.

apollonius.general_1: Circular formation situated in a mountainous region.
apollonius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Daly and Apollonius F to the North-West and Cartan and Apollonius H to the South-West.
apollonius.walls: Fairly high walls in light terraces supporting Apollonius M and E
apollonius.facts: Author of an important work of synthesis on the conical.

appleton.facts: Assistant de Rutherford. Ministre de la recherche en 1939. Etude sur l'ionosphŠre. Auteur du premier‚cho radar sur la Lune en 1946.Prix Nobel en 1947. Rutherford assistant. Research Ministry in 1939. Surveys on atmosphere. Author of firdt radar echo on the Moon in 1946. Nobel laureate in 1947.

arago.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing the ghost crater Lamont to the South-East and domes Arago Beta to the West and Arago Alpha to the North.

aratus.general_1: Bright circular formation with bowl shape situated in Montes Apenninus.
aratus.facts: Author of a poem on the astronomy and on the meteorological phenomena. Author of the name of 48 constellations known in Antiquity.

archimedes.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Mount Archimedes to the South and Bancroft to the South-West.
archimedes.floor: Very flat floor and widened filled with lava. Craterlets.
archimedes.facts: Pupil of Euclide.  Calculation of Pi.  Works in geometry. Inventor of the pulley and the lever.  Founder of the static and the hydrostatic.

archytas.facts: Pythagorician friend of Platon.  Inventor of the kite and flying machines.

argelander.general_1: Circular formation forming a North - South aligned remarkable trio with Airy and Vogel.
argelander.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Argelander A to the East Airy to the South and Vogel to the North.
argelander.floor: Slightly and extensive flat floor.  Small central mountain. Craterlets whose a double to the North.

ariadaeus.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape. Point of arrival of Rima Ariadaeus.
ariadaeus.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Ariadaeus A to the North-East.
ariadaeus.facts: Son of Philippe II. Author of a work on eclipses. Murdered on Olympias order.

aristarchus.general_1: Circular formation visible during the Earthshine. Important rays. Transcient phenomena. Forms an interesting couple with Herodotus. Young formation (450 millions of years).
aristarchus.slopes: Steep slopes especially to the North.
aristarchus.floor: Slightly and extensive flat floor. Small central mountain.
aristarchus.facts: Inventor of the heliocentric theory and a method of distance calculation of the Sun and the Moon.

aristillus.general_1: Forms a remarkable couple with Autolycus. Circular formation. Rays.
aristillus.floor: Flat floor.  Three central mountains of 900 m high.

aristoteles.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a remarkable couple with Eudoxus.
aristoteles.slopes: Very steep and rugged slopes bearing Mitchell to the East.
aristoteles.floor: Flat floor extensive. Two small mountains off-center. Hill rilles and craterlets.
aristoteles.facts: Universal scientist. Creator of the Logic.  Tutor of Alexander the Great.  Works on animals and rocks.

armstrong.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
armstrong.facts: Test pilot.  Commander of the mission Apollo 11.  First man to have walked on the Moon on July 21th 1969.

arnold.slopes: Slightly steep slopes overlapped to the North by Arnold A and a craterlet to the West and to the South.
arnold.walls: Slightly high walls crumbled to the South.
arnold.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Depression rille and crater.

arrhenius.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
arrhenius.facts: Director of Stockholm university in 1897. Director of Nobel institute in 1905. Author of a theory of electrolytes ionization in 1887. Author of panspermia hypothesis in 1900 and of a cosmogonic theory. Chemistry Nobel laureate in 1903.

artamonov.facts: Scientist involved in the soviet space program.

artem'ev.facts: Scientist involved in the soviet space program.

artemis.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
artemis.facts: Girl of Zeus and sister of Apollon.  Goddess protectrice of trees and savage beasts.

artsimovich.facts: Study of plasmas.  Development of reactors with nuclear fusion called Tokamak.

aryabhata.general_1: Very damaged circular formation almost a ghost crater.
aryabhata.slopes: Slightly steep slopes non existent to the North-West.
aryabhata.walls: North-West walls gobbled by the lava of Mare Tranquillitatis.
aryabhata.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Craterlet.
aryabhata.facts: Resolution of equations of 1st degree.  Development of the theory of the epicycles.

arzachel.general_1: Circular formation forming a remarkable trio with Ptolemaeus and Alphonsus.
arzachel.slopes: Very steep slopes of 1000 m bearing Arzachel B and C and Alpetragius M and N to the North-West Arzachel E and R to the South-West and Parrot C to the East.
arzachel.floor: Extensive flat floor. Central mountain of 1500 m high supporting a craterlet on its South slope. Numerous craterlets whose Arzachel A K H and T. Contains Rimae Arzachel to the North-East. Hills and rilles.
arzachel.facts: Personal astronomer of the king of Toledo al-Ma'mun.  Inventor of several instruments of observation.  Editor of the first astronomical tables called

asada.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated to the South-West of the rim of a tray.
asada.slopes: Slightly steep slopes but to the North-East.

asclepi.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Asclepi B and D to the North-West and Asclepi K and L to the South-East.
asclepi.walls: Fairly high walls damaged to the South by a little marked crater.

ashbrook.general_1: Circular formation damaged to the South West.
ashbrook.floor: Flat floor covered by an Drygalski ejecta in the North-West.

aston.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Damaged formation.
aston.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed by Röntgen in tha West.
aston.facts: Discoverer of isotopes. Nobel Price of chemistry in 1922.

atlas.general_1: Forms a remarkable couple with Hercules. Circular formation.
atlas.slopes: Very steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the South.
atlas.floor: Tormented floor. Central mountain. Contains Rimae Atlas. Hills and craterlets.
atlas.facts: Giant father of Pleiads and Hyades condemned by Zeus to sustain the celestial vault on its shoulders to have been the ally of Titans.

atwood.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting trio with Bilharz and Naonobu.
atwood.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Naonobu to the North Bilharz to the West and Langrenus KA to the South-East.
atwood.walls: Fairly high walls in light terraces.
atwood.facts: Inventor in 1784 of a machine that wears its name and allowing to verify laws of the dynamics.  Study on the floating body stability.

autolycus.general_1: Forms a remarkable triangle with Aristillus and Archimedes. Circular formation.
autolycus.slopes: Very steep slopes bearing the craterlet Autolycus A to the East.
autolycus.floor: Flat tormented floor. Central mountain. Hills.

auwers.facts: Author of a fundamental star catalogue used for meridian refractors observations.

auzout.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-East slope of Mare Crisium.
auzout.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Van Albada to the South.
auzout.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor with small central relief.
auzout.facts: Inventor of the micrometer in 1667.  Improved astronomical instruments of the period.

avery.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated in the zone of librations.
avery.facts: Discoverer of properties of the ADN as hereditary support in 1944. Specialist of the pneumonia.  Lasker Price in 1947.

avicenna.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
avicenna.facts: Doctor of prince Boukhara. Author of medecine cannons. Numerous deseases description and of their treatment. Author of a cosmology based on possible and necessary beings.

avogadro.facts: Physics professor in Turino university in 1820. Discoverer of atoms number in an atom-gram. Author of  a law on gases density.

azophi.general_1: Circular formation forming a remarkable trio with Abenezra and Abenezra C.
azophi.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Abenezra to the North-West Azophi J to the North-East Azophi G to the South and a craterlet to the East.
azophi.walls: Very high walls with light terraces pushing Abenezra and ridden by Azophi C to the North.
azophi.floor: Flat floor. Craterlets whose a double to the North.
azophi.facts: Author of the Book on permanent star constellations in 965 and works on the astrolabe and the astrology.

baade.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
baade.facts: Specialist of galaxies.  Discoverer of 2 types of stellar populations.  Study on Cepheids stars.  Discoverer of asteroids Icare and Hidalgo.

babakin.facts: Scientist involved in the soviet space program.

babbage.slopes: Slightly steep slopes crushed by Pythagoras to the North-West and by South to the South-East.
babbage.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting the crater Babbage A & C. Hill rilles and craterlets.
babbage.facts: Invented a machine to calculate known as computer ancestor.  Treaty on the production in large series in 1832.

babcock.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

baby ray.general_1: Smmall circular formation of the Apollo 16 landing site.

back.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations. Forms an interesting couple with Schubert.
back.general_2: Not on Plate 9A but probably Upper Imbrian

backlund.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
backlund.facts: Director of Pulkovo observatory in 1895. Survey of celestial mechanic.

baco.general_2: Probably Nectarian. should be shown on Plate 7A not 6A
baco.slopes: Steep slopes bearing a crater to the East Baco S to the North Baco B and N to the North-West and Baco O and A to the South.
baco.facts: Father of the scientific experimentation.  Nicknamed the 'Admirable Doctor'. Inventor of many transport devices and products including gun  powder.

baillaud.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Euctemon to the North-West and Baillaud A to the North-East.
baillaud.walls: Fairly high walls damaged to the North and to the South.
baillaud.floor: Floor filled with lava with a crater. Hills and craterlets.
baillaud.facts: Director of the observatory of Toulouse.  Participated in the 'map of the Sky' and to the creation of the International Bureau of the Hour in 1913.

bailly.general_1: Circular formation little differentiated. The largest of crater shaped formations.
bailly.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta from Orientale
bailly.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing many craters.
bailly.walls: High walls ridden by Bailly A to the South-East.
bailly.floor: Extensive and Fairly flat floor to the South and tormented to the North. Spangled of craters and craterlets whose Bailly B to the South Bailly D & C to the North-West and Bailly F & I to the center. Hills.
bailly.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1763.  Author of several histories of the astronomy. Mayor of Paris.

baily.general_1: Partially dismantled formation to the South-East.
baily.walls: Slightly high walls supporting an incomplete crater to the North-East and damaged to the South.
baily.facts: Founder of the astronomical Company of London in 1836. Determination of the density of the Earth.  Discoverer of the phenomenon of 'grains of Baily' during solar eclipses in 1836.

balboa.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
balboa.general_2: Probably Nectarian. should be shown on Plate 7A not 6A
balboa.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Balboa A to the South-East and Dalton to the South-West.
balboa.facts: Discoverer of the Pacific Ocean in 1513.

ball.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Ball A to the North-West and Ball C to the South as large.
ball.walls: High walls in terraces supporting a craterlet to the South.
ball.floor: Fairly flat and little extensive floor. Important central mountain.
ball.facts: Amateur having confirmed the discovery of rings of Saturn by Huygens.

ballet.general_1: Formation circulaire isolée en forme de bol

balmer.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing the crater Hecataeus C to the North-East.
balmer.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the North.
balmer.floor: Large flat floor filled with lava. Numerous craterlets whose a central.

banachiewicz.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
banachiewicz.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Banachiewicz E and F to the South-West.
banachiewicz.walls: Fairly high walls supporting Banachiewicz B to the West.

bancroft.slopes: Steep slopes bearing an escarpment to the South-West.

bandfield.general_1: Recent craterlet surrounded by a radiating system
bandfield.facts: Work on instruments of the Osiris-Rex MRO LRO MGS Spirit & Opportunity probes

banting.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape. Recent.
banting.facts: Discovery of the insulin.  Nobel Price of medicine in 1941.

barbier.general_2: Likely to be Nectarian: should be on Plate 7B not 6B. relatively fresh
barbier.facts: Survey on stellar spectrophotometry. Star spectral classification with D. Chalonge. International observation network of atmosphere luminescence.

barkla.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Langrenus M to the North-West and a crater to the North.
barkla.floor: Tormented floor with line of crest.
barkla.facts: Works on radioelectric wavew and X rays.  Nobel Price in1917.

barnard.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
barnard.slopes: Steep slopes crushed by Humboldt to the North-West and bearing Abel to the South.
barnard.walls: High walls in terraces ridden by Barnard B to the South-West and by Abel A to the South.
barnard.floor: Very tormented floor. Numerous craterlets and lines of crests.
barnard.facts: Discoverer of a twenty of comets including the first by the photograph. Director of the Yerkes Observatory.  Photographs of the Milky Way.  Catalogue of dark nebulae.  Discoverer of Amalthee and a close star with strong proper motion.

barocius.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the South-East slope of Maurolycus.
barocius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes overlapped by Barocius B and C to the North-East.
barocius.walls: High walls especially to the South-East.
barocius.floor: Tormented floor supporting Barocius W. Small mountain off-center. Craterlets and lines of crest.

barringer.facts: Survey on Meteor Crater in Arizona. Author of meteoritic origin of lunar craters.

barrow.slopes: Slightly steep slopes overlapped to the North-East by the crater Barrow C and to the South-West by the crater Barrow A.
barrow.facts: Co-author of the infinitesimal calculation.  Author of optical calculation formulae and calculations of areas.

bartels.general_1: In the zone of librations. Circular formation.
bartels.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Bartels A to the North.
bartels.walls: Slightly high walls in light terraces.

bayer.general_1: Circular formation situated on the North-East slope of Schiller.
bayer.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed to the West by Schiller and bearing many craters whose Bayer K to the North-East and Bayer E to the South-East.
bayer.walls: Fairly high walls in light terraces.
bayer.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting a crater to the West.
bayer.facts: Author of the atlas Uranometria using Greek letters to appoint stars in 1603.

beals.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations on the South slope of Riemann. Circular formation.

bear mountain.general_1: Semi-circular hill in Taurus Littrow valley near the Apollo 17 landing site.

beaumont.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the South-West bank of Mare Nectaris.
beaumont.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Beaumont K to the North-East Beaumont E to the South-West and a double craterlet to the South.
beaumont.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by a craterlet to the North-West.  Breach to the East opening on Mare Nectaris.
beaumont.floor: Fairly tormented floor filled with lava supporting an horseshoe shaped  crater to the East. Craterlets and hills.
beaumont.facts: Engineer of Mines.  Author of a geological map of France with Dufrénoy.  Secretary of the Academy of Sciences.  Author of a method of dating rocky layers.

becquerel.facts: Discoverer of piezoelectricity in 1819 and of a photovoltaic battery in 1839. Conceiver of the electrochimic actinometer.

becvar.facts: Author of several celestial and stellar atlases.

beer.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated to the North extremity of a wrinkle ridge of Mare Imbrium. Forms an interesting couple with Feuillée.
beer.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a chain of craterlets oriented West East to the East and a dome to the South.
beer.facts: Collaborator of M?dler. Author of a map of the Moon in 1837 and a map of Mars planet.

behaim.general_1: Circular formation to the limit of the zone of librations.
behaim.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing the crater Behaim B to the West and Behaim S to the West.
behaim.facts: Geographer of the expedition of Diogo Ciao in Africa.  Drew a terrestrial globe in 1492 showing the known world before Colomb.

bel'kovich.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
bel'kovich.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Hayn to the North-West Belkovitch A and B to the South and Belkovitch K to the North-East.
bel'kovich.floor: Large flat floor with a rille. Central hill.

bela.general_1: Very lengthened formation. South starting point of Rima Hadley.
bela.floor: Rounded floor in form of shell of boat.

bell.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
bell.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta possibly pre-Nectarian

bellot.slopes: Steep slopes bearing mountainous crests to the East and to the South and Bellot A and B to the South-West.

belyaev.facts: Voskhod 2 mission cosmonaut with Leonov on the march 18 1965.

bench.general_1: Small geological formation visited by Apollo 12 astronauts.

bergman.facts: Mineralogist. Discoverer of nickel wolfram and of carbonates composition.

berkner.walls: Slightly step walls with not complete terraces.
berkner.floor: Flat floor in the North tormented in the South with a central horseshoe shaped mountain.

bernoulli.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Bernouilli A to the North.
bernoulli.facts: Works on the infinitesimal calculation.  Specialist of probabilities.

berosus.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta younger than Crisium Basin. Maybe Nectarian - on the map in the source (GHM) it is classified as Nectarian.
berosus.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava.
berosus.facts: Inventor of a solar dial.  Author of a history of Babylon about 280 BC.

berzelius.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Craterlets. Rille.
berzelius.facts: Secretary of the Academy of Sciences in 1818.  Separated the organic chemistry and the mineral chemistry.  Inventor of symbols and chemical equations.  Laws of the electrochemistry.

bessarion.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape. Three white radial rays.
bessarion.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Bessarion E to the North.
bessarion.facts: Cardinal in 1439.  Partisan of the Union of Churches.  Promoter of the Renaissance in Italy.

bessel.floor: Extensive flat floor filled with lava. Craterlets.
bessel.facts: Founder of the observatory of K?nigsberg.  Observation of 75 000 stars.  Measure of the distance of 61 Cygni in 1838.  Prediction of the existence of the companion of Sirius.

bettinus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Bettinus A to the South-West and many craterlets whose a couple to the South-East.
bettinus.walls: Fairly high walls ridden by two craterlets to the North-West.
bettinus.floor: Flat floor with a craterlet to the North-East. Mountain slightly off-center to the North-West. Craterlets.

bhabha.facts: Etude sur les rayons cosmiques. Président de la 1ère conférence sur les applications pacifiques de l'énergie nucléaire de Genève en 1955. Mort dans un accident d'avion.

bi sheng.slopes: Steep and rugged slopes crushed by a big crater in the North-West and a big craterlet in the North-East..
bi sheng.floor: Flat floor riddled with craters and craterlets.

bianchini.general_1: Situated on the line of crest of Montes Swore. Circular formation.
bianchini.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Bianchini P to the North.

biela.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Biela A to the East Biela B to the South and Rosenberger A to the North-West.
biela.walls: High walls in terraces overlapped by Biela C to the East and by a crater to the West.
biela.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Mountain with three summits off-center in the North.

bilharz.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting trio with Atwood and Naonobu.
bilharz.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Atwood to the East and Langrenus FB to the North.
bilharz.walls: Slightly high walls in terraces to the East.
bilharz.facts: Has given its name to a sickness caused by parasitic worms :  the bilharziose.

billy.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting couple with Hansteen.
billy.general_2: Partly covered by Orientale ejecta. possibly Lower Imbrian
billy.slopes: Slightly steep slopes but to the South-East and bearing Mons Hansteen to the North Billy K to the North-East and Billy D to the South-West.
billy.floor: Very flat floor filled of somber lava. Craterlets.
billy.facts: Equally astrologer.  Believed in a mysterious comet influence.

bingham.facts: Discoverer of Machu Picchu inca city on 1911. Governer and republican senator of Connecticut.

biot.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated in a gulf of the South part of Mare Fecunditatis.

birkeland.facts: Works on terrestrial magnetic field. Discoverer of the origin of polar aurorae.

birkhoff.facts: General theory of dynamic systems.Demonstration of the last theoreme of Poincaré. Works on relativity theory.

birmingham.walls: Slightly high walls supporting Birmingham B to the South.
birmingham.floor: Tormented floor with a double central craterlet. Hills craterlets depressions and rilles.

birt.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on the bank of Mare Nubium.
birt.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Birt A to the South-East Rima Birt and Birt F to the West and the craterlets Birt K J and H to the South-West.

bjerknes.facts: Hertz assistant. Works on magnetic resonances. Discoverer of equations of climate models.

black.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated in the zone of librations.
black.facts: Disciple of Lavoisier.  Study of the carbonic gas in 1754. Initiator of notions of quantity of heat and latent and specific heat.

blackett.facts: Works on cosmic rays. First photography of a transmutation phenomena on 1925. Author of a general theory on the magnetisme. Nobel prize on 1948.

blagg.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on a wrinkle ridge of Sinus Medii.
blagg.facts: Selenographer.  Participated in the elaboration of the lunar nomenclature of the IAU in 1935.

blancanus.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-West slope of Clavius.
blancanus.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Blancanus D to the East Blancanus C to the South-West and a crater to the South.
blancanus.floor: Flat floor with numerous craterlets whose a group of five to the South-East. Small central triple mountains.

blanchard.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
blanchard.facts: Works on parachute. First Channel crossing on 1785. Balloon fall in la Hague on 1808.

blanchinus.general_1: Slightly lengthened formation oriented North South.
blanchinus.slopes: Steep slopes bearing La Caille and La Caille D to the North-West and Werner to the South
blanchinus.walls: Slightly high walls but to the South and ridden by Blanchinus B to the West.
blanchinus.floor: Flat floor with numerous parallel folds. Hills and craterlets whose Blanchinus M.

blazhko.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union in 1929. Discover of a variation of the amplitude and period of RR Lyrae stars known as the Blazhko effect.

bliss.general_1: Almost circular formation situated on tthe North-West ejecta of Plato.
bliss.walls: Slightly steep walls in the West and flatter in the East.

block.general_1: Small geological formation visited by Apollo 12 astronauts.

bobillier.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on the North slope of Dorsum Buckland.

bobone.facts: Photographic observations of comets and some asteroids.

bode.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Rimae Bode to the North-West.
bode.floor: Extensive and little flat. Radial and raised crest line oriented South-West North-East.
bode.facts: Author of an 'Introduction to the Astronomy' in 1766.  Discoverer of an empirical law on planetary distances in 1772.  Director of the observatory of Berlin in 1786.

boethius.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
boethius.facts: Minister of Theodoric the Great. Comments on Plato and Aristote.  Works in geometry and astronomy.  Author of 'Of the consolation of the philosophy

boguslawsky.slopes: Steep slopes bearing many craters whose one to the West and Bogulawsky F to the South-East.
boguslawsky.walls: Slightly high walls in terraces ridden by Bogulawsky D to the East.
boguslawsky.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Hills and craterlets.

bohnenberger.general_1: Circular formation situated on the bank of Mare Nectaris.
bohnenberger.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Montes Pyrenaeus to the East Bohnenberger F to the North and Bohnenberger G and A to the South.
bohnenberger.walls: Slightly high walls with breach to the North.
bohnenberger.floor: Tormented floor. Double central mountain. Line of crest.
bohnenberger.facts: Studies on gyroscopes condenser and pendulums.  Study of the influence of the terrestrial rotation on the fall of bodies.

bohr.general_1: Deformed formation situated in the zone of librations.
bohr.slopes: Steep slopes bearing many craters and Vasco of Gama to the North-East.
bohr.facts: Theory of the structure of the atom in 1913.  Numerous controversies with Einstein.  Nobel Price in 1922.

bok.facts: Discoverers of compact interstellar dust or Bok globules.

boltzmann.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
boltzmann.facts: Inventor of the gaz cinetics and of a formula describing entrophy and introducing a new fundamental physical constant. Suicide because of a bad disease.

bolyai.facts: Friend of Gauss. Author of a complete system in non euclidian geometry. Works on complex numbers.

bombelli.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
bombelli.facts: Author of a treaty of algebra in 1572 in which it brings  interesting improvements.

bondarenko.facts: Selected as cosmonaut. No participation in a spatial mission.

bonpland.general_1: Damaged circular formation forming a remarkable trio with Fra Mauro and Parry.
bonpland.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Dorsum Guettard to the South-West Fra Mauro to the North and Parry to the East.
bonpland.walls: Slightly high walls divided to the South.
bonpland.floor: Extensive flat floor filled with the lava of Mare Cognitum. Crossed by Rimae Parry. Craterlets.
bonpland.facts: Explorer in Mexico and Colombia with Humboldt.  Author of a collection of 6000 plants and American South works on this continent.

boole.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
boole.slopes: Steep slopes bearing many craterlets whose Boole E to the South-East and Boole G to the North-West.
boole.walls: High walls in light terraces supporting a craterlet to the South-West.
boole.facts: Promoter of the mathematical logic.  Inventor of a branch of the algebra on totalities.

borda.slopes: Fairly steep Slopes riden by several craters to the South-West.
borda.walls: High damaged walls ridden by a crater to central mountain to the South-East and by a craterlet to the North.
borda.floor: Slightly flat floor extensive. Important central mountain. Lines of crest.
borda.facts: Memory on the movement of projectiles in 1756.  Cruises in the Atlantic Ocean.  Inventor of the reflecting circle.  Installation of the metric system.

borel.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape. Recent.
borel.facts: Founder of the Institute Henri Poincaré.  Theory of totalities.  Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1921.

boris.general_1: Small elongated depression composed of two sticked craterlets.

borman.facts: Astronaut of the Apollo 8 mission. First lunar orbit on the December 25th 1968.  Chairman of Eastern Air Lines.

born.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the South and one to the North-East.
born.facts: Initiator of the theory quantique.  Author of a method of approximation that wears its name. Works in physical molecular and atomic.  Price Nobel in 1954.

borya.general_1: Small geological formation on the Luna 17 landing site.

bosch.general_1: Damaged circular formation near North pole.

boscovich.general_1: Wrecked formation of South-East North-West oriented rectangular shape.
boscovich.slopes: Steep slopes bearing the lengthened crater Boscovich P to the North-West.
boscovich.walls: Fairly high walls collapsed to the West.
boscovich.floor: Flat floor filled of somber lava supporting Rimae Boscovich. Line of crest.
boscovich.facts: Author of many astronomy and mathematics works.  Promoter of theories of Newton. Author of an atomic theory of the matter.

bose.facts: Inventor of an electrical ultra short waves generator on 1897. Works on molecular phenomenas.

boss.general_1: In the zone of librations. Circular formation.
boss.general_2: Not on Plate 9A but probably Upper Imbrian. possibly Lower Imbrian
boss.facts: Author of a catalogue of stars.

bouguer.facts: Mission to Peru with La Condamine in 1735.  Discoverer of anomalies of the field of gravity of the Earth.  Inventor of the héliometer in 1748.

boussingault.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Boussingault E to the North-West and Boussingault B to the South-East.
boussingault.walls: High walls in terraces overlapped by Boussingault K to the North-West.
boussingault.floor: Floor replaced by Boussingault A concentric forming a double enclosure.
boussingault.facts: Works in metallurgy and on nitrogenous fertilizer.  Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1839.

bowen.slopes: Fairly steep slopes to the East.

bowen apollo.general_1: Small geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

boyle.facts: Co-inventor of the law on gaz compressibility with Mariotte. Inventor of the zero of temperatures at the ice fusion point. Adversory of the elements theory of Aristote. Inventor of the notion of elements and of analytical methods.

brackett.general_1: Ghost circular formation situated on the North flank of Rimae Plinius.
brackett.floor: Flat floor filled with the lava of Mare Serenitatis.

bragg.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
bragg.facts: Head of the Royal Great Britain Institution on 1923. Autor of numerous works on X rays and radioactivity with his son. Inventor of a high frequency spectrograph. Nobel prize on 1915.

brashear.facts: Builder of astronomical instruments. Inventor of the silver coating of the telescopes mirrors.

brayley.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the South-East.

bredikhin.facts: Head of the Moscow and Pulkovo observatories. Works on comets tails and on the Jupiter Great Red Spot.

breislak.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Baco S to the South and Baco B to the South-West.
breislak.walls: Fairly high walls riddled of craterlets on its East side.
breislak.floor: Flat floor with hills and craterlets whose a couple to the South.

brenner.slopes: Steep slopes subsisting to the West and bearing Metius to the South-East and Stiborius A to the North-West.
brenner.walls: High walls displayed and riddled of craters whose Brenner A to the South and Brenner E to the East.
brenner.floor: Tormented floor with an extensive plateau to the North. Craterlets and lines of crest.
brenner.facts: Amateur observer of the Moon and planets.

brewster.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a hill to the North.
brewster.facts: Laws of the polarization by reflection in 1815.  Discoverer of telluric rays in the solar specter in 1834.  Inventor of a electromagnet of a polarimeter and the kaleidoscope.

brianchon.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
brianchon.slopes: Riddled and Slightly steep slopes of craters.
brianchon.walls: Fairly high walls crushed by Brianchon B to the South.
brianchon.facts: Pupil of Monge.  Specialist of the geometry.  Memory on curved surfaces of the second degree published in 1808.

bridge.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 15 landing site.

bridgman.general_2: Younger than Humboldtianum and Moscoviense basins
bridgman.facts: Works on ultra pressures and on cristals properties. Nobel prize on 1946.

briggs.floor: Flat floor. Central mountain. 3 lines of crest.
briggs.facts: Author of a table of 31 000 logarithms to 14 decimals in 1624 and a table of trigonometrical values in 1633.

brill.general_1: Crater having impacted the floor of the De Gerlache crater.
brill.facts: Worked in the field of launchers in the United States. Specialist in rocket engines. Inventor of a satellite engine.

brisbane.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Peirescius D to the North and Brisbane E to the South-East.
brisbane.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a craterlet to the North-East.

bronk.facts: President of Johns Hopkins University and president of The Rockefeller University. Also president of the National Academy of Sciences.

bronte.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

brouwer.general_2: Partly covered by Orientale ejecta likely pre-Nectarian possibly Nectarian: should be shown on Plate 6A not 7A
brouwer.facts: Revision of astronomical constants. Numerical intégration of celestial mechanics equations.

brown.general_1: South-East North-West lengthened and damaged formation.
brown.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing many craterlets whose a trio to the South-West.
brown.walls: Slightly high walls crushed by Brown E to the South-East.
brown.facts: Specialist of the celestial mechanics.  Editor of a theory of movements of the Moon.  Discovers in 1926 the irregularity of the terrestrial rotation.

bruce.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
bruce.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the North.
bruce.facts: Amateur astronomer.  Financed many astronomy schools and observatories of the world.

brunner.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
brunner.facts: Head of Zurich observatory. Works on solar activity. Member of the Royal Astronomical Society on 1945

buch.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting couple with Busching.
buch.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Busching to the North-East and Busch C to the North.
buch.floor: Very flat floor supporting the craterlets whose a large to the North.
buch.facts: Author of the deep volcano origin and chains of mountains. Geological map of Germany in 1826.

buffon.facts: Member of the Académie des Sciences on 1733. Head of the King Garden on 1739. Author of the 36 volumes of the Histoire naturelle published from 1749 to 1804. First evolutionism hypotheses. Great popularizer of sciences.

bullialdus.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the West bank of Mare Nubium.
bullialdus.slopes: Very steep and rugged slopes bearing the craterlets Bullialdus L to the West Bullialdus E to the South-West and crater Bullialdus A and B to the South.
bullialdus.walls: Very high walls in terraces with sweeter slopes to the South-West.
bullialdus.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor with ruins to the South-West. Important central mountain with several summits. Rays.

bunsen.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
bunsen.walls: Slightly high walls wrecked to the South.
bunsen.facts: Inventor of an electrical battery and many machines.  Creator of the spectral analysis.

burbidge.general_1: Circular formation on the South slope of Nobile Crater
burbidge.facts: Spouse of Geoffrey Burbidge. Head of the Greenwich observatory on 1972. President of the  American Society of Astronomy on 1976. Developer of one of the spectrograph of the Hubble Space Telescope.

burckhardt.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Burckhardt E to the South-West Burckhardt F to the North-East and Burckhardt A to the South-East.
burckhardt.floor: Flat floor. Central mountain. Line of crest to theSouth-East.

burg.general_1: Circular formation. Surrounded by a mountainous uprising.
burg.facts: Author of a theory of movements of the Moon.

burnham.general_1: South North lengthened and wrecked formation. Seems to result from the fusion of 3 craters.
burnham.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Burnham A to the South and Burnham L to the South-East.
burnham.walls: Slightly high walls destroyed to the South by Burnham F and ridden to the North by Burnham K.
burnham.floor: Very tormented floor with craterlets and lines of crests.
burnham.facts: Amateur Astronomer having discovered more than 1300 stars double.

busching.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting couple with Buch.
busching.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Buch to the South-West and many craterlets whose a chain to the East.
busching.floor: Tormented flat floor to the West supporting a small crater to the South-East. Hills and craterlets.

butlerov.facts: Member of Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences in 1870. Works on fat alcohools. Discoverer of  trimethylcarbinol. Author of organic compounds structures theory with Couper and Kekule.

buys-ballot.general_2: Probably Nectarian but age uncertain part of oblique impact cluster?
buys-ballot.facts: Author of a law about depressions direction center. Founder of the Dutch Meteorological Institute in 1854.

byrd.general_1: Situated near the North pole of the Moon. Circular formation.
byrd.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing many craters whose Peary to the North and Gioja to the South.
byrd.facts: 1st flight over the North Pole on May 9th 1926. 1st flight over the South Pole on November 29th 1928.

byrgius.general_1: Circular formation situated in a tormented region.
byrgius.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Byrgius D to the North-West and 2 craterlets to the South-West.
byrgius.walls: Fairly high walls ridden to the East by Byrgius A.
byrgius.floor: Flat floor tormented to the South-West. Craterlets. Rays in source of Byrgius A.
byrgius.facts: Manufacturer of precision instruments and collaborator of Kepler. Constructor of clocks and celestial spheres.

c. herschel.general_1: Situated on a wrinkle ridge. Isolated circular formation.

c. mayer.slopes: Very steep slopes bearing Mayer H in the North-West and Mayer Din the South-East.
c. mayer.floor: Extensive and little flat floor. Lengthened central mountain.

cabannes.facts: Member of french Academy of Sciences in 1946. Studies on Kerr phenomena atmospheric ozona and sky spectrography.

cabeus.general_1: Circular formation situated near the South Pole in the zone of librations.
cabeus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Cabeus A to the North and a crater to the North-East.
cabeus.facts: Jesuit.  Studies on the magnetism.  Author of Philosophia Magnetica in 1629.

cajal.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape and situated between 2 mountains.
cajal.facts: Works on the nervous system.  Discoverer of the polarity of neurons.  Many works.  Nobel Price in 1906 with Golgi.

calippus.general_1: Situated in Montes Caucasus. Circular formation.
calippus.slopes: Steep slopes bearing the craterlet Calippus E to the East.
calippus.walls: Deformed high walls to the East.
calippus.facts: Disciple of Eudoxe and director of its school.  Improvement of the cycle of Meton.

camelot.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

cameron.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated on the North-West wall of Taruntius.

campanus.general_1: Circular formation separating Palus Epidemiarum and Mare Nubium and forming an interesting couple with Mercator separated by a rille.
campanus.slopes: Steep slopes to the North bearing a rille to the South-East.
campanus.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Small central mountain. Craterlets.

cannizzaro.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
cannizzaro.facts: Application of Dulong and Petit law. Determination of atomic mass ofmetals. Synthesis of aromatic alcohools.

cannon.general_1: Circular formation situated alongside the zone of librations.
cannon.general_2: Older than Crisium Basin possibly pre-Nectarian
cannon.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a crater to the West.
cannon.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a craterlet to the North.
cannon.facts: Specialist of the classification of stellar specters.

cantor.facts: Professor at Halle University in 1879. Numerous works on numbers and sets. Discoverer of sets antinomy. Died in a mental hospital.

capella.general_1: Wrecked circular formation forming an interesting couple with Isidorus.
capella.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Isidorus to the West Capella F to the South Vallis
capella.walls: Fairly high walls in very damaged terraces supporting a craterlet to the North.
capella.floor: Slightly extensive floor. Important central mountain. Crossed by Vallis Capella.
capella.facts: Author of a theory Where Venus and Mercury turns around the Sun. Inspirer of Copernic.

capuanus.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South bank of Palus Epidemiarum.
capuanus.slopes: Steep slopes to the South crushed to the South-West by Capuanus P and with perpendicular crests to the North-West.
capuanus.walls: Fairly high walls supporting Capuanus A to the South-East high to the South-West with crater and almost gobbled to the North-East.
capuanus.floor: Flat floor with craterlets and domes.

cardanus.general_1: Circular formation. Forms an interesting couple with Krafft.
cardanus.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Cardanus R to the South Cardanus E to the South-East and Catena Krafft to the North.
cardanus.floor: Slightly flat and extensive floor. Small central mountain.
cardanus.facts: Numerous philosophical works including the astrology. Resolution of equations of 3e`me degree.  Creators of imaginary numbers. Inventor of the mechanical junction with his name.

carlini.floor: Slightly flat and extensive floor. Small central hill.
carlini.facts: Specialist of movements of the Moon.

carlos.general_1: Elongated triangular formation on the Noth end of Bela.

carmichael.general_1: Circular formation. Forms an interesting couple with Hill.
carmichael.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing an mountainous crest to the North and a craterlet to the South-West.

carol.general_1: Almost circular formation at the end of a crater chain including Kasper et Melissa.

carpenter.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed by Anaximander to the South-West.
carpenter.floor: Flat floor with line of crest.

carrel.slopes: Steep slopes bearing a mountainous chain to the North and to the South.
carrel.floor: Slightly flat floor extensive. Central mountain.
carrel.facts: Numerous works on transplants.  Author of 'the Man this unknown' in1936.  Nobel Price in 1912.

carrillo.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations on the North-East slope of K?stner G.

carrington.slopes: Slightly steep slopes crushed by Schumacher in the South.
carrington.walls: Slightly high walls open to the North.
carrington.facts: Discoverer of the differential rotation of the Sun by solar spots observation.

cartan.general_1: Circular formation situated on the West slope of Apollonius.
cartan.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a crater and Cartan H to the South.
cartan.facts: Professor of geometry superior the Sorbonne.  Thesis on the theory of groups in 1894.  Promoter of the differential calculation with Poincaré.

carver.facts: Feeding specialist. Peanut agriculture in United States. Works on colouring substances and cotton.

casatus.general_1: Circular formation forming a double crater with Klaproth.
casatus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Casatus A to the West and Casatus H to the East.
casatus.walls: High walls ridden by several craterlets whose Casatus J to the South.
casatus.floor: Flat floor supporting Casatus C to the North and separated from Klaproth by a line of crest.

cassegrain.facts: Doctor and amateur astronomer. Conceiver of a telescope with convex secondary mirror.

cassini.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Cassini M to the North-West.
cassini.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting Cassini A and B. Hills and craterlets.
cassini.facts: Founder and director of the Observatory of Paris in 1672. Member of the Academy of Sciences.  Discoverer of 4 satellites of Saturn and the main division of its rings.

catalan.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

catena abulfeda.general_1: Alignment composed with more or less marked craterlets of variable dimensions.
catena abulfeda.walls: Share of the South slope of Abulfeda then passes the North slope of Almanon.
catena abulfeda.floor: Ends to the North point of Rupes Altai.
catena abulfeda.facts: Prince of the dynasty of Ayyubides.  Author of 'the History' that continues the work of Ibn al-Athir.

catena artamonov.facts: Scientist involved in soviet launchers program.

catena brigitte.general_1: Small craterlets chain situated between Dawes and Mons Argaeus.
catena brigitte.slopes: Maybe a rille associated to a lava tube.

catena davy.general_1: Formation situated in the arena of the walled plain Davy Y. Oriented West-East.
catena davy.slopes: Constituted of a dozen of craterlets of 1 to 3 km of diameter.  Begins with the craterlet Davy C.
catena davy.walls: Constituted of a dozen of craterlets of 1 to 3 km of diameter.
catena davy.floor: Probably caused by the impact of several parts of a same body.
catena davy.facts: Discoverer of the sodium the potassium the barium the strontium and the calcium in 1807-1808. Specialist of the electrolysis.  Inventor of the electrical arc and a lamp for miners.

catena gregory.facts: Inventor of a reflector telescope with concave secondary mirror on 1632. Member of the Royal Society on 1668. Conception of infinitesimal methods for surfaces and volumes computing. Author of developments of trigonometrical functions and Pi.

catena humboldt.general_1: Chain of craters leaving from the center of Humboldt crossing the wall and prolonging to the North-East.
catena humboldt.facts: Brother of Alexander von Humboldt the explorer. Founder of the University of berlin in 1809.  Studies of linguistics.

catena krafft.general_1: Oriented North - South. Connects Krafft to Cardanus.

catena kurchatov.facts: Surveys in nuclar physics. Radio-elements synthesis.

catena littrow.general_1: Four craterlets aligned North - South to the North of Clercke and overlapped in Rimae Littrow.

catena mendeleev.facts: Numerous works on gases and the air. Author of a chemistry treaty on 1868 and of the periodical classification of elements on 1869.

catena michelson.facts: Inventor of an interferometer. Mesurement of light speed in various media. Mesurement of terrestrial crust tides on 1917. Nobel laureate on 1907.

catena pierre.general_1: Small inequal craters chain sinuous and completing Rima Wan Yu.

catena sylvester.general_1: Not tyîcal big valley of 140 km composed of craterlets closely sticked and joining Sylvester to Poncelet D.

catena taruntius.general_1: Irregularly spaced craterlets chain with variuous sizes on two parallel lines joining Taruntius T to Anville.
catena taruntius.facts: Astronomer friend of Cicero. Author of a birth dat for Romulus. Author of a book on celestial objects in greek which has been used by Plinius.

catena timocharis.general_1: Chain of craterlets oriented North South and very narrow situated in ejected it North Timocharis.
catena timocharis.facts: Close with school of Alexandrie.  Attempt of definitions of coordinate stellar based on the Ecliptique.

catena yuri.general_1: Small sitcked craterlets chain at the border between Mare Imbrium and Oceanus Procellarum. Probably created by an Euler ejecta.

catharina.general_1: Very damaged circular formation forming a South North aligned remarkable trio  with Theophilus and Cyrillus.
catharina.slopes: Fairly steep slopes and rugged to the North-East and bearing Catharina D to the North-West Catharina A to the South-West and Catharina C to the South-East
catharina.walls: High walls to the South-East crushed by the large ghost semi crater Catharina P to the North by Catharina B & G to the North-East and by the crater Catharina S to the South.
catharina.floor: Flat floor to the East and tormented to the West. Craterlets crack and hills.
catharina.facts: Christian martyrdom.  Supports philosophers.  Beheaded on order of the Emperor Maxence

cauchy.general_1: Bright circular formation with bowl shape situated between the 'hyperboles' of Rima Cauchy and Rupes Cauchy.
cauchy.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Rima Cauchy to the North-East.
cauchy.facts: Author of the theory of functions of a complex variable.  Works on the development in series of functions.  Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1816 and of the Bureau of Longitudes in 1839.

cavalerius.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a remarkable couple with Hevelius.
cavalerius.floor: Flat floor with small central mountain. Three lines of crest. Craterlets.
cavalerius.facts: Disciple of Galilée.  Author of the theory of the indivisible in 1635. Precursor of the integer calculation.

cavendish.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Rimae De Gasparis to the East and Cavendish F to the South.
cavendish.walls: Fairly high walls supporting Cavendish A to the North-East and Cavendish E to the South-East.
cavendish.floor: Tormented floor with two ghost craters. Small central mountain. Hills line of crest and craterlets.
cavendish.facts: Member of the Royal Company in 1803. Studies on gases. Discovers hydrogen in 1766.  Synthesis of the water in 1783.  Creator of the quantitative electrostatic with Maxwell.

caventou.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
caventou.facts: Co-Discoverer of the strychnine in 1818 and the quinine in 1820 with Pierre Joseph Pelletier.

cayley.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape. Forms a remarkable trio with Whewell and Morgan.
cayley.facts: Author of the theory of the determinants and the invariants with Sylvester.  Discovery of matrical properties.  Works in projective geometry.   Member of the Royal Mathematics Society.

celsius.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the West slope of Rabbi Levi.
celsius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Celsius A and a craterlet to the North and  three craterets aligned North South to the East.
celsius.walls: Fairly high walls supporting three craterlets to the South-West.
celsius.floor: Flat floor supporting a craterlet to the North.
celsius.facts: Inventor of the centigrade scale of temperature measure.

censorinus.general_1: Bright and circular formation with bowl shape.
censorinus.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a very clear material and Censorinus A larger to the East.
censorinus.facts: Author of an astrological treaty presenting astral them influence according to the chronology.

cepheus.walls: Fairly high walls in terraces overlapped by the craterlet Cepheus A.
cepheus.facts: Imaginary King of Ethiopia.  Designates also a boreal constellation.

chacornac.general_1: Formation wrecked. Forms a remarkable couple with Posidonius.
chacornac.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed by Posidonius to the North-West.
chacornac.floor: Tormented flat floor supporting the craterlet Chacornac A and Rimae Chacornac. Hills.
chacornac.facts: Discoverer of six asteroids.  Study on solar spots. Theory of the lunar crater origin.

chadwick.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
chadwick.facts: Rutherford schoolboy. Works on nuclear physics and elements desint‚gration. Discoverer of neutron nature in 1932. Participation in the first atomic bomb construction in 1945 at Los Alamos. Nobel laureate in 1935.

chaffee.facts: Astronautical engineer and Apollo 1 mission astronaut. Deceased in module ground fire during a training.

challis.general_1: Little deep circular formation. Overlapped with Main.

chalonge.facts: Spectral classification of stars with Daniel Barbier. Jungfraujoch observations promoter.

chamberlin.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

champollion.facts: Oriental languages translator. Hieroglyphs translation using Rosetta stone in 1822.

chandler.facts: Surveys on Earth shape and rotation.

chang-ngo.general_1: Small craterlet included in one of the catenas situated on the floor of Alphonsus.

chapman.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
chapman.facts: Surveys on terrestrial magnetism and lunar attraction influence. Author of a ionosphere formation theory.

chappe.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
chappe.facts: Observer of Venus transits in front of the Sun on june 5th 1761 in Siberia and in 1769 in California where he died.

charles.general_1: Small craterlet situated at the South end of Dorsum Heim.

chawla.general_1: Big craterlet in a group of anonymous craters in a bigger damaged carter.

chebyshev.facts: Founder of a mathematical school. Works on algorithms PI number and elliptical functions.

chevallier.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Chevallier A to the West Chevallier M to the North and Chevallier K to the South.
chevallier.floor: Floor filled with lava containing Chevallier B. Narrow grooves and craterlets.
chevallier.facts: Director of the observatory of Durnham.

chien-shiung wu.general_1: Tiny regular and isolated craterlet on the southern marine part of the Apollo impact basin.
chien-shiung wu.facts: Chinese origin. Participated in the Manhattan Project. Separation of uranium isotopes by gaseous diffusion. Work on weak interactions. Nicknamed the Chinese Marie Curie.

ching-te.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape squeezed between two mountainous mountains.

chladni.general_1: Isolated circular formation in form of bowl situated to the South extremity of a mountainous area.
chladni.slopes: Slightly steep slopes but to the North.
chladni.facts: Specialist of the sounds and vibratory phenomena.  Determination of the speed of the sound in various gas.  Author of a theory on the cosmic meteorite origin in 1794.

chretien.facts: Astronomer in Meudon and Nice Observatories. Professor at Paris Optics Institute. Conceiver of an aplanetic telescope in 1930 with Georges Willis Ritchey. Conceiver of catadioptrical devices and of Hypergonar lens used in Cinemascope since 1925.

cichus.general_1: Circular formation situated on the bank of Palus Epidemiarum.
cichus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Weiss to the North-East.
cichus.walls: High walls in terraces supporting Cichus C to the West.
cichus.floor: Slightly extensive flat floor with two craters. Hills and craterlets.
cichus.facts: Death on the woodshed for heresy.

cinco.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 16 astronauts and comprised in a five craterlets group.

clairaut.slopes: Fairly steep slopes to the North bearing Clairaut E to the North-West. and Clairaut S to the East.
clairaut.walls: Fairly high walls crushed by Clairaut B to the West and by Clairaut A to the South.
clairaut.floor: Deformed flat floor supporting Clairaut D to the North and a second crater. Craterlets.
clairaut.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1731.  Author of the 'Theory of the Moon' in 1752.  Inventor of a partial solution of the problem of 3 bodies.  Calculations on the orbit of the comet of Halley.

clark.facts: Builder of the two biggest astronomical lenses of the World (Lick - 91 cm / Yerkes - 102 cm). Discoverer of Sirius companion in 1862.

clausius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes with perpendicular crest line to the South and two craterlets to the North.
clausius.facts: Has written a new statement of 2nd principle of the thermodynamic in 1850 introducing the entropy.  One of creators of the cinetic of gases in 1857.

clavius.slopes: Steep slopes riddled bearing crater Blancanus to the South-West.
clavius.walls: Very high walls ridden by Porter to the North-East Rutherford to the South-East Clavius K to the South-West and Clavius L to the West.
clavius.floor: Large flat floor with Clavius D C N J & JA on an arc of circle. Numerous craterlets whose a chain to the South-West. Lines of crests.
clavius.facts: Translator of Euclide.  Nicknamed it even

cleomedes.general_2: Younger than Crisium Basin. floor fractured (FFC) DHCs on the floor
cleomedes.slopes: Steep slopes bearing many craterlets whose Tralles to the North-West and Delmotte to the South-East.
cleomedes.walls: Fairly high walls overlapped to the North-West by Cleomedes A and E and to the South by Cleomedes C.
cleomedes.floor: Large flat floor filled with lava and supporting Cleomedes B and J and Rimae Cleomedes. Small mountain off-center.
cleomedes.facts: Author of a treaty of astronomy called 'Theory of circular movements of celestial bodies '.

cleostratus.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Cleostratus E and F to the North-West.
cleostratus.walls: High walls supporting Cleostratus M to the North and two craterlets to the South-West.
cleostratus.facts: Has perfected the athenian calendar by introducing a Moon/Sun cycle of 8 years.  Author of the system of signs of the Zodiac.

clerke.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape and overlapping a rille of Rimae Littrow.

cochise.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

cockcroft.facts: Professor in Cambridge University in 1939. Works on radar andatomic bomb. Director of Harwell nuclear center in 1946. Nobel laureate in 1951 with Ernest Walton.

collins.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
collins.facts: Pilot of the cabin of the mission Apollo 11

colombo.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the West bank of Mare Fecunditatis.
colombo.slopes: Steep slopes to the South and overlapped by the large crater Colombo A to the North-West by Colombo B to the South-West and by Colombo M to the East.
colombo.walls: Slightly high walls to the North but high and tormented to the South-East.
colombo.floor: Flat floor. Small central mountain. Hills and craterlets.
colombo.facts: Discoverer of America (Island Bahamas) 12 October 1492.  Realized three others travel in Southern and Central America."

compton.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
compton.facts: Discoverer of the effect of photons. Surveys on cosmic rays. Nobel laureate in 1927 with Charles Wilson.

condon.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the bank of Sinus Successus.
condon.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Webb F and G to the South-East.
condon.walls: Slightly high walls damaged to the South-West.
condon.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Hills.
condon.facts: President of a commission of studies on UFO and author of a famous report."

condorcet.general_1: Circular formation situated to the East of Mare Crisium.
condorcet.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Condorcet A E and G to the South-West.
condorcet.walls: Slightly high walls ridden to the North by Condorcet Y.
condorcet.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava.
condorcet.facts: Collaborator of 'the Encyclopedia' .  Chief of the 'Philosophical Party' .  Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1769.

cone.general_1: Small craterlet ned by Apollo 14 astronauts where samples of impact Imbrium have been sampled.

congreve.general_2: Younger than Korolev Basin. relatively old
congreve.facts: Conceiver of a military rocket in 1804. Works on powder and color printing. Introduction of gaz for towns lighting.

conon.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated in Montes Apenninus.
conon.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor with small central hill.
conon.facts: Friend of Archimede.  Author of the constellation 'Hair of Berenice'.  Author of 7 books devoted to the astronomy.

cook.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the South-West bank of Mare Fecunditatis.
cook.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a chain of craterlets to the North-East a crater to the South-West and a perpendicular mountainous crest to the North.
cook.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by 2 craterlets to the North-East.
cook.floor: Extensive flat floor filled with lava supporting the crater Cook A to the South-East.
cook.facts: Expeditions on the Endeavour to Tahiti in 1769 for the passage of Venus in front of the Sun.  Discovery of the New-Zealand and Australia in 1770. Discovery of Hawaii in 1778.

copernicus.general_1: Young and isolated formation with hexagonal form. Bright rays all around.
copernicus.slopes: Very steep slopes dominant Mare Insularum of 900 m rugged and bearing Fauth to the South and Gay-Lussac to the North.
copernicus.floor: Floor flatter to the North that to the South. Three central mountains (1200 m). Hills and ruins in the arena.
copernicus.facts: Canon of Frauenburg in 1479.  Doctor of the university of Ferrare in 1503.  Author of the 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium ' in 1543 presenting the heliocentric system in which the Earth and planets turn around the Sun.

coriolis.facts: Ponts et Chauss‚es engineer. Professor in mechanics in 1816. Surveys on centrifugal strengthes.

couder.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
couder.facts: Director of Paris Optics Institute in 1926. Member of french Academy of Sciences in 1954. Numerous surveys on astrometrical and astrophysical instruments. Author of "Refractors and telescopes" in 1935 with Andr‚ Danjon.

coulomb.facts: Discoverer of magnetic field. Author of a law on electrostatical strengthes. Member of french Academy of Sciences in 1781 and of the Institute in 1795.

courtney.general_1: Principal craterlet included in rima Zahia at its North end.

cremona.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
cremona.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Cremona A to the North.
cremona.walls: High walls crushed by Boole L to the South.
cremona.floor: Flat and extensive floor with Cremona B & C to the West.
cremona.facts: Director of School of applications of engineers of Rome. Minister of the Public Instruction in 1898.

crescent.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 12 astronauts and comprised in a seven craterlets group.

crile.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

crookes.facts: Conceiver of the radiometer in 1872 and of an X rays generating tube. Works on viscosity and gaz  conductibility. Member of the Royal Society in 1863.

crozier.general_1: Circular formation forming a clover with Crozier M and D of identical aspect.
crozier.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Crozier M to the South and Crozier D to the East.
crozier.floor: Extensive flat floor filled with somber lava.

cruger.general_1: Remarkable circular formation for its weak albedo.
cruger.floor: Flat floor filled with very somber lava. Craterlet.

curie.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
curie.facts: Discoverer of piezoelectricity in 1880 and of the transformation point in magnetism. Husband of Marie Curie in 1895. Author of the principle of phenomenas symetry. Discoverer of polonium and radium in 1898. Nobel laureate in 1903 with his wife.

curtis.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

curtius.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Curtius B to the North Curtius D to the North-East and Curtius E to the West.
curtius.walls: High walls in terraces overlapped by a crater to the East and a craterlet to the South.
curtius.floor: Flat floor supporting several craterlets whose 2 to the North-West. Small mountain with 3 summits off-center to the North-West.
curtius.facts: Publisher of the observations of Tycho Brahé.

cusanus.walls: Slightly high walls supporting two craterlets to the East.
cusanus.facts: Representative of the Pope in Germany.  Opponent to the geocentrism. Important work in literature.

cuvier.slopes: Steep slopes bearing the quartet Heraclitus to the West and a composed remarkable chain of Cuvier F A E and B to the South-East.
cuvier.floor: Flat floor with lava flood to the North-West.
cuvier.facts: Creator of the compared anatomy and the paleontology.  Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1795 and of the French Academy in 1818.

cyrillus.general_1: Damaged circular formation forming a remarkable trio with Theophilus and Catharina.
cyrillus.slopes: rugged and steep slopes bearing Theophilus to the North-East Ibn Ru'shd to the North-West and Cyrillus E F and G to the South-East.
cyrillus.walls: Fairly high walls more high to the East that to the West crushed by Theophilus to the North-East and ridden by Cyrillus A to the South-West.
cyrillus.floor: Tormented and extensive floor with 3 central mountains and a groove to the South. Hills and craterlets.
cyrillus.facts: Fit to condemn the heresy of Nestor in 431 and specified the doctrine of the Incarnation of the Christ.

cysatus.general_1: Circular formation situated on the slope of Gruemberger.
cysatus.slopes: to the West Steep slopes bearing many craterlets to the North and Cysatus E to the East.
cysatus.walls: Very high walls damaged to the South-East.

d. brown.general_1: Big craterlet Included in a group inside of a damaged anonymous crater.
d. brown.slopes: Fairly steep slopes with sharp crest.
d. brown.floor: Floor presenting two hills covering almost totally it and one could be a volcabic dome.

d'alembert.facts: Member of french Academy of Sciences in 1740 and secretary in 1772. Author of a treaty about dynamics in 1743. Computation of equinoxes precession in 1749. Leader of the Encyclopedia with Diderot.

d'arrest.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing d'Arrest M and A to the West.
d'arrest.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Hills.
d'arrest.facts: Comets and asteroid specialist.  Observer of nebulae and clusters of stars.  Numerous stellar astronomy works.

d'arsonval.facts: Numerous surveys in biological physics. Discoverer of high frequencies currents treatments. Conceiver of numerous apparatus for physics.

da vinci.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Watts to the South-East.
da vinci.walls: Very damaged walls crumbled to the South.
da vinci.floor: Very tormented floor. Central mountain. Hills craterlets and lines of crest.
da vinci.facts: Painter and author sculptor of famous works of the Renaissance. Works in many areas as anatomy the applied mechanics and the geology.
