dag.general_1: Irregularly shaped formation composing a couple with Apollonius F.

daguerre.slopes: Quasi flat slopes bearing a similar crater to the North-West and a craterlet to the South-East.
daguerre.walls: Quasi non-existent walls completely gobbled to the South.
daguerre.floor: Flat floor filled with the lava of Mare Nectaris. Small central relief subsisting. Grooves and craterlets.
daguerre.facts: Inventor of the diorama in 1822.  Associate to Niepce for the invention of the photography by daguerreotypes.

dale.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated in the zone of librations.
dale.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the South.
dale.facts: Works on the chemistry of the nervous system. Nobel Price in 1936.

dalton.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
dalton.slopes: Steep slopes crushed by Balboa in the North Balboa A in the East Vasco de Gama in the South and Einstein In the West.
dalton.floor: Flat floor with groove. Small mountain off-center.
dalton.facts: Creator of the atomic theory.  Studies on the compression of gases.  Study on the daltonism.  Author of an English grammar.

daly.general_1: Formation of irregular form forming a couple overlapped with Apollonius F.
daly.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed by Apollonius F to the East.
daly.facts: Professor in Harvard.  Specialist of glaciations of the Quaternary.

damoiseau.general_1: Fomplex formation. Crater having crushed Damoiseau M. North extremity of Rimae Grimaldi.
damoiseau.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Damoiseau K lengthened to the East.
damoiseau.floor: Tormented floor. Small central mountain. Line of crest. Craterlet.
damoiseau.facts: Author of a theory and tables on movements of the Moon.

daniell.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing the craterlet Daniell W to the North-East.
daniell.facts: Inventor of a hygrometer and an electrical battery.

danjon.general_1: Complex formation. Crater having crushed Damoiseau M. North end of Rimae Grimaldi.
danjon.facts: Director of Paris Observatory in 1945. Member of french Academy of Sciences in 1948. Conceiver of the de unpersonal astrolabe and of an interferometer. Surveys about Venus and Mercury. Author of 2 books with Andr‚ Couderc.

darney.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape of large size and situated in a mountainous region.
darney.facts: Author of many observations of the Moon.

darwin.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Darwin B to the West Cruger to the North-East and crushing Lamarck to the South.
darwin.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by 3 craters to the South-West.
darwin.floor: Tormented floor containing the Rimae Darwin. White stains. Hills and lines of crest. Craterlets. Dome with summit craterlet.
darwin.facts: Trip in South America with the 'Beagle' from 1831 to 1836.  Author of 'Of the origin of species by way of natural selection' in 1859.  Author of the theory of the transforming evolution of species called 'Darwinism'.

daubree.general_1: Deformed formation situated on the North rim of Lacus Hiemalis.
daubree.walls: Fairly high walls collapsed to the North-West.
daubree.floor: Flat floor filled with lava communicating with Lacus Gaudii to the North-West.
daubree.facts: Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1861.  Director of School of Mines in 1872.  Author of 'Synthetic studies of experimental geology' in 1879.

davisson.facts: Discoverer of electrons diffraction in 1927 with L. Germer. Conceiver of electronic optics. Nobel laureate in 1937 with G. Thomson.

davy.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a perpendicular mountain chain to the North and Catena Davy to the East.
davy.walls: Slightly high walls ridden to the South-East by Davy A.
davy.facts: Discoverer of the sodium potassium barium strontium and calcium in 1807-1808.  Specialist of the electrolysis. Inventor of the electrical arc and a lamp for miners.

dawa.general_1: Tiny craterlet in a range on a ridge of Mons Mouton.

dawes.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on a little marked wrinkle ridge to the extremity of Rimae Plinius.
dawes.floor: Fairly flat floor filled with lava. Small central relief.

de gasparis.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a double crater to the South-East Rimae De Gasparis to the North and to the South.
de gasparis.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a craterlet to the North-East.
de gasparis.floor: Flat floor filled with lava and supporting Rimae De Gasparis.

de gerlache.general_1: Almost squared crater near the North Pole.
de gerlache.slopes: Very steep slopes specially on one slide and riddled with small craterlets.
de gerlache.walls: Walls damaged by numerous craterlets and deposits.
de gerlache.floor: Floor filles with materials and digged on onse side by an anonymous big crater with a flat floor.

de la rue.slopes: Damaged steep slopes bearing Strabo to the North.
de la rue.floor: Flat floor supporting De La Rue I and a large craterlet to the center. Lines of crest crack hills and craterlets.
de la rue.facts: Inventor of machines to print in colors and for the folding of envelopes. First stereoscopic cliches of the Moon in 1857.

de moraes.general_2: Younger than Moscoviense Basin older than Humboldtianum Basin

de morgan.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape. Composing a remarkable trio with Whewell and Cayley.
de morgan.facts: Discoverer of laws of duality in logical.  Author of 'Formal logic or the calculus of inference

de roy.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

de sitter.general_1: Circular formation. Overlaps an equivalent crater not named.
de sitter.facts: Works in relativity cosmology and in celestial mechanic. Study of the movement of Jupiter satellites.  President of the IAU in 1925.

de vico.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Vico H to the East Vico P to the South Vico R to the West and Vico C D and E to the South-West.
de vico.facts: Jesuit in 1823.  Director of the Observatory of Roma in 1838. Specialist of Venus and discoverer of 6 comets.  Works on Saturn and its satellites.

de vries.facts: Discoverer of mutations in 1897. General theory about plants growth.

debes.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a couple overlapped with Debes A.
debes.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Debes A and B to the South-West.
debes.walls: Damaged and little high walls to the South-East.

debus.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

debye.facts: Director of Physics Institute of Berlin in. Teacher at Cornell University in 1940. Surveys about quantas theory electrolyths and low temperatures. Molecules measurements. Nobel laureate in chemist in 1936.

delambre.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Deslambres H to the North-West and Theon Junior to the South-West.
delambre.walls: High walls in terraces supporting Deslambres D to the North.
delambre.floor: Tormented floor. Central mountain. Hills crack and craterlets.
delambre.facts: Collaborator of Méchain.  Author of 'Tables of Jupiter and Saturn' in 1789 and of a 'History of the Astronomy'

delaunay.general_1: Double formation with heart shape situated on the North-East slope of La Caille
delaunay.slopes: Steep slopes bearing La Caille M to the West La Caille D E and F to the South and Faye to the North-East.
delaunay.walls: Fairly high walls tormented to the South.
delaunay.floor: Flat floor with important central crest line. Craterlets.
delaunay.facts: Numerous works in celstial mechanic. Director of the

delia.general_1: Squared formation included in Catena Davy.
delia.slopes: Two sides shared with adjacent craterlets.

delisle.slopes: Fairly steep slopes to the South.
delisle.facts: Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1714.  Inventor of the calculation of the distance of the Sun using passages of Mercury and Venus.  Has put in place the observatory of St-Petersbourg.

delmotte.general_1: Circular formation situated on the slope of Cleomedes.
delmotte.slopes: Fairly steep slopes to the North.
delmotte.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a lengthened craterlet to the North-West.
delmotte.floor: Flat floor filled with lava tormented to the North.

deluc.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Deluc D and Deluc T to the South Deluc H to the North-East and the double crater Deluc J to the North-West.
deluc.floor: Flat floor with small central mountain and two craterlets.

dembowski.slopes: Fairly steep slopes to the South-West and bearing Dembowski C to the South.
dembowski.walls: Fairly high walls gobbled to the North-East.
dembowski.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava. Hills.
dembowski.facts: Specialist of double stars.  Measured position of 20 000 couples.

democritus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed by a large crater gobbled to the South-West.
democritus.walls: Fairly high walls in light terraces.
democritus.floor: Slightly flat floor extensive. Central mountain.
democritus.facts: Author of a cosmography and various works on the sky and planets.  Author of the concept of atom.

demonax.general_1: Circular formation situated to the limit of the zone of librations.
demonax.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing many craters whose Scott to the South-West.
demonax.floor: Flat floor with craters to the South-East.

desargues.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.
desargues.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Desargues B and E to the North-East and Desargues A to the North-West.
desargues.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by Desargues M to the South.
desargues.facts: Unification of the theory of the conical.  Specialist of the geometry and of the perspective.

descartes.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Descartes E to the North and Descartes C to the North-East.
descartes.walls: Fairly high walls in terraces composed of several concentric rings collapsed to the North and ridden by Descartes A to the South-West.
descartes.floor: Slightly extensive and tormented floor. Crest and rille line.
descartes.facts: Initiator of the western philosophy.  Author of the 'Speech on the method' in 1637 and many other works as 'Dioptrique' 'The Meteors' and the 'Geometry' .

deseilligny.general_1: Isolated circular formation and with bowl shape situated to the extremity of Dorsum Azara.
deseilligny.facts: Selenographer.  Numerous observations of the Moon.

deslandres.slopes: Fairly steep slopes marked by craters whose Walter to the East Lexell to the South Ball to the South-West and Hell to the East.
deslandres.floor: Flat floor strewn with many craters whose a South North oriented chain to the North-East. Hills and lines of crest. Rilles and craterlets.
deslandres.facts: Inventor of the spectro-heliograph.  Specialist of the Sun. Director of the Observatory of Meudon in 1906.

dewar.facts: Conceiver of an insulated bottle for liquefied gases and of the cordite. Author of the first hydrogene liquefaction and of fluorine in 1896.

diana.general_1: Elongated crater-pit located on the summit of Maraldi 1 (ALPO) volcanic dome to the South end of Mons Esam.

diderot.facts: Leader of the Encyclopedia with D'Alembert.

dionysius.general_1: Bright and isolated circular formation. Rays
dionysius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Rimae Ritter to the North-East.
dionysius.facts: Observer (according to Riccioli) of an eclipse that would have occured during the crucifixion of Jesus - Christ.

diophantus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing the craterlet Diophantus C to the South-West.
diophantus.facts: Not well  known.  Collection of mathematics problems.  Works on equations of the first and second degree.

dirichlet.facts: Professor in Berlin University in 1831. Numerous works on algebric numbers theory.

dobrovol'skiy.facts: Cosmonaut of Soyouz 11 mission. Deceased during return to Earth on the june 30th 1971 with Volkov and Patsayev.

doerfel.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
doerfel.facts: Surveys about comets. Discoverer of the parabolic shape of their orbits.

dollond.general_1: Bright circular formation with bowl shape situated in a mountainous region.
dollond.facts: Inventor of the achromatic objective with two lenses in 1758 as well as of eyepieces with 4 or 5 lenses. Member of the Royal Company.

donati.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Faye to the South-West and many anonymous craters all around.
donati.walls: Slightly high walls of irregular form ridden by a crater to the East.
donati.floor: Tormented floor. Central mountain of 2730 m.
donati.facts: Discovers 7 comets whose that of 1858.  Pioneer of the spectroscopy. Boreal aurorae specialist.

donna.general_1: Crater-pit located on the summit of Cauchy W 1 (ALPO) volcanic dome.

donner.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

doppelmayer.general_1: Circular formation partly gobbled by the lava of Mare Humorum.
doppelmayer.slopes: Steep slopes to the South gobble to the bearing North Puiseux to the North-East.
doppelmayer.walls: High walls to the South gobbled to the North-East and ridden to the South-West by Doppelmayer P and H.
doppelmayer.floor: Flat floor filled with the lava of Mare Humorum and flat to the North but tormented to the South. Important central mountain. Hills and lines of crest.

doppler.facts: Discoverer of the wavelength shift in relation with speed. Director of Wien Physics Institute in 1851.

dorsa aldrovandi.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North - South and situated on the edge of Mare Serenitatis to the North of Mons Argaeus.
dorsa aldrovandi.facts: Professor in the University of Bologne in 1560 and creator of its botanical garden.  Author of the first pharmacopee.  Numerous works on the natural history.

dorsa andrusov.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge on the bank of Mare Fecunditatis.

dorsa argand.general_1: located in the East of Montes Harbinger. Not very visible Wrinkle ridge oriented North-South.
dorsa argand.facts: Precursor of the global tectonic.  Works on the origin of Alps and the Himalaya.

dorsa barlow.general_1: Ramified and little raised wrinkle ridge situated to the North of Mare Tranquillitatis.

dorsa burnet.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge. On the North-East edge of Oceanus Procellarum.

dorsa cato.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge situated to the North of Mare Fecunditatis.
dorsa cato.facts: Governor of Sardinia in 98 av JC.  Author of a 'Treaty on the agriculture' and a history of Rome 'Origins'.

dorsa dana.general_1: Double wrinkle ridge beginning at Nunn and et located in the North-East of Mare Smythii arena.

dorsa ewing.general_1: Ramified and little marked wrinkle ridge situated to the South of Oceanus Procellarum and oriented South-East North-West.
dorsa ewing.facts: Professor in the University of Columbia. Precursor of the tectonic of plates.

dorsa geikie.general_1: Well marked wrinkle ridge situated to the center of Mare Fecunditatis and oriented North - South.
dorsa geikie.slopes: Ride by some craterlets in its South part.

dorsa harker.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge situated in rim of Mare Crisium.

dorsa lister.general_1: System of well marked wrinkle ridge with shape of circle arc situated in Mare Serenitatis. Continues Dorsa Smirnov.
dorsa lister.facts: Specialist of fossils.  Discoverer of the extinction of some species.

dorsa mawson.general_1: Large wrinkle ridge oriented South-West North-East.
dorsa mawson.slopes: Door Goclenius UA and AB to its South extremity and Langrenus FE and FF to its North extremity.

dorsa rubey.general_1: Ramified and little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North - South ending to the South in the arena of Letronne and supporting Letronne A in its middle.

dorsa smirnov.general_1: System of well marked wrinkle ridge oriented North-South. Most important of Mare Serenitatis.
dorsa smirnov.slopes: Situated to the East of Mare Serenitatis.  Wears the craterlet Very on its central part.

dorsa sorby.general_1: Not very high wrinkle ridge and parallel to Dorsum Buckland and Montes Haemus.

dorsa stille.general_1: System of little marked wrinkle ridge in Mare Imbrium to the North-East of Lambert.

dorsa tetyaev.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge situated in North-East rim of Mare Crisium.

dorsa whiston.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North South.

dorsum arduino.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North South.
dorsum arduino.facts: Precursor of the stratigraphy. Works on the exploitation of mines.

dorsum azara.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge situated to the center of Mare Serenitatis and supporting the crater Sarabhai.

dorsum bucher.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North South.

dorsum buckland.general_1: Well marked wrinkle ridge oriented South-East North-West and situated on the South bank of Mare Serenitatis similarly to Montes Haemus.

dorsum cayeux.general_1: Wrinkle ridge pretty marked situated to the North of Mare Fecunditatis. Carry the craterlet Taruntius P and is continued by Dorsum Geikie to the South.
dorsum cayeux.facts: Works on the petrography of sedimentary rocks.  Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1928.

dorsum cloos.general_1: Not very high and large wrinkle ridge located in the North-East of Mare Smythii arena.

dorsum cushman.general_1: Situated to the North of Mare Fecunditatis. Little raised.

dorsum gast.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North South and situated on the bank of Mare Serenitatis.
dorsum gast.slopes: Wears the craterlet Aratus D and a smaller second on its median part.

dorsum grabau.general_1: Pretty marked wrinkle ridge oriented West East.

dorsum guettard.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge situated on the West slope of Bonpland.
dorsum guettard.facts: Author of the volcanic origin of Mounts of Auvergne. Discovery of the Kaolin in 1765. Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1743.

dorsum heim.general_1: Well marked and long wrinkle ridge in arc of circle and oriented South-East North-West. Wears the crater C. Herschel.
dorsum heim.facts: Discoverer of the mechanism of rock fold.  Numerous works on Alps.

dorsum higazy.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented South-West North-East situated in Mare Imbrium to the North-East of Timocharis.
dorsum higazy.slopes: An isolated mountain to the East of its South extremity.

dorsum nicol.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North  South situated to the South of Mare Serenitatis and connecting Dorsa Lister to Rimae Plinius.
dorsum nicol.facts: Inventor of the prism polariseur with spath of Iceland in 1828.

dorsum niggli.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge and perpendicular to Montes Agricola.

dorsum oppel.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge in form of arc of circle. Fringes the West wall of Mare Crisium.

dorsum owen.general_1: Well marked wrinkle ridge oriented North South and situated in Mare Serenitatis to the North of the crater Krishna.

dorsum scilla.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North South.

dorsum termier.general_1: Little marked wrinkle ridge situated to the center of Mare Crisium.
dorsum termier.facts: Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1909.  Director of the Service of the geological map of France in 1911.  Many author works of popularization.

dorsum thera.general_1: Not very high wrinkle ridge becoming the Shallow Hurwitz Rainure 111 Totale rille

dorsum von cotta.general_1: Long and little marked wrinkle ridge oriented North South and situated in Mare Serenitatis.
dorsum von cotta.slopes: Rejoins then lodge similarly Dorsum Buckland in its South part.

dorsum zirkel.general_1: Well marked wrinkle ridge oriented South-East North-West and situated in Mare Imbrium to the North-West of Lambert.
dorsum zirkel.slopes: Slopes bearing the craterlets Lambert A and B to the South.

doublet.general_1: Small double craterlet named by Apollo 14 astronauts.

dove.slopes: Slightly steep slopes crushed by Dove C to the South-West and by the craterlets to the South-East and to the North-East.
dove.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor with line of crest.
dove.facts: Specialist of electricity and the meteorology.

draper.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated to the extremity of a wrinkle ridge connecting it to Pytheas. Forms a couple with  Draper C.
draper.facts: Precursor of the astrophotography and the spectroscopy. Author of the 'Henry Draper Catalogue' containing 240 000 stellar spectra.  Inventor of the basis of the stellar classification.

drebbel.general_1: isolated Formation of with lengthened shape.
drebbel.general_2: Partly covered by Orientale ejecta possibly Lower Imbrian
drebbel.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing some craterlets to the South.
drebbel.floor: Lenghtened flat floor filled with lava.
drebbel.facts: Pioneer of the realization of the first microscopes.  Constructor of one of the first submarines in 1624.

dreyer.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
dreyer.facts: Author of New General Catalogue of nebulae and clusters of stars in 1888 and of the two Index Catalogues in 1895 and 1908.

drude.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
drude.facts: Author of electronic structures of matals theory in 1902.

dryden.facts: Director of National Bureau of Standards in 1946. Surveys about turbulences. Conceiver of the first military autoguided rocket in 1944. Director in Nasa in 1958.

drygalski.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations. Part of
drygalski.walls: Apparently damaged high walls to the West and supporting a crater to the South-East.
drygalski.floor: Partially unknown floor. Central mountain doubles. Hills and craterlets. South North oriented rilles.

dubyago.general_1: Circular formation to the South-East of Mare Undarum.
dubyago.slopes: Fairly steep slopes especially to the South-East and bearing Dubiago L    to the West Dubiago Z to the South-East and Dubiago B and J to the South.
dubyago.walls: Fairly high walls more high to the East that to the West.
dubyago.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava.

dufay.facts: First director of Haute Provence Observatory. Surveys on stellar spectrophotometry sun corona comets and interstellar medium..

dugan.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

dune.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 15 landing site.

dunthorne.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape

dyson.facts: Director of Greenwich Observatory in 1910. Surveys about proper movement of stars and Milky Way structure. Verification of relativity theory during a solar eclipse.

dziewulski.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
dziewulski.general_2: Older than Crisium Basin possibly pre-Nectarian

earthlight.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 15 astronauts.

easley.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
easley.facts: Centaur rockets specialist. Fortran programer. 4th afro-american woman working in NASA.

eckert.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated to the South extremity of a wrinkle ridge of Mare Crisium.

eddington.slopes: Steep slopes to the North and crushed by Struve to the North-West.
eddington.walls: High Walls to the North and gobbled to the South in Oceanus Procellarum.
eddington.floor: Very extensive flat floor filled with lava containing the crater Eddington P.
eddington.facts: Director of the observatory of Cambridge.  Theory of the internal star composition.  Works in cosmology. Studies on the action of the gravitation on the light during the solar eclipse of 1919.

edison.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
edison.facts: Author of more than a thousand patents. Conceiver of duplex telegraph phonograph movie projector... Discoverer of diod principle.

edith.general_1: Possible concentric crater crushing the slope of an anonymous damaged crater.
edith.slopes: Slightly steep Slopes collapsed in the East.
edith.walls: Slightly steep walls and almost flat in the East.
edith.floor: Floor showing an annular low structure.

egede.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava. Craterlets.
egede.facts: Lutherian parson living with people of Greenland.

ehrlich.facts: Surveys on the anticorps. Discoverer of a syphilis treatment with Hata. Nobel laureate in 1908.

eichstadt.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the slope East of Montes Cordillera.
eichstadt.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a crater to the North-West and a crater to the South.
eichstadt.floor: Extensive flat floor supporting a crater to the South. Craterlets.

eijkman.facts: Works on beriberi . Discoverer of some vitamins. Nobel laureate in 1929.

eimmart.general_1: Formation deformed to the South and situated on the North-East slope of Mare Crisium.
eimmart.slopes: Fairly steep slopes especially to the South-West and bearing a craterlet to the South-East.
eimmart.walls: High walls ride by a craterlet to the North-East.
eimmart.facts: Author of a map of the Moon.

einstein.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Damaged formation.
einstein.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Dalton to the East Moseley to the North-West and Vasco of Gama & Bohr to the South-East.
einstein.floor: Flat floor with craterlets. Central crater Einstein Has 45 km.
einstein.facts: Inventor of the concept of photon.  Theory of the brownian movement. Theory of the restrict relativity in 1905 and general relativity in 1916. Mass / energy equivalence.  Nobel Price of physics in 1921.

einthoven.facts: Professor in Leyde University in 1886. Conceiver of electrocardiography. Nobel laureate in 1924.

elbow.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 15 landing site.

elger.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the South bank of Palus Epidemiarum.
elger.slopes: Complex steep slopes to the North.
elger.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a craterlet to the West.
elger.facts: Selenographer.  Author of a map of the Moon in 1895.

ellison.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

elmer.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

elvey.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

emory.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

encke.general_1: Isolated hexagonal formation situated to the South extremity of a field of hills.
encke.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Encke H to the South-West.
encke.walls: Slightly high walls supporting the craterlet Encke N to the East.
encke.floor: Tormented floor. Hills and lines of crest. White stains around a craterlet.
encke.facts: Director of the Royal Observatory of Berlin.  Specialist of comets. Calculation of the orbit of the comet that wears its name.  Determination of the solar parallaxe in 1824.

end.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 16 astronauts.

endymion.general_2: Younger than Humboldtianum Basin. mare fill
endymion.slopes: Very steep slopes bearing Endymion J to the West and Endymion A to the North-East.
endymion.walls: Very high walls especially to the South-East.
endymion.floor: Very large flat floor filled with somber lava. Small lines of crests.

eotvos.general_1: Big damaged crater with numerous craterlets in the South-East of Tsiolkovskiy.
eotvos.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing numerous craterlets and a short chain in the South-East.
eotvos.floor: Flat floor wearing numérous formation whose wrinkles craterlets and ghost craters.

epigenes.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Epigenes P to the South and ruins of crater to the East.
epigenes.walls: Fairly high walls more massive to the East.
epigenes.floor: Flat and tormented floor. Small mountain off center.

epimenides.general_1: Rectangular formation oriented North South situated on the South bank of Lacus Timoris.
epimenides.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Epimenides S to the South-East.
epimenides.facts: Author of many spurious works.  Founder of the orphism.

eratosthenes.general_1: Circular formation situated to the South extremity of Montes Apenninus.
eratosthenes.slopes: Very steep slopes and rugged especially to the South.
eratosthenes.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor. Central mountain with several summits. Wrinkle ridges hills and rilles.
eratosthenes.facts: Numerous works in philosophy and grammar.  Tutor of the son of Ptolemee 3.  Director of the library of Alexandria.  First measures of the circumference of the Earth thanks to shades carried by the Sun.

erro.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

esclangon.facts: Numerous works in mathematical physics and astronomy. Discoverer of the origin of the bang supersonic.  Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1929.  Constructor of

esnault-pelterie.facts: Conceiver of the and of several thermical engines for airplanes. Founder of the International Bourget Airshow. Numerous surveys about spatial propulsion.

euclides.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape and with bright ejecta situated to the West of Montes Riphaeus.
euclides.slopes: Steep slopes bearing a small mountain to the East.
euclides.facts: Organizer of school of mathematics in Alexandrie. Author of a treaty of geometry 'Elements' in 13 books containing many postulates. Authors of many other lost works.

euctemon.slopes: Steep slopes especially to the South.
euctemon.walls: High walls ridden by a craterlet to the West.
euctemon.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. A craterlet in the arena.
euctemon.facts: Athenian friend of Méton associated to the discovery of the Moon / Sun cycle.

eudoxus.general_1: Forms a remarkable couple with Aristoteles. Circular formation.
eudoxus.slopes: Very steep and rugged slopes bearing Eudoxus B to the North and Eudoxus G and A to the North-East.
eudoxus.floor: Tormented floor. Central mountains and hills.
eudoxus.facts: Inventor of the year of 365 days 1 / 4.  Author of the hypothesis of homocentric spheres. Author of a theory of proportions and the method of the exhaustions in mathematics.

euler.general_2: Lies on the Mare Imbrium basalts (or under)
euler.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor. Central mountain.
euler.facts: Author of 900 works on many areas whose mathematics and astronomy.  Author of a 'Complete mechanics treaty' in 1736 and a work 'On the theory of the Moon'.

evdokimov.general_2: Older than Hertzsprung Basin shown as Evdokimov G on LAC 34

fabbroni.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape crushing the extremity East of Mons Argaeus.
fabbroni.slopes: Fairly steep slopes especially to the North.
fabbroni.facts: Supervisor of the construction of the road of the Mount Genevre.

fabricius.general_1: Circular formation forming a South-West oriented and interesting trio with Metius and Rheita.
fabricius.slopes: Steep slopes crushing Janssen to the South-West and bearing Metius to the North-East Metius A to the North and Fabricius A and B to the South-East.
fabricius.floor: Flat floor. Two rectilinear and parallel mountain chains.
fabricius.facts: Discoverer of the variability of the star Mira Ceti.  First observer of spots of the Sun in 1610.

fabry.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
fabry.facts: Director of Optics Institute of Paris and member of french Academy of Sciences in 1921. Conceiver with Perrot and Buisson of an interferometer. Discoverer of the ozona layer. First verification of Doppler-Fizeau effect.

fahrenheit.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
fahrenheit.facts: Has left its name to a scale of measure of temperature.

fairouz.general_1: Elongated crater on the bank of Lacus Solitudinis.
fairouz.slopes: Slightly steep Slopes collapsed in the South-East.

falcon.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 17 astronauts. Possible volcanic cinder cone.

faraday.general_1: Damaged formation that crushes the East wall of St?fler.
faraday.slopes: Steep slopes bearing a complex of craters to the South.
faraday.walls: High walls crushed by Faraday A to the North-East Faraday C to the South and St?fler P to the South-West.
faraday.floor: Flat floor to the North-West and tormented to the South-East with a crater. Craterlets.
faraday.facts: Author of the first liquefaction of gas.  Discoverer of the magnetic induction in 1831. Theory of the electrolysis in 1833.  Works on the electrostatic and the electroluminescence.

faustini.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

fauth.general_1: South North lengthened formation constituted by Fauth and Fauth A two adjacent craters and situated on the South slope of Copernicus. Nicknamed 'Hole of lock'.
fauth.slopes: Steep slopes especially to the North and bearing Fauth A to the South.
fauth.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor communicating with that Fault A.
fauth.facts: Selenographer. Author of maps of the Moon.

faye.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Donati to the North-East Delaunay to the South-West and a craterlet to the West.
faye.floor: Flat floor. Central mountain of 2370 m. Craterlets.
faye.facts: Author of a theory of the Solar System.  Opponent to Laplace.  Discoverer of a periodic comet in 1843.

fechner.facts: Conceiver of a philosophical concept in which the individual spirit is part of the God spirit.

fedorov.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape and lengthened North South.
fedorov.facts: Specialist of rockets and the astronautics.

felix.general_1: Small craterlet located on the North of a small catena including Artemis and Verne on the South of Mons Lahire.

fermat.slopes: Steep slopes crushed by double craterlet Fermat A in the North and by craterlets in the South-West and South-East.
fermat.walls: Walles higher in the East than West and straddled in the East by 3 craterlets.
fermat.floor: Flat floor with mounds in the West.
fermat.facts: Founder of the analytic geometry.  Inventor with Blaise Pascal of the calculation of probabilities.  Precursor of the entire and differential calculation.  Author of a famous theorem non demonstrated.

fermi.facts: Numerous surveys in physics and atomic particles. Discoverer of neutron properties. Director for the first atomic pile in Chicago. Nobel laureate in 1938.

fernelius.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the north slope of St?fler.
fernelius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes overlapped by St?fler to the South Fernelius A to the West and Kaiser to the North-East.
fernelius.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a couple of craterlets to the East.
fernelius.floor: Very flat floor filled of lava.
fernelius.facts: Attempt of measure of the terrestrial meridian.  Physician of Henri II.

fersman.general_2: Younger than Hertzsprung Basin. partly covered by Orientale ejecta
fersman.facts: Author of a remarquable treaty about geochemistry. Author of an inventory of mineral ressouces of USSR. Director of Lomonossov Institute.

feuillee.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape forming a remarkable couple with Beer and situated on a small wrinkle ridge of Mare Imbrium.
feuillee.facts: Director of the observatory of Marseilles.

fibiger.general_1: Eroded crater located on the North-East of Byrd.
fibiger.slopes: Steep slopes Damaged in the South by craters and landslides. Sharp crest.
fibiger.walls: Steep walls collapsed in the South..
fibiger.floor: Flat floor riddled with all sizes craterlets.

firmicus.general_1: Circular formation situated between Mare Crisium and Mare Undarum.
firmicus.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Lacus Perseverantiae to the West and Firmicus G and F to the South-West
firmicus.walls: Fairly high walls and ridden to the North by a craterlet.
firmicus.floor: Very flat floor filled of somber lava.
firmicus.facts: Author of a work on the astrology and a work on profane religions in 346.

fischer.facts: Numerous surveys in organic chemistry. Synthesis of glucose and fructose. Nobel laureate in 1902.

fitzgerald.facts: Author of electromagnetic waves theory. Interpretation of Michelson experience. Measurement of electron mass in 1897.

fizeau.facts: First sun photography with Foucault in 1845. First measurememt of light speed in 1849. Co-discoverer with Doppler of wavelengthe shift with speed in 1848. President of the french Academy of Sciences in 1878.

flag.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 16 astronauts.

flammarion.slopes: Steep slopes to the South but non-existent to the North bearing Herschel C to the South and Sp?rer to the South-East.
flammarion.walls: Wall gobbled to the North by the lava of Sinus Medii raised to the South and ridden by M?sting Has to the West.
flammarion.floor: Flat and extensive floor. Closed by Rima Flammarion to the North. Craterlets.
flammarion.facts: Talented popularizator.  Author of  'The Popular Astronomy' in 1879. Creator of an observatory in Juvisy in 1883 and of the Société Astronomique de France in 1887.  Works in occult sciences  meteorology and climatology

haworth.floor: Narrow flat floor riddled with craters and craterlets.

hayn.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations. Circular formation.

head.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 12 astronauts.

heaviside.facts: Surveys on electricity and magnetism. Author of the hypothesis of the existence of an atmospheric ionised layer.

hecataeus.general_1: Circular formation situated to the limit of the zone of librations on the North slope of Humboldt.
hecataeus.slopes: Steep slopes overlapped by a large crater to the South-West.
hecataeus.walls: Fairly high walls supporting two craterlets to the East.
hecataeus.floor: Flat floor but tormented to the South-West.
hecataeus.facts: Author of a work on its trip in Perse.  Realized one of the first maps of the Earth.  Author of the 'Genealogies'.

hedervari.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

hedin.general_1: Little marked and wrecked formation situated to the limit of the zone of librations.
hedin.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing many craters to the East and Riccioli H to the South
hedin.walls: Slightly high walls almost flat to the North.
hedin.floor: Tormented and very large flat Floor to the East. Lines of oriented parallel crest South-East North-West.
hedin.facts: Exploration of Asia central. Discoverer of sources of the Indus.

hegu.general_1: Isolated formation with a bowl shape.
hegu.facts: Constellation on an old chinese sky map containing  Altaïr and also named Niulang as the cowboy who married  Zhinyu in chinise legends.

heinrich.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
heinrich.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing two craterlets to the North.

heinsius.general_1: South-East North-West lengthened and damaged formation .
heinsius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes rugged to the South-East with craterlets and bearing Heinsius B to the South-West and Heinsius C to the South.
heinsius.floor: Flat floor supporting the crater Heinsius A to the South. Hills and craterlets whose two important to the South-East.

heis.walls: Slightly high walls supporting Heis A to the North.

helicon.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a remarkable couple with Le Verrier.
helicon.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing the craterlet Helicon E to the West.
helicon.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a craterlet to the South-West.
helicon.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Small central relief.
helicon.facts: Disciple of Platon and Eudoxe.  Prediction of an eclipse of Sun.

hell.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the South-West wall of Deslandres.
hell.slopes: Fairly steep slopes rugged to the North-East and bearing a couple of craterlets to the South-West.
hell.floor: Tormented floor. Important mountain off center.
hell.facts: Founder of the first observatory of Comes.  Observer of the passage of Venus ahead the solar disc of 1769.

helmert.general_1: Dark floor crater partly covering Kao and located in the South of Mare Smythii.
helmert.walls: Slightly steep walls buried in the North and steeper in the South.
helmert.floor: Dark flat floor filled with lava mounds wrinkles and craterlets.

helmholtz.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Neumayer to the South and Boussingault to the South-West.
helmholtz.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by a craterlet to the North-East.
helmholtz.floor: Flat floor with craterlets whose a double to the South-East. Small double relief.
helmholtz.facts: Numerous works in acoustics optical electricity and physiology. Measure of the speed of the nervous impulse in 1850.

henderson.facts: Author of 60 000 mesurements of planets. Mesure de la parallaxe et de la distane d'Apha Centauri en 1839.

hendrix.general_1: Recent deep crater stuated on the South of White.
hendrix.slopes: Steep slopes with sharp crest bearing a crater overlaapped by ejectas in the South-East.
hendrix.walls: Steep walls with terraces in the North.

henry.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting couple with Henry Brothers.
henry.general_2: Formerly Paul Henry. partly covered by Imbrian ejecta
henry.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Henry Brothers to the West.
henry.walls: Slightly high walls ridden to the South by a craterlet.
henry.floor: Extensive flat floor with line of crest to the West.
henry.facts: Works on the electromagnetism.  Discovery of the induction and the extracourant in 1832.  Inventor of the electrical relay and the electrical engine.

henry freres.general_1: Circular formation making a couple with Henry.
henry freres.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Henry Freres C in the South-West and Henry Freres B in the West.

henson.general_1: Deep circular formation between Sverdrup and De Gerlache.
henson.facts: Afro-american polar explorer with Robert Peary and reaching first the North Pole on april 6th 1909.

henyey.general_1: Destroyed formation on the North-West slope of Planck

heraclitus.general_1: Circular formation forming a remarkable quartet with Licetus Heraclitus D and an other crater to the West.
heraclitus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed by Licetus to the North Cuvier to the East and Heraclitus D to the South.
heraclitus.walls: Fairly high walls riddled of craterlets.
heraclitus.floor: Tormented floor riddled with craterlets and separated in two by a central crest line.
heraclitus.facts: Author of a treaty 'Of the Nature'.  Considered the fire as essential element.

hercules.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a remarkable couple with Atlas.
hercules.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Hercules D to the South-East.
hercules.walls: High walls with terraces supporting Hercules E to the South-West.
hercules.floor: Flat floor containing Hercules crater G. Three hills. Stain sinks in the enclosure.
hercules.facts: Heracles for Greeks.  Son of Jupiter. Author of twelve remarkable works.

herigonius.general_1: Isolated circular formation overlapping Dorsa Ewing to the East and supporting a craterlet to the North.
herigonius.facts: Author of a theory on the movement of planets.

hermann.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated in the West part of Oceanus Procellarum to the South extremity of a small wrinkle ridge.
hermann.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing the craterlet Hermann B to the North.
hermann.facts: Calculation of the number Pi with new series and sketch of a classification of the quadriques.

hermite.general_1: Situated in the zone of librations near the North pole.  Circular formation.
hermite.slopes: Steep slopes bearing many craters whose Lovelace and Sylvester to the South.
hermite.walls: Fairly high walls supporting a crater to the South.
hermite.facts: Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1856.  General theory of elliptic functions and abeliens.  Memory on the exponential function in 1873.

herodotus.slopes: Steep slopes to the South and to the East.
herodotus.walls: Slightly high walls supporting the craterlet Herodotus N to the North.
herodotus.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava. Starting point of Vallis Schr?ter to the North.
herodotus.facts: Large traveler. Lived in Athens.  Author of the 'Histories' in 9 volumes.

heron.facts: Works on mechanics dioptric optics and surfaces measurements.

herschel.general_1: Young circular formation situated on the North slope of Ptolemaeus.
herschel.slopes: Steep slopes overlapped to the South by Herschel G.
herschel.floor: Tormented floor with mountain off center. Craterlets.
herschel.facts: Constructor of a telescope of 1.2 m.  Discoverer of Uranus on march 13th 1781 Titania and Oberon in 1787 and Encelade and Midas in 1789.  Author of a catalogue of 2500 celestial objects.  Studies of double stars and the infrared.

hertz.facts: Helmholtz pupil. Professor in Bonn University on 1889. First electromagnetic waves production on 1887. Travaux on induction and photoelectrical effect.

hertzsprung.facts: Director of Leyde observatory from 1935 to 1944. Author of a theory about stars clssification according to their spectral class on 1905 as Russell.

hesiodus.general_1: Wrecked circular formation situated on the West slope of Pitatus.
hesiodus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Hesiodus A to the South-West.
hesiodus.walls: Slightly high walls riddled with anonymous craterlets and collapsed to the North.
hesiodus.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Several craterlets whose Hesiodus D to the center. Communicating with the floor of Pitatus by a collar in the wall.
hesiodus.facts: Poems on agricultural works.  Author of an origin of the World and a genealogy of Gods in the 'Theogony'.

hess.facts: Discoverer of cosmic rays in 1912. Nobel laureate in 1936.

hess apollo.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 17 astronauts.

hevelius.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a remarkable couple with Cavalerius.
hevelius.general_2: Faulted. Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta
hevelius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Cavalerius to the North Lohrmann to the South and many craterlets to the East and to the West.
hevelius.walls: Slightly high walls supporting Hevelius H F & B to the West and Hevelius C G & E to the North-East.
hevelius.floor: Very large flat floor supporting Hevelius A to the North. Small central mountain. Contains Rimae Hevelius.
hevelius.facts: Determination of the rotation of the Sun by observation of spots in 1645.  Discoverer of the solar facules. Author of the first detailed map of the Moon in 1647 (6 preserved names).

hevesy.general_1: Very damaged crater touching Rozhdestvenskiy U.
hevesy.slopes: Slightly steep slopes riddled with craters and craterlets whose a big in the South-East.
hevesy.walls: Steep walls in the East and disappeared in the West and bearing a big craterlet in the South-West.
hevesy.floor: Rough floor bearing five big craterlets and numerous small ones.

heymans.general_2: Probably Nectarian should be shown on Plate 7B not 8B

heyrovsky.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

hilbert.facts: Works on algebrics. Inventor of axiomatic method.

hildegard.general_1: Damaged formation on the North-West slope of Planck.
hildegard.general_2: Eroded slope on the East and South
hildegard.slopes: Walls higher on North and bearing craters Pikel'ner K et G.
hildegard.walls: Flat floor supporting two ghost craters and numerous craterlets.
hildegard.floor: Flat floor bearing two ghost craters and numerous craterlets.
hildegard.facts: Mystic and visionnary monkess. Considered as the founder of scientific method in natural science. Canonized and named Church doctor on 2012 by Benoit XVI pope. Author of Riesencodex.

hill.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape.  Forms an interesting couple with Carmichael.
hill.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a lengthened crater to the North-West.
hill.facts: Calculator to the Nautical Almanac.  Works on movements of the Moon and planets.

hind.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-East slope of Hipparchus and forming an interesting aligned trio with Hipparchus C and Hipparchus L.
hind.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Hind C to the South and Hipparchus C to the North-East.
hind.walls: Very high walls ridden by a craterlet to the North.
hind.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor. Hills and craterlets.
hind.facts: Discoverer of 10 asteroids between 1847 and 1854. Calculation of the orbit of more of 70 comets and asteroids.  Director of the 'Nautical Almanac' in 1853.

hinshelwood.general_1: Crater on the East slope of Peary and not lighted by Sun.
hinshelwood.slopes: Steep slopes bearing a double craterlet in the North.
hinshelwood.floor: Flat floor riddled with craterlets whose two in the North-East.

hippalus.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the East bank of Mare Humorum.
hippalus.slopes: Non-existent slopes to the West enough steep to the East and bearing Rimae Hippalus to the East.
hippalus.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the South-West by the lava of Mare Humorum.
hippalus.floor: Floor crossed by a groove of Rimae Hippalus flat to the West and tormented to the East. Craterlets whose Hippalus B. Hills.

hipparchus.general_1: Deformed and wrecked formation. Place of the landing of Tintin on the Moon imagined by Herge'.
hipparchus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing many craters whose Pickering to the North-East Halley to the South and Hind to the South-East.
hipparchus.walls: Slightly high walls ridden to the North by Horrocks and to the East by Hipparchus G.
hipparchus.floor: Very large flat floor containing Hipparchus N and the ghost crater Hipparchus X. Two parallel rilles. Hills and craterlets.
hipparchus.facts: Promoter of the division of the circle in 360„ø.  Creator of tables of the position of the Sun.  Discoverer of the precession of equinoxes.  Author of the first celestial catalogue containing more than 1000 stars.

hirayama.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

hohmann.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
hohmann.facts: Discoverer of the elliptical and economical transfert orbit between two celestial bodies.

holden.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Holden T to the East and Holden E to the North-West.
holden.walls: High walls with terraces overlapped by a craterlet to the North-West.
holden.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting a large craterlet. Line of crest.
holden.facts: First director of the Observatory of Lick from 1888 to 1898. Founder of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific.  Author of a photographic atlas of the Moon.

hommel.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Hommel H to the North Hommel P to the South-West and Hommel B Q and S to the South-East.
hommel.walls: Wall crushed by many craters whose Hommel A to the North-East Hommel C to the West and Hommel D to the South.
hommel.floor: Tormented floor. Hills and lines of crest.

hooke.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the North and Hooke D to the South-East.
hooke.facts: Laws on the elastic body deformation.  Works on solar spots  Jupiter Saturn and comets.  Discoverer of living cells."

horatio.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 17 astronauts on the slope of Camelot.

hornsby.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on the East slope of Dorsum von Cotta.

horrebow.general_1: Situated on the wall of J. Herschel. Overlaps the crater Horrebow A.
horrebow.walls: Fairly high walls with light terraces.
horrebow.facts: Author of a method of determination of the latitude.

horrocks.general_1: Circular formation situated on the floor of Hipparchus.
horrocks.floor: Slightly extensive and tormented floor and tormented. Central mountain. Hills.
horrocks.facts: First observation of a passage of Venus ahead the Sun in 1639. Application of theories of Kepler to the movement of the Moon.

hortensius.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
hortensius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the South and a field of domes to the North.

houssay.general_1: Elongated crater in a group of five joined in a complex shape.
houssay.slopes: Fairly steep slopes in the North-East and South-West part and collapsed in the North-West.
houssay.floor: Floor filled with an elongated mound oriented South-East North-West.

houtermans.general_1: West East lengthened Formation situated in the zone of librations.
houtermans.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Kraiken to the North-West.
houtermans.walls: Slightly high walls with debris to the East.
houtermans.floor: Flat floor with craterlet to the North.

hubble.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
hubble.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Craterlets.
hubble.facts: Discovery of obviousness of stars in galaxies in 1923.  Author of the law on the recession of galaxies in 1929.

huggins.general_1: Circular formation forming a remarkable trio with Nasireddin and Miller.
huggins.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Orontius to the West and Saussure to the South-West.
huggins.walls: High walls crushed by Nasireddin to the East.
huggins.floor: Flat floor to the West and tormented to the East supporting Huggins A to the North-West. Central mountain. Craterlets.
huggins.facts: Pioneer of the spectroscopy.  Measured the speed of Sirius in 1868.  Published a stellar spectra atlas in 1899.

humason.facts: Specialist of the astrophotography and the spectroscopy. Collaborator of Hubble to part of 1928.

humboldt.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
humboldt.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Phillips to the West and Barnard to the South-East.
humboldt.floor: Very large flat floor. Internal mountain chain. Stains sunk on the periphery. Radial grooves. Craterlets. Rilles.
humboldt.facts: Brother of Alexander von Humboldt the explorer.  Founder of the University of Berlin in 1809.  Studies of linguistics.

hume.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
hume.slopes: Slightly steep slopes non existent to the North.
hume.floor: Flat floor with a group of hills in the North-East.

husband.general_1: Crater on the South slope of Borman and covered by its ejecta.
husband.slopes: Slightly steep slopes pierced by a small crater in the North-West.
husband.walls: Slightly steep walls with a lanslide in the North.
husband.floor: Flat floor with some big craterlets.

hutton.facts: Author of an Earth theory on 1785. Discoverer of the volcanic origin of some rocks.

huxley.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
huxley.facts: Defender of theories of Darwin.  Author of the 'Place of the Man in the nature' in 1891 describing the descendance of the Man from monkeys.

hyginus.general_1: Circular formation situated on Rima Hyginus. Transient lunar phenomena (smokes according to Sacco).
hyginus.walls: Slightly high walls damaged by a craterlet to the North.

hypatia.general_1: Wrecked formation of lengthened form South-East North-West. Seems formed by the melting of several craters.
hypatia.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Hypatia A to the South-West Hypatia D and DA to the North and the ghost crater Hypatia M to the South-East.
hypatia.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Crests and rille line.
hypatia.facts: Girl of Theon of Alexandrie.  Co-author of works of her father. Author of a comment on the 'Arithmetics'of Diophante and on the 'Conical' of Apollonios.

ian.general_1: Craterlet located in a graben of the Palus Putredinis rilles network.

ibn battuta.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated to the South extremity of Dorsa Geikie.
ibn battuta.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing several ghost craters to the South and to the West.

ibn yunus.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the North-West slope of Cyrillus.
ibn yunus.slopes: Slopes steeper to the East and bearing Cyrillus C to the South.
ibn yunus.walls: Slightly high walls destroyed to the South by Cyrillus C.
ibn yunus.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Craterlets.
ibn yunus.facts: Cadi of Sevilla and Great Cadi of Cordoue.  Numerous works in medicine right and philosophy.  Partisan of Aristote and Galien.

ibn-rushd.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
ibn-rushd.slopes: Slopes steeper in the East and bearing Cyrillus C in the South.
ibn-rushd.walls: Slightly high walls damged in the South by Cyrillus C.
ibn-rushd.floor: Flat floor filled with lava and craterlets.
ibn-rushd.facts: Abu al Wafa pupil. Works on Sun Moon and stars motion. Author of Hakimites astronomical tables on 1007.

idel'son.slopes: Steep slopes bearing the craterlets to the South Ideler L to the East and Ideler R to the West.

igor.general_1: Geological formation on the Luna 17 landing site and visited by Lunokhod 1.

il'in.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

ina.general_1: Recent volcanic origin formation located on the summit of a large and very flat volcanic dome.
ina.floor: Rough floor presenting more than 80 flat mounds and numerous craterlets eround the mounds.

index.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 15 astronauts.

ingalls.facts: Amateur astronomer. Author of a famous amateur instruments making book.

inghirami.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta from Orientale
inghirami.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Vallis Inghirami to the North-West and Inghirami Q to the South-West.
inghirami.floor: Very tormented floor. Central mountainous mountain. Craterlets. Parallel crest lines.

ioffe.general_2: Possibly Nectarian. Erroneously labeled Friedmann on Plate 9B. misspelled "Loffe" on LAC 89
ioffe.facts: Surveys on photoelectrical effect cristals and dielectrics.

isabel.general_1: Irregularly shaped craterlet included in a short catena on the North slope of Diophantus.

isidorus.general_1: Damaged circular formation forming an interesting couple with Capella.
isidorus.slopes: Steep slopes crushed to the East by Capella.
isidorus.walls: Fairly high walls with terraces deformed by Capella to the North-East.
isidorus.floor: Extensive flat floor supporting Isidorus Has to the West and a craterlet in iron to horse to the South. Wrinkle ridges and craterlets.
isidorus.facts: Archibishop of Sevilla in 601.  President of the council of Toledo in 633.  Author of the 'Etymologiae'. Organizer of the Spanish Church. Amateur astronomer.

j. herschel.walls: Slightly high walls partly dismantled and ridden by Horrebow and Horrebow A to the South.
j. herschel.floor: Very large flat floor. Line of crest crack hills and craterlets whose Herschel C to the center.

jaci.general_1: Tiny craterlet in a range on a ridge of Mons Mouton.
jaci.facts: First name of the Tupi ethnic group of Brazil

jackson.facts: Modern neurology founder. Surveys on neuronal deseases.

jacobi.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Jacobi F C E and G to the South.
jacobi.walls: Fairly high walls ridden by a crater to the North.
jacobi.floor: Flat floor supporting a chain of craterlets transverse.
jacobi.facts: Elliptic functions and calculation of variations specialist. Resolution of equation systems to n stranges. Works in mechanical celestial.

jansen.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing to the South-East a line of important crest oriented South-East North-West.
jansen.walls: Slightly high walls almost gobbled to the South.
jansen.floor: Floor filled by the lava supporting the craterlet Jansen LA to the South.
jansen.facts: Presumed manufacturer of the first refractor telescope.

jansky.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
jansky.walls: High walls in damaged terraces to the South.
jansky.facts: Discoverer of the radioelectric emision of the Milky Way in 1931. Founder of the radioastronomy.

janssen.slopes: Slightly marked slopes crushed by Fabricius to the North and riddled of craters whose Lockyer to the West Janssen F R E and D to the South-West Janssen B J M and X to the North West.
janssen.floor: Very tormented floor with the trio Janssen H K & L to the East. Hills and craterlets. Contains Rimae Janssen.
janssen.facts: Specialist of the Sun. Discovers the helium in 1868 as Lockyer. Founder of the Observatory of Meudon near Paris in 1876 and of an observatory on the White Mount summit in the Alps in 1890.

jeans.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
jeans.facts: Co author of a law about thermical rays with lord Rayleigh on 1900. Author of another solar system formation theory.Professor at Cambridge University on 1912.

jenkins.general_1: Circular formation. Forms an East West oriented trio with Schubert X and Nobili.
jenkins.general_2: Formerly Schubert Z. younger than Crisium Basin
jenkins.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a crater to the South-East and crushed by Schubert X to the West.
jenkins.walls: Fairly high walls supporting a craterlet to the West.

jenner.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

jerik.general_1: Circular formation associated to Catena Brigitte situé between Dawes and Mons Argaeus.

joliot.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
joliot.facts: Works on positon. Discoveries of numerous isotopes. Nobel laureate with his wife IrŠne on 1935. Professor in CollŠge de France on 1937. Building of the first french atomic pile. President of World Peace Council on 1954.

jomo.general_1: Crater-pit located on the South-East end of Rima Hadley beyond Bela.

jose.general_1: Crater-pit located on a branch of Rimae Alphonsus.

joule.facts: Discoverer of the thermical effect produced by electricity on 1841. Determination of the calory mechanical equivalent on 1842. Numerous works on thermodynamics.

joy.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

jules verne.facts: Engineer Author of numerous adventures and science-fiction books as From the Earth to the Moon and Around the Moon.

julienne.general_1: Double craterlet located on the North bucckle of Rima Hadley.

julius caesar.general_1: Wrecked formation of South-East North-West oriented rectangular shape.
julius caesar.slopes: Steep slopes to the South-West and collapsed to the North-East.
julius caesar.walls: High walls to the South-West and damaged to the North-East.
julius caesar.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava. Hills. Wrinkle ridges and craterlets.
julius caesar.facts: General and Emperor of Rome. Realized many warlike expeditions from North of Europ to Minor Asia. Reformed the calendar and roman institutions.

kaiser.general_1: Circular formation situated on the North-East slope of Fernelius.
kaiser.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Fernelius to the South-West and Kaiser A to the East.
kaiser.walls: Fairly high walls supporting a craterlet to the West.
kaiser.floor: Very flat floor filled of lava. Craterlets.
kaiser.facts: Specialist of double stars and Mars.

kamerlingh onnes.facts: Conceiver of the Leyde University Cold Laboratory. Helium liqu‚faction on 1908. Discoverer of supreconductivity. Nobel laureate on 1913.

kane.slopes: Steep slopes to the North and to the East.
kane.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the South by the lava of Mare Frigoris.
kane.floor: Fairly flat floor filled with lava. Craterlets.
kane.facts: Specialist of the North Pole and Greenland.

kant.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Kant E to the East Kant M and N to the North Kant DA to the South-West and Kant S and T to the South.
kant.floor: Slightly extensive and flat floor supporting an important central mountain.
kant.facts: Author of an important number of philosophical works on the origin of the World whose 'Natural history' and a 'General Theory of the Sky' in 1755. Inventor of the theory of the birth of the Solar System from a primitive nebulae.

kao.general_1: Dark floor crater covering partly Helmert and located on  the South of Mare Smythii.
kao.slopes: Slightly steep slopes buried in the North steeper in the South and bearing a craterlet in the South-West.
kao.floor: Dark flat floor filled with lava mounds wrinkles and craterlets.

kapteyn.slopes: rugged and steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the North-East.
kapteyn.facts: Promoter of the 'Selected Areas' for the study of the Milky Way in 1906. Study on the proper movement of close stars.

karrer.facts: Works on sugars vitamins and colouring substances. Nobel laureate on 1937 with Haworth.

kasper.general_1: Almost circular formation in the middle of a catena including Carol and Melissa.

kastner.general_1: Circular formation forming a vast couple with K?stner G.
kastner.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing K?stner G and A to the North K?stner C and E to the South-West and Black to the South-West.
kastner.walls: Fairly high walls supporting K?stner B to the North-East.

kathleen.general_1: Elongated crater on the West end of Rima Vladimir and the Hurwitz Rainure 113 Totale.

kekule.facts: Directchemistry Institute on 1865. Discoverer of tetravalent carbon on 1857 and of the cyclic formula of benzen on 1865. Inventor of phenols  synthesis and of numerous others organic compounds.

kepinski.general_2: Younger than Moscoviense Basin older than Humboldtianum Basin

kepler.general_1: Isolated circular formation behind extensive clear rays.
kepler.slopes: Steep slopes especially to the South and bearing Kepler F to the West.
kepler.floor: Enough tormented floor. Weak central relief. Hills. Craterlets.
kepler.facts: Assistant of Tycho Brahé. Author of 'Astronomia nova' in 1611 presenting the first 2 laws of the movement of planets and 'Harmonia mundi' in 1619 presenting the third law. Author of the 'Rudolphine Tables' of planetary positions in 1627.

kies.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing the dome Kies Pi to the South-West a small wrinkle ridge to the East and white stains to the North.
kies.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the North and with a perpendicular extension to the South.
kies.floor: Flat floor filled with the lava of Mare Nubium.

kiess.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
kiess.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing K?stner R to the South-West K?stner S to the South and Widmanst?tten to the North-East.

laue.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

lauritsen.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

lippershey.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
lippershey.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a small wrinkle ridge to the North and to the South.
lippershey.facts: Declared inventor maybe excessively of the refractor in 1608.

mackin.general_1: Geological formation on the Luna 17 landing site.

maestlin.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

marco polo.general_1: South North lengthened and wrecked formation.

mavis.general_1: Small craterlet joined to Charles with a North-South catena.

mcadie.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
