mons hadley.facts: Astronomical instruments manufacturer. Inventor of the quadrant with reflection. Member of the Royal Society in 1717

mons hadley delta.general_1: Summit of Montes Apenninus situated South of the landing point of of the Apollo 15 mission.
mons hadley delta.facts: Astronomical instruments manufacturer. Inventor of the quadrant with reflection. Member of the Royal Society in 1717

mons hansteen.general_1: brilliant and isolated Mountain with triangular shape situated between Hansteen and Billy.
mons hansteen.facts: Discovers variations of the terrestrial magnetic field in 1821. Founder of an observatory in Oslo in 1833. Supervisor of works of triangulation of Norway.

mons heng.general_1: Elongated North-South mountain emerging from Oceanus Procellarum.
mons heng.facts: Named from the terrestrial mountain Mont Heng in the Hunan province in China.

mons herodotus.general_1: Isolated small mountain on the North of Herodotus.
mons herodotus.facts: Large traveler. Lived in Athens. Author of the 'Histories' in 9 volumes.

mons hua.general_1: Mountain emerging from Oceanus Procellarum. Numerous craterlets. Possible volcanic vent on the South.
mons hua.facts: Named from the terrestrial mountain Mont Hua in the Shaanxi province in China.

mons huygens.facts: Numerous works in mathematical and physical. Discoverer of the ring of Saturn and its satellite Titan in 1655. First hypothesis on the nature of stars and Sun. Member of the Royal Society in 1663.

mons la hire.general_1: Isolated mountain chain oriented West East. Craters on two summits.
mons la hire.facts: Promoter of the first meridian refractor of the Observatory of Paris. General description method of the conical. Author of a 'Memory on the epicycloids' in 1694. Member of the french Academy of Sciences in 1678.

mons latreille.general_1: Mountain emerging from Mare Crisium. Damaged crater on the South slope. Possible volvanic vent. Dark halo on the East.
mons latreille.facts: Named Prince of entomology. Author of the arthropods volume in le Règne Animal by Georges Cuvier. Separated amphibians versus reptiles. Founder of the Société entomologique de France with Bory de Saint-Vincent on 1832.

mons malapert.general_1: Mountain located between the Malapert and Haworth craters.
mons malapert.facts: Jesuit priest professor of mathematics in Poland and then in the North of France. In correspondence with Mersenius.

mons maraldi.general_1: Isolated and rounded mountain situated to the edge of Sinus Amoris and to the North-East of Maraldi.
mons maraldi.facts: Assistant of Jacques Cassini. Works on the astronomy of position and the celestial mechanics.

mons moro.general_1: Lengthened little raised and isolated hills oriented North South.

mons mouton.general_1: Mountain chain North of Malapert. Composed by the reunion of several craters slopes.
mons mouton.facts: Chef programmeuse au Goddard Space Flight Center. Calcul des trajectoires des premiers satellites US.

mons penck.general_1: Mountainous cape to the South-West of Sinus Asperitatis.
mons penck.slopes: Seems to form the edge of a high tray.
mons penck.walls: Bordered to the North by Kant C.
mons penck.facts: Professor in the University of Vienna then in Berlin. Director of the Institute of oceanography of Berlin. Author of the theory of 4 large glaciations in 1909. Works on several countries.

mons pico.general_1: Lengthened and South-East North-West oriented mountain. Isolated summit emerging from the lava of Mare Imbrium. Mountain Beta equally isolated to the South.

mons piton.general_1: Elongated isolated formation North-West to South-East.
mons piton.slopes: Mountain emerging from Mare Imbrium lava. Elongated and oriented North-South. Small summit crater. Craterlets Piton A and B in the South.

mons rumker.general_1: Complex of agglomerated lunar domes forming a circular tray. Enough steep slopes. Tormented surface.
mons rumker.facts: Director of school of navigation of Hamburg.

mons song.general_1: Southern part of the Apollo Impact Basin rampart
mons song.slopes: Has a 12 km crater in its middle.
mons song.facts: Named after Mount Song Shan in Henan Province of China.

mons tai.general_1: Situated at 46 km in the North-West of the landing site of the Chang'e 4 chinese probe.
mons tai.facts: Named from terrestrial mountain Mount Tai in the chinese Shandong province.

mons usov.general_1: Isolated mountain pretty raised on the East edge of Mare Crisium.

mons vinogradov.general_1: Isolated mountain with intersected narrow valleys.

mons vitruvius.general_1: Tormented mountainous region to the North of Vitruvius.
mons vitruvius.facts: Author of the alone treaty of architecture of Antiquity.

mons wolff.general_1: Southern summit of Montes Appeninus.  Situated across a curious chain of oriented South-West North-East slim hills emerging from Mare Imbrium.
mons wolff.facts: Tutor of Kant and popularizer of theories of Leibniz.  Author of 'First Philosophy' in 1729.

montanari.slopes: Slopes deleted to the South with a number of craterlets.
montanari.walls: Slightly high walls riddled of craterlets and ridden by Montanari D to the West and by Wilhelm A to the North-West.
montanari.floor: Flat floor but tormented to the South. Craterlets.
montanari.facts: Author of the first visual measures for a lunar cartography.

montes agricola.general_1: Remarkable oriented South-West North-East mountain chain. Very lengthened shape.
montes agricola.facts: Author of an encyclopedia on mining and geological data known as well as on techniques of extraction of ores and metallurgic processings.

montes alpes.general_1: Rough chain oriented South-East North-West. Numerous summits alongside Mare Imbrium. Culminate to Mount Blanc. Cut in two by Vallis Alpes.

montes apenninus.general_1: South wall of Mare Imbrium. Circular form oriented South-West North-East. Slopes to 30„ø on the average.

montes archimedes.general_1: Mountainous region with rectangular shape to the South of Archimedes.Numerous isolated mountains separated by deep valleys.
montes archimedes.walls: Contains Bancroft and some disseminated craterlets.
montes archimedes.floor: very large and parallel Grooves oriented South-East North-west to the North-west of the chain near Bancroft.
montes archimedes.facts: Pupil of Euclide. Calculation of Pi. Works in geometry. Inventor of the lever. Founder of the static and the hydrostatic.

montes carpatus.general_1: Oriented West East mountain chain situated to the North of Copernicus.
montes carpatus.slopes: Composed with several joined  mountains separated by deep valleys.
montes carpatus.walls: 15 km wide collapse in the East part.

montes caucasus.general_1: Continuation of Apennins. Mountains intersected with deep and numerous valleys. Wears the crater Calippus.

montes cordillera.general_1: Apparently rectilinear formation situated in the zone of librations.
montes cordillera.slopes: External mountainous ring of Mare Orientale.

montes haemus.general_1: South-East wall of Mare Serenitatis. Very somber region with two white stains around the craterlets Sulpicius Gallus L and M (diameter 4 km).

montes harbinger.general_1: North South oriented trio of 3 lengthened and isolated mountains South emerging from the lava of Mare Imbrium.

montes jura.general_1: Mountainous North wall of Sinus Iridum. Composed of several parallel and concentric summit lines.

montes pyrenaeus.general_1: Little marked and South North oriented mountain chain to the South of Gutenberg.
montes pyrenaeus.slopes: Separates Mare Fecunditatis and Mare Nectaris.

montes recti.general_1: Oriented West East remarkable rectilinear mountain chain.

montes riphaeus.general_1: Nrth South oriented mountain chain. Formed of isolated mountains and parallel linkages. North Part sometimes called Montes Ural or Mount Oural.
montes riphaeus.slopes: Flat region contained in mountains to the North in communication with Mare Cognitum.

montes rook.slopes: Internal mountainous ring of Mare Orientale.
montes rook.walls: Seem formed of two rings more or less distinct separated notably by Lacus Veris.

montes secchi.general_1: Oriented South-West North-East and little marked rectilinear mountain.
montes secchi.facts: Pioneer of the stellar spectroscopy. Author of the first classification of stars according to their spectrum in 1868. Solar prominences studies.

montes spitzbergen.general_1: Oriented North  Sud mountain chain. 4 high main summits of 1060 m / 1220 m / 1410 m / 1270 m.

montes taurus.general_1: Very tormented region suitable of ancient crater ruins to the North of R?mer.

montes teneriffe.general_1: Roughly and rectilinear chain oriented West East. Two blocks detached to the North and to the East. Six main summits emerging from the lava of Mare Imbrium.

montgolfier.facts: With his brother Joseph (1740 /1810) conceiver of an hot air balloon. First flight on june 4th 1783. Second flight with animals on september 19th in front of King Louis XVI. Director of Conservatoire des Arts & M‚tiers. Member of french Academy of scienceson 1796.

moretus.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Gruemberger to the North-West Cysatus to the North Short to the South Curtius to the North-East and Moretus A to the West.
moretus.floor: Flat floor filled with enough somber lava. Imposante central mountain of 2700 m. Line of crest. Hills and craterlets.

morley.facts: Collaborator of Michelson. Works on oxygen and the water.

morse.facts: Inventor of the electrical telegraph on 1832. First line between Washington and Baltimore on may 24th 1844. Inventor of the binary code of letters.

moseley.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
moseley.facts: Discovery of the relation between the atomic number of elements and their nucleus charge on 1913. Deceased in Gallipoli battle during first World War.

mosting.slopes: Steep slopes bearing M?sting D to the North-East and a small chain of mountains to the South-East and a second to the North-West.
mosting.walls: High walls with terraces splited by a crevice to the North.
mosting.floor: Flat and little extensive floor supporting a hill to the North and a small central mountain."

mouchez.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by a crater to the South.
mouchez.floor: Flat floor filled with lava and craterlets.
mouchez.facts: Hydrographic measures of coasts of Brazil and Algeria. Observer of the passage of Venus ahead the Sun in 1874. Director of the Observatory of Paris in 1878.

moulton.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

mount marylin.facts: Named by astronaut James Lovell during Apollo 8 mission to honour his wife.

muller.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a chain of craterlets oriented South-East North-West to the South-West.
muller.walls: High walls ridden to the South by the craterlets Muller A and O.

murchison.general_1: Deformed and wrecked formation. Forms an interesting couple with Pallas.
murchison.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Chladni to the South-East and Pallas to the North-West.
murchison.walls: Walls overlapped by Pallas to the North-West Murchison C to the South-West and gobbled in the lava of Sinus Medii to the South-East.
murchison.floor: Flat floor communicating with Pallas and supporting a debris to the North-west and Murchison T to the South-East. Hills crack
murchison.facts: Director of the Geological Service of the Kingdom United. Studies on the Silurian in 1839.

mutus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing many craters whose Mutus C to the North and Mutus Z LA & E to the South-East.
mutus.walls: Walls overlapped to the East by Mutus V & A.
mutus.floor: Flat floor with Mutus B to the West.

nagaoka.facts: Principal responsable of japanese physical surveys.

nam byeong-cheol.general_1: Large and decayed crater among the northwestern ejecta of the Orientale impact basin.
nam byeong-cheol.slopes: Very slightly steep slopes crushed by Houzeau to the South and by Fridman to the North-West. Higher slopes to the East than to the West.
nam byeong-cheol.walls: Slightly steep wall higher in the East than in the West. Wall marked by two anonymous craters in the West.
nam byeong-cheol.floor: Very rugged floor with mounds and an old dilapidated crater in its center.
nam byeong-cheol.facts: Joseon Dynasty astronomer. Constructor of an armillary sphere.

nansen.general_1: Circular formation. Situated in the zone of librations.
nansen.general_2: Older than Humboldtianum Basin. possibly pre-Nectarian
nansen.slopes: Steep slopes riddled with craters whose a large to the North.
nansen.walls: High walls with terraces supporting a crater to the South.
nansen.floor: Flat floor with debris to the North.
nansen.facts: Trip to Greenland in 1888. On the ship 'Fram' approached in 1895 to less of 4 degrees of the North pole.

nansen apollo.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

naonobu.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting trio with Bilharz and Atwood.
naonobu.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Atwood to the South and Langrenus BB to the South-East.
naonobu.walls: Slightly high walls supporting a craterlet to the West.
naonobu.floor: filled extensive flat Floor of lava with crater excentre' to the West.

nasireddin.general_1: Circular formation forming a remarkable trio with Huggins and Miller. The most recent of the three.
nasireddin.slopes: Steep slopes crushing Huggins to the West and Miller to the North-East.
nasireddin.walls: High walls with terraces in sweeter slope to the South-East.
nasireddin.floor: Slightly flat and wide floor. Central mountain and craterlets whose one to the North-west.
nasireddin.facts: Constructor of the observatory of Mar?rha in 1259. Translator of many works of Antiquity.

nasmyth.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting trio with Wargentin and Phocylides.
nasmyth.slopes: Slightly steep slopes overlapped by Wargentin to the North-West.
nasmyth.walls: Slightly high walls crushed by Phocylides to the South and supporting Nasmyth D to the North.
nasmyth.floor: Flat floor filled with lava with craterlets whose a large to the center.
nasmyth.facts: Inventor of the vapor hammer-pestle. Erected an observatory to Penshurst. Researches on the Moon. Inventor of telescopes with fixed focus.

natasha.general_2: Formerly Euler P. Unapproved name Vinogradov

naumann.facts: Author of symbols used for the classification of the different crystals shapes.

neander.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Neander E to the North and an anonymous deformed crater to the South-East.
neander.walls: High walls with terraces supporting Neander A to the North-West.
neander.floor: Slightly flat and wide floor. Central mountain. 2 craterlets principals.

nearch.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a group of craterlets to the North Nearch W to the East Nearch L to the West and Nearch A to the South.
nearch.walls: Fairly high walls damaged by Nearch A to the South.

nefed ev.general_1: Damaged crater on the North slope of Schrodinger.
nefed ev.slopes: Slightly visible slopes and very tormented.
nefed ev.floor: Unshaped and irregular floor bearing a curious elongated crater in the center.

neison.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava. Craterlets.

neper.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
neper.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Tacchini to the South and Jansky to the East.
neper.walls: High walls with terraces supporting several craters to the South-West.
neper.floor: somber and flat Floor. Central mountain. Craterlets.
neper.facts: Inventor of the calculation rule in 1617 and of logarithms in 1619.

nernst.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
nernst.facts: Director of Physics Institute of Berlin on 1925. Numerous works on electrolytes. Author of a theory of the electromagnetic force of batteries. Author of 3rd principle in thermodynamics. Nobel laureate on 1920.

neumayer.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South slope of Helmholtz.
neumayer.slopes: Slightly steep slopes overlapped by Helmholtz to the North and by a crater to the East and to the North-East.

newcomb.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Newcomb J & C to the South-East.
newcomb.walls: Walls overlapped by Newcomb A to the South.
newcomb.floor: little tormented Floor widened. Small relief excentre'.
newcomb.facts: Works on the movement of the Moon and planets. Determination of the main astronomical constants internationally  adopted in 1896.

newton.general_1: Damaged circular formation seeming to result from the fusion of two craters.
newton.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Newton C to the North.
newton.walls: Very high walls damaged by a crater to the North.
newton.floor: Flat floor supporting a craterlet to the East.
newton.facts: Construction of 1st telescope in 1671. Theory of colors in 1672. Theory of the universal gravitation in 1687. President of the Royal Society in 1703.

nicholson.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations on Montes Rook. Forms an interesting couple with Pettit.
nicholson.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a crater to the North-West.
nicholson.facts: Works on the Sun. Measured the temperature of planets with a thermocouple developed with Pettit. Also the discoverer of Jupiter's satellites IX X XI and XII.

nicolai.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a crater to the South a crater with horse-shoe shape to the South-East and two craterlets to the North.
nicolai.floor: Flat floor filled with lava with a craterlet to the North.
nicolai.facts: Specialist of the celestial mechanics and comets orbits.

nicollet.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated to the center of the South part of Mare Nubium on a wrinkle ridge.
nicollet.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a hill to the West.
nicollet.walls: High walls with small debris to the South.

niepce.general_2: Possibly pre-Nectarian IAU changed spelling from Ni‚pce
niepce.facts: Inventor on an explosion engine using petrol. Works on lithography. Works with Daguerre on 1829 producing plates photography.

nikolaev.facts: First flight of Voshkod spaceship with Popovich on 1964.

nikolya.general_1: Few visible formation near the Luna 17 landing site.

nobel.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
nobel.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta possibly pre-Nectarian or Lower Imbrian
nobel.facts: Production of nitroglycerin on 1863. Inventor of detonator on 1864. Conceiver of dynamit on 1875. Founder of french Sevran laboratory on 1881. Creator of five annual prices for great scientific and intellectual works.

nobile.general_1: Crater damaged by two important craters on its North and South creasts.
nobile.slopes: Slightly steep slopes riddeled with craterlets.
nobile.walls: Tormented walls bearing big craters in the North-West.
nobile.floor: Unshaped floor with a central mound numerous craterlets and an anonymous catena.

nobili.general_1: Circular formation. Forms an East West oriented remarkable trio with Jenkins and Schubert X.
nobili.slopes: Slightly steep slopes crushing Schubert X to the East.
nobili.facts: Inventor of the galvanometer with astatic system  in 1826 and a thermoelectric battery in 1830. Works on the infrared radiation in 1831 with Melloni.

noggerath.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Noggerath J to the West Noggerath H to the South-West and Noggerath G to the South.
noggerath.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by three craterlets to the South.

nonius.general_1: Damaged triangular formation situated on the South-East slope of Walter.
nonius.slopes: Very rugged slopes crushed by Nonius K & L to the North and bearing Nonius A to the South-East and Nonius B to the South-West.
nonius.floor: Tormented floor with numerous craterlets and hills.
nonius.facts: Inventor of nonius and innovatory of loxodromy in navigation.

norman.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
norman.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the South.

north complex.general_1: Geological formation named by the Apollo 15 astronauts.

north massif.general_1: Mountain named by the Apollo 17 astronauts.

north ray.general_1: Craterlet named by the Apollo 16 astronauts and located at the foot of Smoky Mountains..

nunn.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

oberth.facts: Thesis on rockets on 1923. Conceiver of V2 german rockets during World War II.

oceanus procellarum.general_1: Larger lunar sea. 2 102 000 km2. Very flat to the center. 80 m altitude difference in a 400 km diameter circle.

oenopides.slopes: Slightly steep slopes riddled with craterlets and crushed by Babbage to the North-East.
oenopides.floor: filled extensive flat Floor of lava. Hills and craterlets.
oenopides.facts: Has measured the inclination of Ecliptic as compared to the celestial equator. Determination of 12 signs of the Zodiac.

oersted.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the West.
oersted.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting the craterlet Oersted A. Craterlets and crevice.
oersted.facts: Discovers the electromagnetism in 1820. Director of Danish polytechnic School in 1829. Inventor of a piezometer. Studies on the compressibility of gases and liquids.

ohm.general_2: Should be shown on Plate 11B not 1B
ohm.facts: Author of a fundamental law about electrical currents on 1827. Discovery of polarization of batteries on 1830. Professor at Munich physics University on 1849. Works on polarized light rays on 1852.

oken.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing two craters to the North.
oken.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava.
oken.facts: Founder of school of philosophers of the nature. Author of a general natural History published from 1833 to 1841.

olbers.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Olbers A to the North-West Olbers K to the West and Olbers B to the East.
olbers.facts: Discoverer of Pallas in 1802 Vesta in 1807 and a comet in 1815.  Hypothesis of an ancient planet origin of asteroids. Author of a solution to the paradox of the blackness of the nocturnal sky.

old nameless.general_1: Very damaged crater named by the Apollo 14 astronauts.

omar khayyam.general_1: Complexe crater resulting of the fusion of two craters.
omar khayyam.slopes: slightly steep slopes in the North part but very steep with a sharp crest in the South. Craterlets all around.
omar khayyam.walls: Slighltly steep walls in the North but very steep in the South.
omar khayyam.floor: Floor in two parts. Rough North part with numerous craterlets and mounds. Flat South part with numerous craterlets.

onizuka.facts: Challenger shuttle crew member accidented in 1986.

opelt.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing the craterlet Opelt E to the South-West to the departure of a perpendicular extension of the wall.
opelt.walls: Slightly high walls subsisting to the North-West and supporting the craterlet Opelt H to the North-East.
opelt.floor: Flat floor with craterlets whose Opelt G to the South-East.
opelt.facts: Sustained works of the selenographers Lohrmann and Schmidt.

oppenheimer.facts: Numerous works on quantic theory of atom. Director of Los Alamos center on 1943. Director of first american atomic bomb building. Enrico Fermi prize on 1963.

oppolzer.slopes: Fairly steep slopes to the South and non-existent to the North.
oppolzer.walls: Slightly high walls almost totally gobbled to the North.
oppolzer.floor: Flat floor crossed by Rhyming Oppolzer and filled lava with white spots and craterlets.
oppolzer.facts: Works on the celestial mechanics. Author of 'Canon der Finsternisse' containing 13 200 Moon and Sun eclipses between 1207 av JC and 2161 published in 1887.

orontius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Saussure to the South Orontius C to the North Orontius D to the North-West Pictet E and Sasserides A to the West.
orontius.walls: Slightly high walls crushed by Huggins to the East.
orontius.floor: Tormented floor with debris to the East and with ghost crater Orontius F to the North. Craterlets whose a couple to the South. Hills. Lines of crest. White spots

osama.general_1: Crater-pit located at the South-East end of IMP INA..

osiris.general_1: Circular formation associated to Catena Brigitte situé between Dawes and Mons Argaeus.

osman.general_1: Squared fomation included in Catena Davy.
osman.slopes: Two shared sides with neighbour craterlets.

ostwald.facts: Author of a law about electrolytes dilution on 1888. Industrial preparation of nitric acid on 1907. Nobel laureate on 1909.

palisa.slopes: Fairly steep slopes non-existent to the South and bearing Palisa D A & W to the North-East.
palisa.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the South.
palisa.floor: Flat floor in communication with Davy Y and supporting the craterlets whose Palisa P to the South.

palitzsch.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated on the South-East slope of Petavius and marking the debut of Vallis Palitzsch.
palitzsch.slopes: Steep slopes crushed by Hase to the South-West by Palitzsch A to the North-West and bearing Vallis Palitzsch to the North.
palitzsch.walls: Slightly high walls collapsed to the North supporting a craterlet to the South and one to the North West.
palitzsch.floor: Flat floor tormented to the North.
palitzsch.facts: Amateur having observed the Comet of Halley in 1758.

pallas.general_1: Damaged circular formation. Forms an interesting couple with Murchison.
pallas.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta. possibly pre-Nectarian
pallas.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Bode to the North-West Pallas B & E to the South and crushed by Murchison to the East.
pallas.walls: Walls supporting the craterlet Pallas A to the North-West and Pallas H to the South.
pallas.floor: Flat floor filled with lava in communication to the North-East with that of Murchison. Central mountain. Hills wrinkle ridges and craterlets.
pallas.facts: Explorer of Russia and Siberia. Author of many natural science works on these countries.

palmetto.general_1: Very damaged crater named by the Apollo 16 astronauts.

palmieri.general_1: South North lengthened and damaged formation.
palmieri.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Palmieri E to the South-West.
palmieri.walls: Slightly high walls collapsed to the South.
palmieri.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Crossed by two rilles of Rimae Palmieri that cross themselves like a X.
palmieri.facts: Works on the telluric currents the terrestrial magnetism and atmospheric electricity. Director of the Observatory of the Vesuvio in 1850.

palus epidemiarum.general_1: Pretty flat region located on the South-East bank of Mare Humorum joining Mare Nubium to Mare Humorum.
palus epidemiarum.slopes: Comprises many internal mountains and rilles whose Rima Hesiodus and Rima Ramsden.

palus putredinis.general_1: Rectangular very flat area located between Archimedes and Montes Apenninus.

palus somni.general_1: Pretty flat continental band between Mare Crisium and Mare Tranquillitatis.

paneth.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

paracelsus.facts: One of the fathers of medecine. Also alchemist saying having  created the Homonculus and discovered an immortality elixir.

parrot.general_1: Damaged and deformed circular formation situated on the South slope of Albategnius.
parrot.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Parrot A to the South-West Vogel to the East and riddled of craters to the North.
parrot.walls: High walls to the East disapeared to the West and ridden to the North-West by several craters.
parrot.floor: Tormented floor supporting a complex structure to the West.

parry.general_1: Damaged circular formation forming a remarkable trio with Fra Mauro and Bonpland.
parry.general_2: Partly covered by Imbrian ejecta. possibly pre-Nectarian
parry.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a mountain to the North Fra Mauro to the North-West and Bonpland to the West.
parry.walls: Slightly high walls ridden to the South-West by craterlet Parry E.
parry.floor: Flat and extensive floor with double central craterlet Parry D.  Crossed by a rille of Rimae Parry to the South.
parry.facts: Specialist of polar regions. Explorer of the Strait of Lancaster.  Discoverer of the Island Melville and the Strait of Wellington.

parsons.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

pascal.general_1: Circular formation. Situated in the zone of librations.
pascal.slopes: Steep slopes supporting Poncelet C & D to the North.
pascal.walls: High walls supporting Pascal F to the North-West and Pascal A to the South.
pascal.facts: Author of the famous 'Thinks'. Experiences on the void. Works on probabilities and the geometry. Inventor of a calculating machine in 1642.

paschen.facts: Discoverer of infrared rays in the hydrogen spectra on 1909. Verification of relativistic rays of X rays.

pasteur.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
pasteur.facts: Works on cristallography on 1847. Discovery of microorganisms role in fermentation on 1857. Works on silk worm. Inventor of a feed conservation process on 1872. Discoverer of pathogen microbes.

patricia.general_1: Very elongated branch of Rimae Bradley.

patsaev.facts: Cosmonaut in Soyouz 11 mission . Deceased during return to Earth on the june 30th 1971 with Volkov and Dobrovolsky.

pauli.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
pauli.facts: Author of quantuum exclusion principle. Author of the hypothesis of neutrino existence on 1931. Nobel laureate on 1945.

pavlov.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
pavlov.facts: Works on nerves and blood circulation. Discoverer of conditionnal reflexes on 1903. Nobel laureate on 1904.

pawsey.walls: Steep walls bearing a big crater in the North-West.
pawsey.floor: Tormented floor with a big craterlet in the West.

peary.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-West wall of Humboldt.

playfair.general_2: Steep slopes supporting Playfair G to the West a craterlet to the South-West and the South North aligned trio Abenezra A Azophi A & B to the East.
playfair.slopes: High walls with debris to the South-West overlapped by Playfair B to the West and an anonymous craterlet to the South.
playfair.walls: Flat floor with craterlets whose a double central one.
playfair.floor: A ring-plain 28 miles in diameter with massive walls. It is situated on the N. of Apianus and is connected with it by a mountain arm. The rampart is tolerably continuous but varies considerably in altitude rising on the S. to a height of more than 8000 feet above the interior. On the E. extending towards Blanchinus is a magnificent unIAU Named formation bounded on the E. by a broad lofty rampart flanking Blanchinus Lacaille Delaunay and Faye. and on the W. by Playfair and the mountain arm just mentioned. It is fully 60 miles in length from N. to S. Sunrise on this region affords a fine spectacle to the observer with a large telescope. The best phase is when the morning terminator intersects Aliacensis as at this time the long jagged shadows of the wall of Playfair and of the mountain arm are very prominent on the smooth greyish-blue surface of this immense enclosure.
playfair.facts: Precursor of the geomorphology. Author of a law on the convergence of confluences.

plinius.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Rimae Plinius to the North.

promontorium archerusia.general_1: Mountainous cape situated to the South edge of Mare Serenitatis. Starting point of Rimae Plinius.

protagoras.facts: Creative orator excellent in the art of persuading. Author of a 'Treaty on the Being' and a 'Treaty on Gods'.

pytheas.facts: Expedition in Scandinavia. Discoverer of Feroe islands and of the Jylland. Discoverer of the influence of the Moon on tides. Determination of the latitude of Marseille. Test of determination of the celestial pole.

quetelet.general_1: Cover an older big crater with Quetelet T.

quetelet.walls: Flat floor with craterlets whom one big and invated by fallen rocks on the East
quetelet.facts: Founder of Bruxelles observatory. Statistics applied to social sciences sociales and probabilities to polotical sciences and anthropometrics. Numerous surveys. Member of Royal Academy of sciences.

rabbi levi.slopes: Slightly steep slopes riddled with craters whose Rabbi Levi B & P to the East and Rabbi Levi U to the South-West.
rabbi levi.walls: Fairly high walls higher to the East.
rabbi levi.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting  Rabbi Levi A & L to the North-West and Rabbi Levi D & M to the South-West. Depression hills and craterlets.
rabbi levi.facts: Author of a treaty of arithmetic and a treaty of trigonometry. Inventor of the Jacob's stick.

racah.slopes: Slightly steep slopes with sharp crest bearing numerous craterlets whose one big.
racah.walls: Steep walls tormented in the North-West and South-East.
racah.floor: Floor with a flat part and numerous landslides riddled with craterlets.

raimond.floor: Rough floor with a small central mountain and a big craterlet in the North.

raman.general_1: Very lengthened formation. Seems constituted by several aligned craterlets.
