ramsden.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated in the West part of Palus Epidemiarum. Created after the birth of Rimae Ramsden.
ramsden.slopes: Steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the South-East and overlapping Rimae Ramsden to the North-East and to the North-West.
ramsden.facts: Astronomical equipment inventor whose a type of ocular. Inventor of the theodolite and the dynamometer.

rankine.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated in the arena of Rankine B.
rankine.facts: Inventor of notions of energy and potential or cinetic energy.  Constructor of railroads. Numerous works in various areas.

raspletin.general_1: Eroded crater. On the bank of Gagarin impact basin.
raspletin.slopes: Slightly steep slopes with sharp crest and bearing Purkyne K in the South and one damaged crater in the North-West.
raspletin.walls: Steep walls collapsed in the East.
raspletin.floor: Floor with craterlets and landslides in the East.

ravi.general_1: Crater-pit on a branch of Rimae Alphonsus.

ravine.general_1: Small craterlet on the basement of Smoky Mountains named by Apollo 16 astronauts.

rayet.slopes: Slightly steep slopes with sharp crest bearing craterlets in the North-East.
rayet.floor: Flat floor with a low elongated crest.

rayleigh.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
rayleigh.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Urey to the South-West Liapunov to the South and Joliot to the South-East.
rayleigh.walls: Fairly high walls supporting many craterlets to the South.
rayleigh.floor: Flat floor to the North and tormented to the South supporting Rayleigh B & D to the center.
rayleigh.facts: Numerous works in optical and physic of gases. Discoverer of the argon in 1894. President of the Royal Company in 1905. Nobel Price in 1904.

reaumur.slopes: Non-existent slopes to the North and steep slopes to the South bearing Reaumur C and K to the South and Rima Reaumur to the East.
reaumur.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the North.
reaumur.floor: Flat and extensive floor crossed by Rima Oppolzer to the North. Hills and craterlets.
reaumur.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1708. Inventor of the alcohol thermometer in 1730. Works on ferrous alloys. Numerous studies on animals.

recht.facts: Director of the Chamberlin Observatory on 1928. Works in Yerkes observatory on 1939. Great astronomy popularizer.

regiomontanus.general_1: Lengthened and wrecked formation oriented West East.
regiomontanus.slopes: Steep slopes riddled with craterlets to the West and to the South and crushed by Purbach to the North.
regiomontanus.walls: High walls to the East and collapsed to the West ridden by Werner A to the East.
regiomontanus.floor: Flat floor with craterlets and hills. Central mountain supporting the summit craterlet Regiomontanus A.
regiomontanus.facts: Pupil of Purbach. Observer of the comet of 1472. Author of a treaty of trigonometry and 'The Epitome' a comment of the Almagest of Ptolemee.

regnault.general_1: Circular formation. Situated in the zone of librations.
regnault.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Regnault C to the North-West.
regnault.facts: Discoverer of the chloride of vinyl in 1835. Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1840. Has perfected the steam machine. Famous photographer.

reichenbach.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Reichenbach G to the South-East Reichenbach T to the North-West and Reichenbach A & B to the North.
reichenbach.walls: Very high walls with terraces ridden by Reichenbach F to the South.

reimarus.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a curious lengthened formation to the West and two anonymous craters to the South and South-East.
reimarus.walls: Fairly high walls supporting a craterlet to the North-west.
reimarus.floor: Flat floor supporting a crater westward.
reimarus.facts: Author of a planetary system resembling to that of Tycho Brahe.

reiner.general_1: Isolated circular formation to the South of the field of domes of Marius.
reiner.floor: Somber and flat floor. Central mountain.

reiner gamma.general_1: Formation composed with a deposit of very clear materials in form of kite. Seems to be linked with a completely gobbled ghost crater.

reinhold.slopes: Very steep and rugged slopes bearing the almost ghost crater Rheinhold B to the North-East.
reinhold.floor: Flat floor with small off-centered mountains and craterlets.
reinhold.facts: Partisan of Copernic. Author of new calculations destined for sustaining the model of the heliocentric system.

repsold.general_1: Wrecked formation. Situated in the zone of librations.
repsold.slopes: Slightly steep slopes highest to the East.
repsold.walls: Slightly high walls collapsed to the South.
repsold.floor: Flat floor supporting Rimae Repsold & Repsold G. Craterlets.

resnik.facts: Member of the crew of the Challenger Space Shuttle destroyed on 1986.

respighi.general_1: Circular formation situated alongside the zone of librations.
respighi.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Respighi B to the North-West and Respighi N large somber and lengthened crater to the South.

rhaeticus.slopes: Steep slopes bearing several craterlets whose a South-West North-East oriented chain to the North-East.
rhaeticus.walls: Slightly high walls but to the East.
rhaeticus.floor: Fairly flat floor. Small central mountain. Hills and craterlets.
rhaeticus.facts: Disciple of Copernic that spread its theories and managed to print his book 'De Revolutionibus orbium coelestium' in 1543. Author of a table of sinus to 15 decimals.

rheita.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting trio oriented South-West North-East with Fabricius and Metius.
rheita.slopes: Steep slopes fringed to the South-West by Vallis Rheita and crushing Rheita A to the East.
rheita.walls: High walls with terraces supporting a craterlet to the North.
rheita.facts: Manufacturer of the telescope of Kepler and author of a lunar map in 1645.

rhysling.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 15 landing site.

riccioli.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a large crater to the South-West Riccioli K to the West and Riccioli G to the North-East.
riccioli.walls: More high walls to the East that to the West.
riccioli.floor: Floor very tormented to the South and filled with lava to the North. Contains Rimae Riccioli. Hills craterlets and lines of crests.
riccioli.facts: First observer of a double star (Mizar). Author of the 'New Almagest' comprising a map of the Moon drawn by Grimaldi with a new lunar nomenclature.

riccius.general_1: Very damaged circular formation and riddled of ulterior craters.
riccius.slopes: Steep slopes replaced to the East by a chain of craters whose Riccius H A & B.
riccius.walls: High walls subsisting to the West and supporting Rabbi Levi M to the South.
riccius.floor: Tormented floor supporting two craters and several craterlets. Crest and hill lines."
riccius.facts: Jesuit missionary in China. Published maps of the World.

richards.facts: Works in electrochemistry thermochemistry and thermodynamics. Inventor of the adiabatic calorimeter on 1905. Discoverer of the atomic mass of one lead isotop. Nobel prize on 1914.

richardson.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
richardson.facts: Author of the laws on electron emissions by heated metals on 1901 basis of the electroniques tubes principle. Nobel prize on 1928.

riemann.general_1: Damaged circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
riemann.slopes: Slightly steep slopes riddled of craterlets and bearing Beals to the South and Riemann B to the North.
riemann.walls: Fairly high walls to the East and riddled of craterlets to the West.
riemann.floor: Tormented floor supporting many craters and craterlets.
riemann.facts: Theory of variable functions complex in 1851. Creator of the topology. Inventor of a non euclidian geometry.

rima agatharchides.walls: Crosses the large crater Agatharchides P.

rima agricola.general_1: Narrow and very sinuous rille parallel to Montes Agricola.

rima archytas.general_1: Very narrow rille oriented South-East North-West.
rima archytas.facts: Pythagorician friend of Platon. Inventor of the kite and flying machines.

rima ariadaeus.general_1: Large rectilinear East West oriented rile. Ramifies to the West with a branch going to Rima Hyginus.
rima ariadaeus.slopes: Splits to the East near Ariadaeus. Fulfillled by a mountainous cape to the North of Silberschlag. Floor filled by places.
rima ariadaeus.facts: Son of Philippe II. Author of a compilation of eclipses. Assassinated on the order of Olympias.

rima artsimovich.general_1: Shallow and narrow rille located on the East of Montes Harbinger.

rima billy.general_1: Very narrow rille oriented South-East North-West and situated on the South-East slopes of Billy.
rima billy.facts: Equally astrologer. Believed in a mysterious comet influence.

rima birt.general_1: Narrow rectilinear rille with bend in form of S in its middle.
rima birt.slopes: North South oriented and connecting the lengthened craterlet Birt E and the craterlet Birt F.
rima birt.walls: Broadsided to its North extremity by a second anonymous groove again more narrow and parallel.

rima bradley.general_1: Large South-West North-East oriented rille situated at the foot of Montes Apenninus.
rima bradley.facts: Discovered the aberration of the light in 1727 and the nutation in 1748. Director of the observatory of Greenwich. Royal astronomer in 1742.

rima brayley.general_1: Very narrow sinuous rille oriented South-West North-East.

rima calippus.general_1: South-West North-East oriented narrow rille situated at the foot of Montes Caucasus.
rima calippus.facts: Disciple of Eudoxe and director of his school.  Improvement of the cycle of Meton.

rima cardanus.general_1: Pretty long and large rille oriented South-West North-East.
rima cardanus.facts: Numerous philosophical works including the astrology. Resolution of equations of third degree. Creators of imaginary numbers. Inventor of a linking system wearing his name.

rima carmen.general_1: Few sinuous rille located on the East of Mons Argaeus.

rima cauchy.general_1: Large and rectilinear rille on the North-East slope of Cauchy and oriented South-East North-West.
rima cauchy.slopes: Comprises a very short passage in form of S in the middle.  Prolongs to the East until Lawrence by crossing a mountainous region.
rima cauchy.facts: Author of the theory of functions of a complex variable.  Works on the development in series of functions. Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1816 and the Bureau of Longitudes in 1839.

rima cleomedes.general_1: Situated in the arena of Cleomedes. Oriented South-East North-West. In form of Y. A branch ends to the North of the craterlet Cleomedes J.
rima cleomedes.facts: Author of a treaty of astronomy in two appointed works 'Theory of circular movements of celestial bodies'.

rima cleopatra.general_1: Sinuous rille located on the North of Montes Agricola.

rima conon.general_1: Sinuous rille oriented South-East North-West that passes Sinus Fidei.
rima conon.facts: Friend of Archimede. Inventor of the constellation 'Hair of Berenice'. Author of 7 books devoted to the astronomy.

rima dawes.general_1: Straight rille located on the North-East slope of Dawes

rima delisle.general_1: Very narrow and short sinuous rille oriented South-West North-East.
rima delisle.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1714. Inventor of the calculation of the distance of the Mercury and Venus Sun crossing.  Has put in place the observatory of St-Petersbourg.

rima diophantus.general_1: Sinuous and very narrow rille oriented West East.
rima diophantus.facts: Bit known. Collection of mathematics problems. Works on equations of the first and second degree.

rima draper.general_1: Narrow and very sinuous rille located on the basement of Montes Carpatus.
rima draper.facts: Precursor of the astrophotography and the spectroscopy. Author of the 'Henry Draper Catalogue' containing 240 000 stellar spectra.  Inventor of the basis of the stellar classification.

rima euler.general_1: Narrow and sinuous rille starting at Jehan.
rima euler.facts: Author of 900 works on many areas whose mathematics and astronomy.  Author of a 'Complete mechanics treaty' in 1736 and a work 'On the theory of the Moon'.

rima flammarion.general_1: Straight rille becoming double at its East endand located on the North slope of Flammarion.
rima flammarion.facts: Talented popularizator.  Author of  'The Popular Astronomy' in 1879. Creator of an observatory in Juvisy in 1883 and of the Société Astronomique de France in 1887.  Works in occult sciences  meteorology and climatology

rima furnerius.general_1: Almost straight rille on the floor of Furnerius.

rima g. bond.general_2: Large rille oriented North South. Crosses a lenghtened mountain in Lacus Somniurum and closes the crater Hall.
rima g. bond.facts: Son of W. Bond. Proposed the non solid nature of rings of Saturn and discovers the nature of the Orion nebula.

rima galilaei.general_1: Very narrow sinuous rille oriented North South. Wanders in the field of domes of Marius.
rima galilaei.facts: Founder of the modern mechanics. First usage of the telescope on stars. Discovers Sun spots the satellites of Jupiter and the lunar relief. Had to renounce to the rotation of the Earth around the Sun.

rima gartner.general_1: Situated in G?rtner. Oriented South-West North-East. Starts to the East of the craterlet G?rtner D. Ends by a lengthened craterlet.

rima gay-lussac.general_1: South-West North-East oriented straight rille situated on the North-West slope of Copernicus.
rima gay-lussac.slopes: Apparently formed of an alignment of craterlets.
rima gay-lussac.facts: Law on the dilation of gases in 1802. Preparation of the sodium of the potassium and many acids. Discovery of halogens.

rima hadley.general_1: South-West North-East oriented sinuous rille. Passes the craterlet Hadley C in its center. Visited by the Apollo 15 mission.
rima hadley.facts: Astronomical instrument manufacturer. Inventor of the quadrant to reflection. Member of the Royal Society in 1717

rima hansteen.general_1: North South oriented narrow rille and situated on the South-West slope of Hansteen.
rima hansteen.facts: Discovers variations of the terrestrial magnetic field in 1821. Founder of an observatory to Oslo in 1833. Supervisor of works of triangulation of Norway.

rima hesiodus.slopes: South-West North-East oriented. Marks a double bend in S near its West extremity.
rima hesiodus.walls: Crosses several formations whose of hills to the North of Cicchus.
rima hesiodus.floor: Wears several craterlets whose Cichus N in its middle.
rima hesiodus.facts: Poems on agricultural works. Author of an origin of the World and a genealogy of Gods in the 'Theogony'.

rima hyginus.general_1: Large rille South-East North-West oriented to the departure. Crosses the crater Hyginus.
rima hyginus.slopes: Then West East oriented. Slightly Deep. Seems formed of an alignment of craterlets. Connected by a small groove to Rima Ariadaeus.

rima jansen.general_1: Deep little narrow rectilinear rille. Oriented South-East North-West. Ends to the South close to Dorsa Barlow.
rima jansen.facts: Presumed manufacturer of the first magnifying telescope.

rima krieger.general_1: Small narrow and sinuous rille starting at Wollaston and ending on the East slope of Krieger while cutting it.

rima louville.general_1: Shallow and very sinuous rille oriented North-South. Joining Rima Sharp to its South end.
rima louville.facts: Author of a calculation method about eclipses come back. Member of Academy of Sciences. Dicoverer of the variation of the Earh axis rotation.

rima mairan.general_1: Very narrow sinuous rille oriented North South.

rima marcello.general_1: Small craterlets chain located between Dawes and Mons Argaeus.

rima marius.general_1: Sinuous rille  West - East oriented to the departure with a width passing from 2000 to 1000 m. Elbow near the crater Marius B. Then oriented North - South with a width varying from 1000 to 500 m.
rima marius.facts: Discoverer of 4 large satellites of Jupiter independently from Galileo and inventor of their names. First western observer of the galaxy of Andromeda

rima messier.general_1: Very narrow and little rille deep situated to the North-West of Messier.
rima messier.walls: Wears a craterlet to its South extremity.
rima messier.facts: Nicknamed 'The Ferret of comets' by King Louis XV.  Discoverer of 16 comets and editor in 1771 of a catalogue of 103 celestial objects (Nebulae clusters and galaxies).

rima milichius.general_1: Very narrow sinuous rille oriented North South and discovered by Lunar Orbiter probes. Passes a small chain of hills in its South part.

rima oppolzer.general_1: Large oriented West East rile. Interrupted in the middle by the East wall of Oppolzer.
rima oppolzer.slopes: Crosses the arena of Oppolzer and closes that of Réaumur.
rima oppolzer.facts: Works on the celestial mechanics. Author of 'Canon der Finsternisse' containing 13 200 Moon and Sun eclipses between 1207 av JC and 2161 published in 1887.

rima reaumur.general_1: South-East North-West oriented narrow rille situated on the East slope of Reaumur.
rima reaumur.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1708. Inventor of the alcohol thermometer in 1730. Works on ferrous alloys. Numerous studies on animals.

rima reiko.general_1: Small craterlets chain located between Dawes and Mons Argaeus.

rima rudolf.general_1: Slightly sinuous rille located on the basement of Mons Argaeus.

rima schroter.general_1: Short and narrow rille oriented South-West North-East joining S?mmering to Schr?ter.
rima schroter.facts: Selenographer. Specialist of rills and wrinkle ridges.

rima sharp.general_1: Long and very narrow sinuous rille oriented North South.

rima sheepshanks.general_1: Very narrow rille invisible from the Earth oriented West East.
rima sheepshanks.facts: Sister of the astronomer of the same name.

rima suess.general_1: Very narrow sinuous rille oriented North South. Discovery by Lunar Orbiter probes.
rima suess.facts: Professor in the university of Comes in 1857. First general geology of the Earth in the work 'Face of the Earth' in 1909. Discoverer of the cosmic origin of the moldavites.

rima t. mayer.general_1: Shallow and very sinuous rille oriented North-South.
rima t. mayer.slopes: Located between Milichius 16 et Milichius 19 (ALPO) volcanic domes.
rima t. mayer.facts: Selenographer. Author of lunar position tables in 1761.

rima wan-yu.general_1: S shaped rille on the West slope of Natacha.
rima wan-yu.slopes: Link between North and South areas around Natasha.

rima yangel.general_1: Shallow and wide straight rille located on the Sputh slope of Yangel.
rima yangel.facts: Specialist of the propulsion of rockets and the astronautics.

rima zahia.general_1: Almost straight and shallow rille starting from a craterlets group at its North.

rimae alphonsus.general_1: Short narrow North South oriented rilles situated in the arena of Alphonsus on the East side.
rimae alphonsus.slopes: Comprises small craterlets riding some rilles.
rimae alphonsus.facts: Initiator of the Greek and Arabic work translation. Coordinator of the calculation of Alphonsins tables replacing astronomical tables of Ptolemee in 1256.

rimae apollonius.general_1: Slightly curved rille located on the North-East bank of Mare Fecunditatis.
rimae apollonius.facts: Author of an important work of synthesis on the conical.

rimae archimedes.general_1: Little deep South-East North-West oriented rille to the South-East of Archimedes.
rimae archimedes.facts: Pupil of Euclide. Calculation of Pi. Works in geometry.  Inventor of  the lever. Founder of the static and the hydrostatic.

rimae aristarchus.general_1: Narrow rilles situated on the West slope of Prinz.
rimae aristarchus.slopes: Eight fine South-West North-East oriented parallel rilles.
rimae aristarchus.facts: Inventor of the heliocentric theory and a calculation method of distances of the Sun and the Moon.

rimae arzachel.walls: Situated on the edge East the arena of Arzachel.
rimae arzachel.facts: Personal Astronomer of the King of Toledo  Al-Ma'mun.  Inventor of several instruments of observation. Editor of the first astronomical tables called 'Table of Toledo'.

rimae atlas.general_1: System of rilles in form of Y situated in the arena of Atlas.
rimae atlas.facts: Giant father of Pleiads and Hyades condemned by Zeus to sustain the celestial vault on its shoulders to have been the ally of Titans.

rimae bode.general_1: Very sinuous and narrow rilles connecting Bode to Bode B. South rille more rectilinear and supporting the craterlet Bode G.
rimae bode.facts: Author of an 'Introduction to the Astronomy' in 1766.  Discoverer of an empirical law on planetary orbits in 1772. Director of the observatory of Berlin in 1786.

rimae boscovich.general_1: Very narrow rilles oriented South-West North-East situated in the arena of Boscovich.
rimae boscovich.facts: Author of many astronomy and mathematics works. Promoter of theories of Newton. Author of an atomic theory of the matter.

rimae burg.general_1: Large rilles situated in Lacus Mortis and perpendicular between them.
rimae burg.facts: Author of a theory of movements of the Moon.

rimae chacornac.general_1: Ramified rilles system crossing the wall of Chacornac and prolonging until Le Monnier.
rimae chacornac.facts: Discoverer of six asteroids. Study on solar spots. Theory of the lunar crater origin.

rimae daniell.general_1: Situated in Lacus Somniorum. Four large rilles whose two main ones oriented West East and parallel.
rimae daniell.facts: Inventor of an hygrometer and an electrical battery.

rimae darwin.general_1: Formation comprising several parallel and narrow rille oriented South-East North-West.
rimae darwin.slopes: Cross the East wall of Darwin.
rimae darwin.facts: Trip in South America with the 'Beagle' from 1831 to 1836. Author of 'About the origin of species by natural selection way' in 1859. Author of the theory of the transformist evolution of species called 'Darwinism'.

rimae de gasparis.general_1: Wide and very branched rilles system.
rimae de gasparis.slopes: Some rilles perpendicular looking like a wheel rays.

rimae focas.general_1: Branched rille located on a small marine area near Mare Orientale.

rimae fresnel.general_1: Ramified and pretty large rilless system oriented South-West North-East to the West of Promontorium Fresnel.
rimae fresnel.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1823. Specialist of the refraction and the diffraction. Inventor of lenses and mirrors wearing his name.

rimae gassendi.slopes: Situated in the arena of Gassendi.
rimae gassendi.facts: Pioneer of the observation with a telescope. First observer of a passage of Mercury ahead the Sun in 1631. Copernician in connection with Kepler and Galileo.

rimae gerard.general_1: Branched rille located on the South-West of Gerard.
rimae gerard.facts: Specialist of the Himalaya and the Tibet.

rimae goclenius.general_1: Large parallel rilles oriented South-East North-West.

rimae grimaldi.general_1: Ramified system of narrow rilles to the South-East of Grimaldi joining Damoiseau to Sirsalis.
rimae grimaldi.slopes: Comprises 2 overlapping craterlets in the center and to the South-East.
rimae grimaldi.facts: Jesuit. Discoverer of the luminous interferences and the diffraction of the light in 1650. Author of a map of the Moon used by Riccioli in 1651.

rimae gutenberg.general_1: Several large parallel rilles oriented South-East North-West.
rimae gutenberg.slopes: Start from Censorinus C until Mare Fecunditatis.
rimae gutenberg.walls: Crosses different relief types whose Censorinus C.
rimae gutenberg.facts: Inventor of ypographic letters in lead and of the press to print in 1440. Printed the first Bible in series. Ennobled in 1465 by the archbishop of Mayence.

rimae herigonius.general_1: Sinuous and very narrow rille oriented North South and starting from Dorsa Ewing.
rimae herigonius.facts: Author of a theory on the movement of planets.

rimae hevelius.general_1: System comprising four narrow and rectilinear main rilles situated in Hevelius. Some are perpendicular between them.
rimae hevelius.facts: Determination of the rotation of the Sun by observation of spots in 1645. Discoverer of the solar facules. Author of the first detailed map of the Moon in 1647 (6 preserved names).

rimae hippalus.general_1: Large and parallel rilles system situated on the East bank of Mare Humorum.
rimae hippalus.slopes: System of larges North South oriented and concentric rilles.
rimae hippalus.walls: One of them crosses the crater Hippalus.

rimae hypatia.general_1: Large oriented West East rille on the South bank of Mare Tranquilitatis.
rimae hypatia.slopes: Wears the craterlet Molkte AC in its middle.
rimae hypatia.walls: Ends by a pitchfork to the East that wears the craterlet Molkte B to its birth.
rimae hypatia.facts: Girl of Theon of Alexandrie. Co-author of works with her father. Author of a comment on the 'Arithmetics' of Diophante and on the 'Conical' of Apollonios.

rimae janssen.slopes: On the East side of the floor of the crater Janssen.
rimae janssen.facts: Specialist of the Sun. Discovers of the helium in 1868 as Lockyer. Founder of the Observatory of Meudon in 1876 and of an observatory on the White Mount in 1890.

rimae kopff.general_1: Straight rilles sometimes perpendicular located on the bank of Lacus Veris.

rimae littrow.general_1: Branched and sinuous rille on the bank of Mare Serenitatis.

rimae maclear.general_1: Two parallel North South oriented rilles joining Al-Bakri to Maclear. Prolonging in the South by Rimae Sosigenes.

rimae maestlin.general_1: System of several little marked parallel North West oriented rilles.

rimae maupertuis.general_1: very narrow and sinuous South-West North-East oriented rilles.
rimae maupertuis.facts: Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1723. Expedition in Lapland. Flattening of the Earth to poles. Director of the royal Academy of Prusse in 1746.

rimae menelaus.general_1: Narrow and parallel rilles system oriented West-East located on the South bank of Mare Serenitatis and whose est end is near Tacquet..
rimae menelaus.facts: Works on the geometry and the spherical surface trigonometry.

rimae mersenius.general_1: Long parallel and pretty narrow rilles.
rimae mersenius.slopes: North South oriented similarly to Rupes Liebig.
rimae mersenius.walls: Crosses the walls of Mersenius D to their South extremity.
rimae mersenius.facts: Friend of Descartes. Numerous works particularly in acoustic. Measure of the gravity with a pendulum in 1644.  Organizer of scientist meeting behind the Academy of Sciences.

rimae opelt.general_1: System of sinuous rilles oriented North South and situated to the frontier between Mare Cognitum and Mare Nubium.
rimae opelt.facts: Promoter that sustained works of the selenographes Lohrmann and Schmidt.

rimae palmieri.slopes: Prolong Rupes Liebig to the South.
rimae palmieri.walls: Crosses Palmieri by crossing in its center.
rimae palmieri.facts: Works on telluric currents the terrestrial magnetism and atmospheric electricity. Director of the Observatory of the Vesuvio in 1850.

rimae parry.general_1: System of North South oriented and ramified rilles.
rimae parry.slopes: Cross craters Fra Mauro Bonpland and Parry.
rimae parry.facts: Polar regions specialist. Explorer of the Strait of Lancaster. Discoverer of the Island Melville and the Strait of Wellington.

rimae petavius.general_1: Narrow rilles system situated in the arena of Petavius.
rimae petavius.slopes: Like rays starting from the central mountain of Petavius.
rimae petavius.walls: A rille again finer on the floor East Petavius.

rimae pettit.general_1: Straight rilles sometimes perpendicular located on the South bank of Mare Serenitatis.

rimae pitatus.general_1: Narrow and ramified rilles system situated in the arena of Pitatus.
rimae pitatus.slopes: Distributed whole around the floor of the crater.

rimae plato.general_1: West East oriented sinuous rilles situated to the East of Plato.
rimae plato.facts: Tutor of Denys the Youth. Founder of the Academy. Documented 28 'Dialogues' and many 'Letters'. Philosophy making the synthesis between the rationalism and the spiritualism. Believed in spherical stars

rimae plinius.general_1: System of three parallel rilles on the South edge of Mare Serenitatis situated between Promontorium Archerusia and Mons Argaeus.
rimae plinius.slopes: The largest is composed of aligned craterlets and is interrupted in its center by the North slope of Plinius.
rimae plinius.facts: Known for his encyclopedia in 37 appointed books 'Natural History'. Dead in an eruption of the Vesuvio.

rimae posidonius.general_1: System of ramified rilles situated in the arena of Posidonius whose some perpendicular.
rimae posidonius.facts: Founder of school of philosophy of Rhodes. Tutor of Ciceron and Pompee.

rimae prinz.general_1: System of large ramified rilles mainly oriented North South.
rimae prinz.facts: Author of a comparative study of the Earth and the Moon.

rimae ramsden.general_1: System of pretty marked ramified rilles.
rimae ramsden.slopes: Situated on the West bank of Palus Epidemiarum.
rimae ramsden.walls: Ridden by the craterlet Marth to the North and by the North-East walls of Ramsden to the North-East.
rimae ramsden.facts: Astronomical equipment inventor whose a type of ocular. Inventor of the theodolite and the dynamometer.

rimae repsold.general_1: System of rilles situated in the arena of Repsold and Galvani.

rimae riccioli.general_1: Very narrow and ramified rilles system situated in the arena of Riccioli to the South-East.
rimae riccioli.facts: First observer of a double star (Mizar). Author of the 'New Almageste' comprising a map of the Moon drawn by Grimaldi with a new lunar nomenclature.

rimae ritter.general_1: System of fourparallel rilles to the East of Dyonisus. Oriented South-East North-West prolonging Rima Ariadaeus and surrounding crater Ritter B C & D.
rimae ritter.facts: Author of a 'Compared universal geography' realized from 1817 to his death

rimae romer.general_1: Large North South oriented and fragmented rilles ending to the South on the West slope of R?mer.
rimae romer.facts: Determined the speed of the light thanks to eclipses of Jupiter satellites in 1676. Inventor of the meridian telescope.

rimae secchi.general_1: South-West North-East oriented rille ramified to its North extremity and situated on the North-West rim of Mare Fecunditatis.
rimae secchi.facts: Pioneer of the spectroscopie stellar. Author of the first classification of stars according to their specter in 1868. Solar prominences studies.

rimae sirsalis.general_1: North South oriented rilles system comprising mainly Rima Sirsalis.
rimae sirsalis.general_2: Rille continuing to the South with Rima Byrgius.

rimae sosigenes.general_1: Very sinuous rille few visible and oriented North-South. Join Rima Sharp at its South end.
rimae sosigenes.general_2: Two parallel North South oriented rilles joining Maclear to Sosigenes A.
rimae sosigenes.slopes: Continuing in the North with Rimae Maclear.
rimae sosigenes.walls: Prolonged to the North by Rimae Maclear.
rimae sosigenes.floor: Crossed in the middle by a perpendicular chain of craterlets.
rimae sosigenes.facts: Helped Jules Cesar to reform the calendar and announced the variation of the apparent diameter of the Moon and the Sun.

rimae sulpicius gallus.general_1: System of rilles situated on South-West rim of Mare Serenitatis.
rimae sulpicius gallus.slopes: South-East North-West oriented and parallel to Montes Haemus. In form of paw of goose with 3 fingers.

rimae taruntius.general_1: Concentric rilles located on the floor of Taruntius.
rimae taruntius.facts: Astronomer friend of Cicero. Author of a birth dat for Romulus. Author of a book on celestial objects in greek which has been used by Plinius.

rimae triesnecker.general_1: Very ramified rilles system spreading the North slope of Rhaeticus to Rima Hyginus and situated on the slope East slope of Triesnecker.
rimae triesnecker.slopes: The densest of the visible face of the Moon.
rimae triesnecker.walls: Comprises 5 North South oriented main rilles.

rimae vasco da gama.general_1: Straight rilles sometimes perpendicular located on the South bank of Vasco de Gama and on the floor of Vasco de Gama T.

rimae zupus.walls: Spread between Billy to the North and Zupus to the South.

ritchey.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Ritchey F to the North-West Ritchey C to the East and Ritchey A to the South-West.
ritchey.walls: Slightly high walls crushed to the North by Ritchey E.
ritchey.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Small central mountain.
ritchey.facts: Producer of mirrors of 1.52 m and 2.54 m for telescopes of the Observatory of the Mount Wilson. Important works in stellar photography.  Inventor of a telescope without abberations with H. Chretien in 1930.

rittenhouse.facts: Builder of astronomical instruments. Inventor of the first diffraction grating.

ritter.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a remarkable couple with Sabine.
ritter.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing to the North the aligned North South trio of craterlets Ritter D B & C and to the South-East Sabine.
ritter.floor: Tormented floor with low internal rings mounds and craterlets.
ritter.facts: Author of a 'Compared universal geography' realized from 1817 to his death.

ritz.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
ritz.facts: Resolutions of differential equations and partial derivations. Works on elements infrared spectral lines.

robert.general_1: Circular formation associated to Catena Brigitte situé between Dawes and Mons Argaeus.

robertson.general_2: Should be shown on Plate 1B not 11B
robertson.facts: Works on quantic mecanics and general relativity. Concept of Universe expansion.

rocca.general_1: Wrecked circular formation situated to the North-West of Lacus Aestatis.
rocca.general_2: Partly covered by Orientale ejecta possibly Lower Imbrian or pre-Nectarian
rocca.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Rocca R and P to the North and Rocca K to the North-East.
rocca.walls: Slightly high walls dismantled to the North and ridden to the South by Rocca L.
rocca.floor: Tormented floor darker in the North with mounds and craterlets. Central line of crests

romeo.general_1: Craterlet located on the East slope of Shahinaz on the floor of Ibn Farnas.

romer.slopes: Steep slopes bearing R?mer D to the South and a craterlet to the North.
romer.walls: Very high walls with terraces supporting a craterlet to the North.
romer.floor: Tormented floor. Central mountain lengthened to the North.  Craterlets.
romer.facts: Determined the speed of the light thanks to eclipses of Jupiter satellites in 1676. Inventor of the meridian telescope.

rontgen.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
rontgen.facts: Director of the Physic Institute of Munich on 1900. Discoverer of des X rays on 1895. Nobel prize on 1901.

rosa.general_1: Small craterelet located on the South-West of Jehan.

rosenberger.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-East slope of Vlacq.
rosenberger.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Vlacq to the North-West and Rosenberger D to the South.
rosenberger.walls: High walls with terraces supporting many craterlets.

ross.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a craterlet to the North.
ross.facts: Expedition in Antarctic on 1845. Discoverer of volcanoes Erebus and Terror.

rosse.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on the South part of Mare Nectaris.
rosse.facts: Producer of a telescope of 183 cm of diameter in 1845. Discovered the spiral structure of galaxies and studied the nebulae.

rosseland.facts: Bjerknes assistant. Cretor of journal Astrophysics Norvegica on 1934. Works at the Princeton University. Works on Harestua solar observatory on 1959.

rost.general_1: Circular formation forming an interesting couple with Rost A. Pretty raised Wall supporting a craterlet to the South-West.
rost.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Rost A to the West Rost M to the North-East and Rost D to the South-East.
rost.walls: Fairly high walls supporting a craterlet to the Southwest.
rost.floor: An oblong-shaped ring-plain 30 miles in diameter on the S.W. of Schiller with moderately high walls and according to Neison a shallow depression within nearly central. I have seen a crater shown by Schmidt on the E. side of the floor. A valley runs from the E. side of Rost to the S. of Schiller.
rost.facts: Amateur and popularizer of the Astronomy.

rothmann.slopes: Very steep slopes bearing doubles crater Rothman B to the South and a crater to the West.
rothmann.floor: Flat floor with an irregular shape. Off-centered mountain towards the North with two principal summits.

rowland.facts: Discoverer of the nature of static and dynamic electricities. Discoverer of the mechanic value of the calorie. Discoverer of 39 elements in the solar spectra.

rubin.general_1: Regular and isolated craterlet on the southern slope of the Hedervari crater.
rubin.facts: Measuring the rotation speed of stars in galaxies leading to the theory of dark matter. Numerous awards.

rumford.facts: Inventor of the water calorimeter of the air thermoscope and of a photometer. Numerous works on the caloric properties of water.

runge.general_1: Almost ghost crater located on the floor of Mare Smythii.
runge.slopes: Slightly steep slopes buried in lava and bearing a craterlet in the South.
runge.floor: Flat floor with a curious broken internal ring and an internal perpendicular rilles network.

rupes altai.general_1: Cliff more or less abrupt joining Catena Albufeda in the North to Piccolomini in the South.
rupes altai.walls: In form of arc of circle.
rupes altai.floor: Tray in altitude more tormented than the plain below in the North-East..

rupes boris.general_1: Slightly elevated crests line between Boris Gaston and Linda.

rupes cauchy.general_1: Rectilinear South-East North-West oriented fault. Adjacent craterlets whose Cauchy B F E and C from the North-West to the South-East.
rupes cauchy.facts: Author of the theory of functions of a complex variable.  Works on the development in series of functions. Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1816 and the Bureau of Longitudes in 1839.

rupes kelvin.slopes: Fringes the South-East bank of Mare Humorum.
rupes kelvin.facts: President of the Royal Company in 1890. Specialist of thermodynamic and electricity. Inventor of the galvanometer. Studies on tides of the terrestrial bark and the contraction of the Sun. Inventor of the calculation rule.

rupes liebig.general_1: Large curved and North South oriented fault passing the West bank of Mare Humorum.
rupes liebig.slopes: Ridden by Liebig F to the South.
rupes liebig.facts: Professor in the University of Munich. Teacher of von Hofmann and Kekule. Numerous works in organic chemistry. Inventor of a silvering method for astronomical mirrors and a method of manufacture of meat extract.

rupes mercator.general_1: Edge of a rectilinear mountain situated on the south rim of Mare Nubium.
rupes mercator.walls: Situated on the South-West bank of Mare Nubium.
rupes mercator.facts: Author of two maps of the World in 1538 and in 1569.  Inventor of a new mode of cartographic projection that wears his name in 1552.

rupes recta.general_1: Rectilinear fault situated on the East bank of Mare Nubium.
rupes recta.slopes: Connects Thebit D to the North with a small mountain to the South.

rupes toscanelli.general_1: Rectilinear fault overlapped in Rimae Aristarchus.

russell.slopes: Fairly steep slopes to the North.
russell.walls: High walls to the North supporting Briggs A to the East and Russel B to the West.
russell.floor: Flat floor filled with lava in communication with that of Struve.  Craterlets

rutherford.facts: Born in New-Zealand. Numerous works on radioactivity and transmutations. Discoverer of the particles nature on 1906. Determination of the neutron mass. President of the Royal Société Royale en 1925. Prix Nobel de chimie en 1908.

rutherfurd.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-East wall of Clavius.
rutherfurd.slopes: Very steep and rugged slopes to the North.
rutherfurd.floor: Tormented floor with an important off-centered mountain in the North-east hilles and crest lines.
rutherfurd.facts: Pioneer of the photography of the Moon and the Sun.

rydberg.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.
rydberg.facts: Determination of a fundamental constant for the theories about the atom structure.

ryder.general_1: Elongated and very bright crater located on the East wall of Pauli E.
ryder.slopes: Very steep slopes specially in the East with a sharp crest.
ryder.floor: Triangular shaped floor with landslides or impact melts in the East.

sabatier.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a flat region to the South-West.
sabatier.facts: Discoverer of the catalytic role of the nickel. Author of a method for synthetizing hydrocarbons. Member of the Academy of Sciences in 1913.  Nobel Price in 1912.

sabine.general_1: Circular formation. Forms a remarkable couple with Ritter.
sabine.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Sabine A to the South-West a craterlet to the South-East and a branch of Rimae Hypatia to the South.
sabine.floor: Tormented floor with mounds and craterlets.
sabine.facts: Works on the exact form of the Earth. Discoverer of the magnetic origin of solar spots in 1852.

sacrobosco.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing many craters whose Sacrobosco G & F to the North Sacrobosco L to the South-West and the double crater Sacrobosco H to the East.
sacrobosco.walls: Damaged and high walls ridden by Sacrobosco R to the North and presenting debris to the North-East.
sacrobosco.floor: Very wide tormented floor bearing 3 important craters Sacrobosco A & B in the ceter and Sacrobosco C in the North. Mounds craterlets and depessions..
sacrobosco.facts: Monk professor of mathematics in the University of Paris in 1220. Author o '

safarik.general_1: Eroded crater located on the rim of Freundlich-Sharonov impact basin.
safarik.slopes: Tormented slopes with sharp crest bearing a craterlet in the East.
safarik.walls: Steep Walls bearing a crater in the West

salam.general_1: Regular craterlet on the southern marine part of the Apollo impact basin.
salam.floor: Flat rugged floor with shallow craterlets
salam.facts: Work on electroweak interaction. Nobel Prize in Physics 1979 with Shelden Glasgow and Steven Weinberg.

samir.general_1: Young crater located in the North ejectas of Diophantus.
samir.walls: Slightly steep walls with a curiuous terrace.
samir.floor: Two levels floor with landslides deposits.

sampson.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

santbech.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the South-West bank of Mare Fecunditatis.
santbech.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Santbech E to the South Santbech J to the North and Santbech H to the North-West.
santbech.walls: Very high walls damaged by many craters whose Santbech D to the East.
santbech.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Small off-centered mountain.  Hills and craterlets.

santos-dumont.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated on the mountain of Promontorium Fresnel.
santos-dumont.facts: Constructor of dirigibles having achieved the Deutsch de la Meurthe Price in 1901. Constructor of airplanes. First flight confirmed in Europe 23 October 1906 with the Deutsch-Archdeachon Price.

sarabhai.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape and situated on Dorsum Azara.

sasserides.general_1: Very damaged formation difficult to distinguish.
sasserides.slopes: Very Slightly steep slopes bearing many craterlets whose trio Ball C G and Sasserides P to the North-West Sasserides H to the West Sasserides M to the East and Sasserides A to the South-East.
sasserides.walls: Very sweet walls disapeared to the East and supporting Sasseriddens F to the South.
sasserides.floor: Tormented floor with 2 couples of craters whose Sasserides S.  Numerous oriented North South cracks.

saunder.general_1: Wrecked circular formation situated on the North-East slope of Hipparchus.
saunder.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Saunder B to the North-East.
saunder.walls: Slightly high walls with gaps to the North-East.
saunder.floor: Flat and extensive floor communicating with an external lava extent to the North-East and supporting several craterlets whose a large to the North and a ghost crater to the South-East.
saunder.facts: Selenographer. Catalogue of positions of 3000 lunar formations.

saussure.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South slope of Orontius.
saussure.slopes: Steep slopes especially to the North and to the South and bearing a crater to the North-East.
saussure.walls: Fairly high walls damaged to the South.
saussure.floor: Flat floor with craterlets whose a central.
saussure.facts: Organizer of the first ascension of the White Mount with Jacques Balmat. Notions on geological layers. Inventor of the hygrometer. Has posed the first principles of the meteorology.

schaeberle.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

scheele.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
scheele.facts: Discoverer of many chemical substances whose hydrogen in 1768 oxygen in 1773 and the chlorine in 1774 as well as of several organic acids.

scheiner.general_1: Wrecked formation situated on the West slope of Clavius.
scheiner.slopes: Fairly steep slopes riddled of craters whose Scheiner C & D to the West and Scheiner G & E to the South.
scheiner.walls: Very high walls to the East
scheiner.floor: Flat floor supporting 4 main craters whose Scheiner J double to the North and Scheiner A to the center. Hills and  West East oriented crest line.
scheiner.facts: Constructor of first telescope with a straightened vision. First observations of solar spots with a filter. Author of 'Rosa Ursina' in 1630.

schiaparelli.floor: Flat floor. Small central mountain. Hills and craterlets.
schiaparelli.facts: Discoverer of the asteroid Hesperia in 1861. Comet relationship with meteorites in 1866. Observer of the 'Chanels' of Mars.

schickard.general_1: Immense isolated circular formation with dark color.
schickard.slopes: Fairly steep slopes riddled of craters bearing Lehmann to the North Schickard E to the South Wargentin A to the South-West and Drebbel to the North-East.
schickard.walls: Slightly high walls with summits reaching 2700 m.
schickard.floor: Immense somber flat floor filled with lava supporting Schickard B to the North-East and Schickard A to the South. Numerous craterlets to the South-West whose Schickard C. Hills and grooves. Black and white stains.
schickard.facts: Correspondent and friend of Kepler. Numerous works on the mechanics

schiller.general_1: Very lengthened and South-East North-West oriented formation. Seems to come from the fusion of 2 craters or from a low-angled meteorite impact.
schiller.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Bayer to the East and Schiller H to the North-East.
schiller.walls: High walls with terraces to the South.
schiller.floor: Very flat floor to the South-East and tormented to the North-West. Mountain to the North-West. Craterlets.
schiller.facts: Author of the 'Coelum Stellarum Christianus Atlas' showing Bible inspired constellations.

schlesinger.facts: Author of General Catalog of Stellar Parallaxes from 1924. One of the founders of the International Astronomical Union and president on 1932.

schluter.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
schluter.walls: High walls with terraces supporting a double crater to the South and a collapsed crater to the north.
schluter.floor: Flat floor partially darkened. Central mountain.

schmidt.facts: Selenographer. Has worked with von Hoffman

schomberger.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a crater to the North Schomberger C to the West Schomberger A to the South-West and Schomberger D to the North-East.

schonfeld.general_1: Circular formation in the libration zone.

schorr.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations and crushing two other craters.

schrodinger.facts: Author of fundamental equations of quantic physics on 1926. Nobel laureate on 1933.

schroter.slopes: Very steep slopes to the North and bearing Schr?ter K to the North-West and Schr?ter L to the South.
schroter.walls: Fairly high walls interrupted to the South and higher to the North supporting a craterlet to the South-West.
schroter.floor: Flat floor filled with lava communicating with Mare Insularum.  Hills and craterlets whose Schr?ter E to the center.
schroter.facts: Selenographer. Specialist of rilles and wrinkle ridges.

schubert.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-West slope of Banachiewicz. Forms an interesting couple with Back.
schubert.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Back to the South.

schumacher.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Carrington to the North-East overlapped by a crater to the West and crushed by Messala to the South.
schumacher.facts: Founder of the observatory of Altona and an astronomical review in 1822.

schuster.facts: Determination of cathodic rays nature on 1890. Numerous works on terrestriel magnetism solar physics and spectroscopy.

schwabe.walls: Fairly high walls partially dismantled to the West.

schwarzschild.general_2: Older than Humboldtianum Basin. ring arcs
schwarzschild.facts: Pioneer of stellar photometry with photography. First solution of general relativity equations on 1916. Inventor of black hole concept.

scobee.facts: Challenger shuttle crew member accidented in 1986.

scoresby.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Double central mountain. Hills and craterlets.
scoresby.facts: Explorer of the oriental coast of Greenland.

scott.general_1: Circular formation situated near the South Pole to the edge of the zone of librations.
scott.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a double crater to the North and to the North-East.
scott.walls: Fairly high walls supporting a craterlet to the South.
scott.facts: Author of two expeditions in Antarctic. Died little time after having reached the terrestrial South pole but after Amundsen in January 1912.

secchi.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
secchi.general_2: Wrecked formation of North South lengthened shape.
secchi.slopes: Steep slopes supporting Montes Secchi to the North-West.
secchi.facts: Pioneer of the stellar spectroscopy. Author of the first classification of stars according to their specter in 1868. Solar prominences studies.

seeliger.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

segner.general_1: Circular formation situated on the North-East slope of Zucchius.
segner.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Zucchius to the South-West and a crater to the North-East. Line of North South oriented crest connecting it to Schiller C.
segner.walls: Damaged and little high walls to the South-West.
segner.floor: Wavy floor supporting a chain of craterlets to the North-East and hills.
segner.facts: Author of a theory of the capillarite. Specialist of eclipses.

seidel.facts: Application of des probabilities to photometry works of Steinheil.

seleucus.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Central mountain.  Craterlets.

seneca.general_1: Irregular and wrecked formation forming an interesting couple with Plutarch.
seneca.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing many craters whose Plutarch to the South.
seneca.walls: Slightly high walls supporting several craters.
seneca.facts: Tutor of Neron. Author of the celestial comet origin.

seyfert.facts: Discoverer of a type of galaxy with active nucleus on 1943.

shakespeare.general_1: Small craterlet named by Apollo 17 astronauts.

shaler.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
shaler.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a crater to the West.
shaler.facts: First lunar geology test according to images.

shapley.general_1: Isolated and damaged circular formation situated on the South bank of Mare Crisium.
shapley.walls: Fairly high walls damaged to the North.
shapley.facts: Discoverer of the pulse nature of the cepheides and the distribution of the globular clusters in the halo of the Milky Way. Discoverer of two dwarf galaxies of the Local Group.

sharonov.general_2: Probably Eratosthenian possibly Upper Imbrian. should be shown on Plate 1B not 11B

sharp apollo.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 12 landing site.

sheepshanks.facts: Sister of the astronomer of the same name.

shen kuo.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
shen kuo.facts: Head of astronomy bureau during Song dynasty. Inventor of variuous machines. Author of atlases treatisi in music. Works on magnetic compass.

sherlock.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

sherrington.facts: Famous astronomical builder. Pioneer of astrophotography. Discoverer of 2 comets on 1880 and 1881.

shioli.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape. Young formation with bright ejectas.

shoemaker.general_1: Damaged crater between Haworth and Faustini.
shoemaker.slopes: Slightly steep slopes riddled with craterlets.
shoemaker.floor: Flat floor bearing Tooley and craterlets.
shoemaker.facts: Also geologist. Discoverer of one comet with her wife Carolyn

short.general_1: Circular formation located on the South slope of Moretus.
short.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Short B in the Soutrh-East Short C in the West and 3 craterlets in the South.
short.floor: Flat floor with a centered carterlet.

shorty.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

shternberg.general_1: Flat plain inserted between two mountains and opened to Oceanus Procellarum at the South-East

shuckburgh.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Shuckburgh C to the North and Schuckburgh A to the East.
shuckburgh.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Crevice.

shuleykin.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

siedentopf.facts: Inventor on 1902 with Zsigmondy of the ultramicroscope.

silberschlag.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on South slope of Rima Ariadaeus.

simpelius.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Simpelius D to the North-West Simpelius E to the North and others craters.
simpelius.floor: Flat floor tormented to the South-East with craterlet to the North.

sinas.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated on a small wrinkle ridge. Forms an interesting couple with Sinas E.

sinus aestuum.general_1: Very flat Region to the South-East of the crater Erathostenes supporting a South-West North-East oriented wrinkle ridge. 40 000 km2.

sinus amoris.general_1: Large very flat region to the West of Mare Crisium. Central mountain to the West of the crater Carmichael.
sinus amoris.slopes: Contains Mons Maraldi to the West.

sinus asperitatis.general_1: Very tormented region situated to the North of Theophilus. Comprises many parallel crests lines and chains of craterlets due to the impact of Theophilus.
sinus asperitatis.slopes: Wears a large ghost crater on its East bank surrounding Toricelli.

sinus concordiae.general_1: Flat region situated to the East of Mare Tranquillitatis.

sinus fidei.general_1: Gulf situated on the North bank of Mare Vaporum.
sinus fidei.slopes: Fairly flat region with some hills. Contains Rima Conon.

sinus honoris.general_1: Flat region situated to the North-East of Mare Tranquillitatis. Covered of South-East North-West oriented parallel crests lines.
sinus honoris.slopes: Broadside by Rimae Sosigenes and by Rimae Maclear.

sinus iridum.general_1: Very large crater shaped formation of 237 000 km2.
sinus iridum.slopes: Steep slopes constituted by North slopes of Montes Jura.
sinus iridum.walls: Walls constituted by Montes Jura gobbled to the South in the lava of Mare Imbrium.
sinus iridum.floor: Flat floor filled with lava and situated 600 m lower than Mare Imbrium.

sinus lunicus.general_1: Flat region between Aristillus and Archimedes where has crushed the Luna 2 probe on September 1959. Wears the craterlets Archimedes D & C.

sinus medii.general_1: Small sea situated to the center of the visible face. 52 000 km2. Broadsided to the South by Rima Oppolzer and to the East by Rimae Triesnecker.

sinus roris.general_1: Very flat Region uniting Mare Frigoris and Oceanus Procellarum.

sinus successus.general_1: Flat region situated on the North-East bank of Mare Fecunditatis.

sinus viscositatis.general_1: Marine formation open towards Oceanus Procellarum on the South-West.
sinus viscositatis.general_2: Continuing at North with a valley between Mons Gruithuisen Delta and Mons Gruithuisen Gamma.
sinus viscositatis.slopes: Extended to the North with a valley passing between Mons Gruithuisen Delta and Gamma.
sinus viscositatis.floor: Very flat floor filled with marine lava with craterlets with onr bigger in center.

sirsalis.general_1: Circular formation overlapping the crater Sirsalis A as large as Sirsalis to the South-West.
sirsalis.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing the North extremity of Rima Sirsalis to the East and Sirsalis F & J to the South.
sirsalis.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Central mountain.

sita.general_1: Small craterlet located on the Central mountain of King.

sklodowska.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
sklodowska.facts: Spuse of Pierre Curie. Production of metallic radium. Nobel laureate in physics on 1903 and in chemistry on 1911.

slater.general_1: Damaged crater on the South slope of Faustini.
slater.slopes: Slightly steep slopes riddled with craterlets.

slava.general_1: Small geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

slipher.facts: Pioneer of planetary photography. Author of more than 200 000 pictures of Mars.

slocum.general_1: Almost ghost crater located on the floor of Mare Smythii.
slocum.slopes: Slightly steep slopes buried in lava.
slocum.floor: Flat floor presenting a curious cressent shaped formation in the South and numerous carterlets.

smith.facts: Challenger shuttle crew member accidented in 1986.

smithson.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape surrounded by a white stain.
smithson.facts: Numerous mineralogical studies. Has given his name to the smithsonite.

smoluchowski.general_2: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
smoluchowski.walls: Steep swalls crushed by two big craters in the South.

strabo.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Thal‡s to the West.
