vendelinus.slopes: Slopes crushed by Lohse to the North-West by Lamé to the North-East by Holden to the South and bearing Vendelinus F to the South-East.
vendelinus.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by Vendelinus E to the South.
vendelinus.floor: Immense flat floor with numerous craterlets whose Vendelinus H to the North and the trio Vendelinus L Z & Y to the South. Hills and crevices.

vening meinesz.facts: President of the Geodesics international association on 1933. Author of geophysical theory of mountains origin.

vera.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape. Starting point of Rima Prinz I.

verne.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

very.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated on the median part of Dorsa Smirnov.

vesalius.facts: Author of several books on human anatomy. Doctor of Charles Quint on 1544.

vestine.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

victory.general_1: Geological formation on the Apollo 17 landing site.

vieta.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing the couple Vieta A & B to the South-West and Fourier to the South-East.
vieta.walls: Very high walls ridden to the South by a craterlet.
vieta.floor: Extensive tormented floor. Numerous craterlets. Hills and depressions.
vieta.facts: Numerous works in astronomy. Author of a table of trigonometrical functions in 1579. Inventor of the symbolization of the algebra in 1591. Method of approximation of equations roots.

virchow.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape situated in the zone of librations in the arena of Neper.
virchow.facts: Works in pathological anatomy. Creator of the cellular pathology. Political adversary of Bismarck.

virtanen.general_2: Should be shown on Plate 11B not 1B
virtanen.facts: Numerous works in agricultural or feeding chemistry. Nobel laureate on 1945.

vitello.slopes: Fairly steep slopes crushed by Lee M to the North-West with craterlet to the South-West.
vitello.floor: Tormented floor with internal ring and central mountain.

vitruvius.general_1: Circular formation situated to the South of Mons Vitruvius.
vitruvius.slopes: Slightly steep slopes but to the North.
vitruvius.walls: Slightly high walls partially gobbled to the South-West and ridden by a craterlet to the South.
vitruvius.floor: Tormented floor filled with lava. Central hills.
vitruvius.facts: Author of the alone treaty on architecture during Antiquity.

vitya.general_1: Geological formation on the Luna 17 landing site.

viviani.facts: Galileo's disciple. Works on bodies fall and conics. Member of the London Royal Society on 1696 and of Paris sciences Academy on 1699.

vlacq.slopes: Wrecked steep slopes to the South-West by Vlacq G and Hommel A B & Q and bearing Rosenberger to the South-East Vlacq C to the North-West and Vlacq A to the North.
vlacq.walls: High walls with terraces overlapped by many craterlets.
vlacq.floor: Flat floor. Central mountain with two summits. Craterlets.
vlacq.facts: Author of a table of logarithms in 1628.

vogel.general_1: Circular formation forming a North South oriented remarkable trio with Argelander and Airy.
vogel.slopes: Slightly steep slopes overlapped by a group of craters to the North whose Vogel A B and C and by a deformed craterto the South.
vogel.facts: Founder of the Observatory of Potsdam in 1882. First measures of the speed of rotation of the Sun by Doppler effect in 1871. Radial speed catalogue of 51 stars and stellar specters in 1883.

volkov.general_2: Partly covered by ejecta from Upper Imbrian crater Tsiolkovskiy

volta.general_1: Circular formation well defined Crushing North-West wall of Joule T crater.
volta.general_2: Situated in the zone of librations. Damaged formation.
volta.slopes: Slightly steep slopes supporting many craters whose Regnault and Stokes to the West.
volta.walls: Slightly high walls supporting Volta K & J to the South.
volta.facts: Inventor of the electroscope in 1782 and the first electrical battery in 1800.

volterra.general_2: Older than Humboldtianum basin possibly pre-Nectarian
volterra.facts: Author of the functionnals theory and of the solution of numerous integrals. Biometry application.

von baeyer.general_1: Craterlet composing a couple with Svedberg.

von behring.slopes: Steep slopes bearing a mountainous crest to the North.
von behring.facts: Director of the Hygienic Institute of Marburg in 1895. Discoverer of the tetanic antitoxin and the diphtery antitoxin. Nobel Price in 1901.

von braun.general_1: On the West bank of Oceanus Procellarum.
von braun.general_2: Formerly Lavoisier D. partly covered by Imbrian ejecta
von braun.slopes: Steep slopes crushed by Lavoisier E in the West.
von braun.floor: Wide flat floor with numerous straight rilles and bearing two craterlets in the South
von braun.facts: Director of NASA during Apollo missions

von karman.facts: Numerous works in aerodynamics hydrodynamics and thermodynamics. One of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory founder on 1944 of the International aeronautical sciences Council on 1956 and of the Astronautics international Academy on 1960.

von neumann.facts: Author of the electronical computers theory.

voskresenskiy.general_1: In the zone of librations. Circular formation.
voskresenskiy.facts: Specialist of rockets and the astronautics.

w bond.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Epigenes A to the North-West and Barrow F and E to the North.
w bond.walls: Slightly high walls specially to the East and ridden by Timaeus to the South-West.
w bond.floor: Immense flat floor containing the crater W. Bond B and two ancient gobbled craters. Hills craterlets crest and crevice lines.
w bond.facts: Director of the observatory of Harvard. Pioneer of the astronomical photography.

wallace.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the South-East in the lava of Mare Imbrium.
wallace.floor: Very flat floor filled with lava.
wallace.facts: Partisan of the theory of Darwin. Author of many works and studies on the natural selection whose 'Geographical animal Distribution' in 1876 and 'The Darwinism' in 1889.

wallach.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.
wallach.facts: Disciple of Kekule. Works on the structure of the composed organic. Nobel Price in 1910.

walter.general_1: Small pear shaped craterlet on the North-East slope of Diophantus.

walther.general_2: Not on Plate 6A (see entry in Table 2.1)
walther.slopes: Steep slopes bearing many craters whose Nonius to the South-East Walter C to the North-West and Walter D & Nonius L to the East.
walther.floor: Immense flat floor with Walter E to the West and a group of craters whose Walter A to the North-East. Craterlets and lines of crests.

wapowski.general_1: Crater located on the South slope of Scott.
wapowski.walls: Steep slopes bearing a craterlet in the South.
wapowski.floor: Slighty wide flat floor curiously off-centered..

wargentin.general_1: Heightened circular formation forming an interesting trio with Nasmyth and Phocylides.
wargentin.slopes: Fairly steep slopes overlapping Nasmyth to the South-East.
wargentin.walls: Non-existent walls because of raised floor.
wargentin.floor: Flat floor filled with lava very flat and heightened to height of the crest of slopes forming a plateau in altitude. Numerous lines of crests resembling to the wrinkle ridges. Hills.
wargentin.facts: Director of the Observatory of Stockholm.

wargo.general_1: Cirdular formation crushing the North-Ouest wall of Joule T Crater.
wargo.walls: Very high walls collapsed on the East.
wargo.floor: Flat floor presenting a straight mountains chain.
wargo.facts: Executive secretary of Lunar Exploration Analysis Group. Member of the Perseverance Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and LCROSS probes teams.

warner.general_1: Almost ghost crater located on the floor of Mare Smythii.
warner.slopes: Slightly steep slopes buried in lava.
warner.walls: Slightly high walls cut in the North.
warner.floor: Flat floor with a curious incomplete internal ring and a central mountain and a parallel rilles network.

waterman.general_2: Partly covered by ejecta from Upper Imbrian crater Tsiolkovskiy

watt.general_1: Circular formation forming a remarkable couple with Steinheil.
watt.slopes: Steep slopes overlapped by Steinheil to the North-West and bearing Watt A & R to the South-West and Watt C to the South-East.
watt.floor: Tormented floor with a craterlet to the South-West. Craterlets.
watt.facts: Works on the vaporization of the water. Improved the steam machine. Inventor of the regulator and the condensor.

watts.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the South-East slope of da Vinci.
watts.slopes: Slightly steep slopes flat to the South.
watts.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the South by the lava of a gulf of Mare Fecunditatis.

webb.general_1: Isolated circular formation situated on the East bank of Mare Fecunditatis.
webb.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a lengthened mountain to the North.
webb.facts: Religious. Amateur astronomer. Talented popularizer and specialist of the Deep Sky.

wegener.facts: Author of the continents drift theory on 1915. Dead in a Greenland expedition begun on 1929.

weierstrass.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Gilbert S to the South-West and Van Vleck to the South-East.
weierstrass.facts: Professor in the University of Berlin in 1864. Numerous works on functions and series.

weigel.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Weigel A to the South-East Weigel B to the South-West and a crater to the North-West.
weigel.facts: Author of 'Spherica Atlas' with constellations inspired from emblems of states.

weinek.slopes: Slightly steep slopes but to the North-East.
weinek.walls: Walls overlapped by a double craterlet to the North and others craterlets to the South.
weinek.floor: Flat floor filled with lava and with central craterlet.
weinek.facts: Author of an Atlas of the Moon. Appointed Director of the Observatory of Prague in 1883

weird.general_1: Small double craterlet named by Apollo 14 astronauts.

weiss.general_2: Flooded by Mare Nubium. may not be a crater
weiss.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Cichus to the South-West Cichus J & B to the South.
weiss.walls: Slightly high walls gobbled to the North.
weiss.floor: Flat floor filled with lava supporting Weiss E to the North. Grooves and hills. Craterlets.
weiss.facts: Founder and director of the Observatory of Comes.

werner.general_1: Young circular formation forming an interesting couple with Aliacensis.
werner.slopes: Very steep and rugged slopes bearing Blanchinus to the North Aliacensis to the South-East and Regiomontanus to the West.
werner.walls: Walls in very raised tiers supporting the craterlet Werner D to the North.
werner.floor: Flat floor but tormented alongside the South wall. Slightly off-centered mountain.

wessex cleft.general_1: Sculptured hills peculiar formation named by Apollo 17 astronauts.

west.general_1: Small double craterlet named by Apollo 11 astronauts.

wexler.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
wexler.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing a crater to the North and Wexler E to the East.

whewell.general_1: Circular formation with bowl shape. Forms a remarkable trio with Cayley and Morgan.
whewell.facts: Has given its name to a variety of natural calcium oxalate called whewellite.

whipple.general_1: Young crater on the South wall of Peary.
whipple.facts: Discoverer of the nature of comets

white.general_1: Complex crater located on the South-West slope of Apollo impact basin and near the impact basin Grissom-White cebter.
white.slopes: Very steep slopes bearing a crater in the West.
white.facts: Astronaut deceased in the Apollo 1 accident

wichmann.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape situated to the South of a chain of hills in form of stone lance.
wichmann.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing a North South oriented mountainous chain to the North.
wichmann.facts: Discovers the physical libration of the Moon.

widmannstatten.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations on the North-East slope of Kiess.
widmannstatten.facts: Researches in metallography. Has given his name to visible crystalline metallic structures on polite and attacked with nitric acid meteorites.

wiener.facts: Author  of a general definition of standardized spaces. Cybernetics founder on 1940.

wildt.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

wilhelm.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Montanari to the South Lagalla to the South-West Wilhelm C to the North Wilhelm D to the North-East and Wilhelm O & E to the East.
wilhelm.walls: High walls very sweet to the West supporting Wilhelm B to the South-West and Wilhelm K to the South.
wilhelm.floor: Fairly flat floor to the West and tormented to the East. Four aligned hills to the North-East. Craterlets. Hills and lines of crest.

wilkins.slopes: Slightly steep slopes supporting Wilkins A to the West Wilkins E to the North and Pons B to the North-East and a beautiful group of craterlets to the South-East.
wilkins.floor: Flat floor. Craterlets whose one to the East.
wilkins.facts: Author of maps of the Moon.

williams.slopes: Slightly high walls collapsed to the North.
williams.walls: Flat floor filled with lava. Line of crest. Hills and craterlets.
williams.floor: Flat floor filled with lava and with a crests line mounds and craterlets.

winthrop.general_1: Damaged circular formation overlapping the West wall of Letronne.
winthrop.slopes: Slightly high walls gobbled to the East and to the West.

wohler.facts: Discovers the aluminium and the bore in 1827. Succeeded in the first synthesis of an organic body (the urea) in 1828. Numerous works on organic bodies.

wolf.slopes: Slightly high and damaged walls crushed to the South by Wolf B.
wolf.walls: Flat floor filled with lava communicating to the South with Mare Nubium. Craterlets.
wolf.floor: Flat floor filled with lava and numerous craterlets and communicating with Mare Nubium.
wolf.facts: Inventor in 1891 of a photographic research method of asteroids that permited him to discover more than 40 of them.

wollaston.floor: A small bright crater on the Mare N. of the Harbinger Mountains surpassed in interest by a remarkable formation a few miles S. of it Wollaston B an object of about the same size but which is associated with a much larger enclosure resembling a walled-plain lying on the N. side of it. This formation has a lofty border on the W. surmounted by two small craters. The wall is lower on the E. and exhibits a gap. There is a central hill only visible under a low sun. About midway between Wollaston and this enclosure stands a small isolated triangular mountain. From a hill on the E. runs a rill valley to the more westerly of a pair of craters connected by a ridge on the S.E. of Wollaston B.
wollaston.facts: Specialist of the electrolysis. Discoverer of the polarization of electrodes of a battery. Isolated the palladium and the rhodium. Noticed dark rays in the solar spectrum in 1802.

wood.facts: Author of numerous works in spectroscopy photography and high frequencies. Inventor of interferential filters based on metals vapors deposits.

wreck.general_1: Shallow depression located North of Stubby craterlet and named by Apollo 16 astronauts.

wright.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.
wright.floor: Flat floor with a central mountain.

wroblewski.facts: Auteur de la premiŠre liqu‚faction de tous les gaz sauf l'h‚lium et l'hydrogŠne.

wrottesley.general_1: Circular formation situated on the North-West slope of Petavius.
wrottesley.slopes: High walls with terraces overlapped by a crater to the South-West.
wrottesley.floor: A formation about 25 miles in diameter closely associated with the E. wall of Petavius the shape of which it has clearly modified. Its border on the E. of the linear type rises nearly 9000 feet above a light interior where there is a small bright central mountain and some mounds. There is a prominent valley running along the inner slope of the W. wall.
wrottesley.facts: Has realized a catalogue of double stars and a catalogue of stellar positions measures.

wurzelbauer.slopes: Slightly high and sweet walls deleted to the South-West.
wurzelbauer.walls: Flat floor to the East raised to the center. Craterlets hills and lines of crest.
wurzelbauer.floor: Another irregular walled-plain about 50 miles in diameter on the S.E. of Pitatus with a very complex border in connection with which on the S.W. is a group of fine depressions and on the S.E. a large crater. There is much detail on the very uneven floor.

wyld.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

xenophanes.general_1: Isolated formation with a bowl shape.
xenophanes.general_2: Situated in the zone of librations. Damaged formation.
xenophanes.slopes: Fairly steep slopes supporting several craterlets to the North-East.
xenophanes.facts: Founder of school of Elee. Equally poet and satirical author. Partisan of an idealist pantheism.

xu guangqi.facts: Admited in the imperial court under Ming dynasty. Friend of the Jesuit Matteo Ricci. Converted to catholicism. Chinse translator of numerous books. Author of an agricultural treatise.

xu xiake.slopes: Slightly steep slopes interrupted to the West.
xu xiake.walls: Slightly steep wall with a recent craterlet with a white halo on the southern part and another craterlet on the eastern part.
xu xiake.floor: Flat extended floor riddled with craterlets.
xu xiake.facts: Writer of numerous travel stories. Discoverer of rare minerals.

yablochkov.general_1: Isolated formation with a bowl shape.

yakovkin.general_1: Circular formation situated to the edge of the zone of librations.
yakovkin.general_2: Formerly Pingr‚ H. partly covered by Imbrian ejecta
yakovkin.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing 3 craters to the South whose Pingré K.
yakovkin.facts: Specialist of the rotation and the shape of the Moon.

yangel.general_1: Isolated circular formation in a mountainous region
yangel.floor: Flat floor filled with somber lava.
yangel.facts: Specialist of the propulsion of rockets and the astronautics.

yerkes.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing to the North a line of North South oriented crest joining it to Yerkes E.
yerkes.floor: Flat floor filled with lava in communication with Mare Crisium to the East.
yerkes.facts: Financed the construction of an observatory in 1897 (Refractor telescope of 1m of diameter).

yoshi.general_1: Small craterlet located to the West end of Vallis Christel.
yoshi.slopes: Part of the complex formation associated to aratus CA.

young.general_1: Damaged circular formation and South starting point of Vallis Rheita.
young.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Young D to the South and a parallel crater alignment to Vallis Rheita to the East.
young.floor: Very tormented floor uprising to the North and supporting and Young A to the North.
young.facts: Discoverer of luminous interference fringes in 1801.

zach.slopes: Fairly steep slopes bearing Zach E to the North Zach D to the South-East Zach A to the South and the double crater Zach F to the North-West.
zach.walls: Very high walls with terraces to the East.
zach.floor: Flat floor with several small mountains to the North. Hills and craterlets whose a central couple.
zach.facts: Founder of a review of astronomy. Specialist of the gravity.

zagut.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Zagut A to the South-West a trio of craters to the North and a South-West North-East oriented chain of craterlet to the North-East.
zagut.walls: Fairly high and tormented walls crushed by Zagut E to the East.
zagut.floor: Flat floor supporting Zagut A to the center and a craterlet on the slope of Zagut E. Lines of crest.

zahringer.general_1: Isolated circular formation with bowl shape.

zasyadko.general_1: Circular formation situated in the zone of librations.

zeeman.facts: Discoverer of spectral rays modification by magnetic fields on 1896. Nobel laureta with Lorentz on 1902.

zeno.general_2: Younger than Humboldtianum Basin older than Crisium Basin
zeno.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing the trio Zeno D A & B to the South-West.
zeno.walls: Slightly high walls ridden by several craterlets.
zeno.facts: Author of many mathematics paradoxes. Invention of the philosophical dialogue. Explained eclipses.

zhang yuzhe.floor: Flat floor with a crater and craterlets.

zhang zhongjing.general_1: Regular craterlet on the southern marine part of the Apollo impact basin.
zhang zhongjing.facts: Editor of a treatise on the pathology of cold and various diseases.

zhinyu.facts: Constellation name on an old chinese celestial map.  Fairy name in the chinese legend the Cowboy and the Spinner.

zhukovskiy.slopes: Younger than Korolev Basin relatively old

zi wei.facts: One of the three enclosures near the celestial North Pole including the circumpolar constellations in old  chines maps.

zollner.general_1: Wrecked formation of North South lengthened form.
zollner.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Z?llner H to the North Z?llner D & DA to the West and Z?llner E to the South-West.
zollner.walls: High walls with terraces supporting a craterlet to the North to the South and to the South-West.
zollner.floor: Tormented floor. Central mountain and lines of crest.
zollner.facts: Inventor of a photometer. Author of 1st photometric catalogue  of stars in 1861 and of the first planetary albedo measures in 1865.

zsigmondy.facts: Important works in colloids chemistry and on glasses. Inventor of the first ultramicroscope on 1903 with Siedentopf.

zucchius.general_1: Circular formation situated on the South-West slope of Segner.
zucchius.slopes: Steep slopes bearing Segner to the North-East the couple Zucchius A & B to the West Zucchius C to the North-East and Bettinus B to theSouth.
zucchius.floor: Flat floor filled with lava. Central mountain with four summits. Large hill to the South-West.

zupus.general_1: Irregular formation resembling to a small sea.
zupus.slopes: Slightly steep slopes bearing Zupus S to the North-East and Zupus A to the West.
zupus.floor: Flat floor filled with very somber lava. Craterlets and crevices.

zwicky.facts: Discoverer of the difference between nova and supernova. Author of the neutrons stars theory on 1935 and of a photographical catalogue of galaxies. Discoverer of compact galaxies and of matter bridges between galaxies.
